author: julianshen
body:
## Summary
Upstream graphify shells out to yt-dlp for YouTube audio. gogfy's no-shell-out policy ruled that out — but a pure-Go alternative is viable via `github.com/kkdai/youtube/v2`, which handles the parts of yt-dlp's job that aren't trivial to reproduce (player-JS extraction and signature deciphering).

## What lands
- New `internal/ytaudio` package wrapping `kkdai/youtube/v2`.
- `pickAudioFormat` selects highest-bitrate audio-only stream; falls back to smallest combined (video+audio) when audio-only isn't offered (some live streams / shorts).
- `IngestFetcher` adapter satisfies a structural interface in `internal/ingest` without leaking `ytaudio.Result` across the package boundary.
- New `ingest.Options` struct (knob-bearing form alongside the historical `Ingest` signature).
- `gogfy ingest <yt-url> --audio` writes a `.m4a` / `.webm` binary sidecar alongside the existing oembed `.md` metadata path. Sidecar is content-hashed for idempotency (probes both extensions before re-fetching since the codec YouTube serves isn't known in advance).

## Best-effort design
A geo-block / age-gate / takedown falls back to the metadata-only path with a stderr log, so the URL still lands in the corpus. Failing the entire ingest just because audio fetch hit a 403 would be worse than landing the title+author from oembed.

## Dependency note
`kkdai/youtube/v2` is pure Go (transitively pulls `goja` for JS execution — needed to evaluate YouTube's signature decipher function). No cgo, no shell-out. The dep is widely used and actively maintained.

## Test plan
- [x] `internal/ytaudio` — 5 tests pin `pickAudioFormat` priority order (audio-only > combined; highest bitrate within each tier; nil for video-only; ErrNoAudioStream sentinel).
- [x] `internal/ingest` — `TestIngestYouTubeAudioModeWritesBinarySidecar` (stub fetcher), `TestIngestYouTubeAudioFallsBackToMetadataOnError` (fetcher errors → no audio sidecar; metadata fallback fires).
- [x] Full repo: 1111 passed across 47 packages.

author: josejmizrahi
body:
## Summary

V1-01 / FASE 0 correctness. iOS has no automatic RPC retry — the user's "retry" is re-tapping "Aportar" / "Registrar gasto" after seeing a network error. Each re-tap previously fired a fresh RPC → second `ledger_entries` row → fund_balance doubled. **Founder doctrine: "Un retry que duplique dinero destruye confianza sistémica."**

- **Mig 00351** — adds `p_client_id uuid default null` to both `fund_contribute` and `fund_record_expense`. Optimistic EXISTS-check pre-INSERT + race-safe `unique_violation` catch + partial unique index on `ledger_entries((metadata->>'client_id'))`. Backwards-compat (param defaults to null).
- **Mig 00352** — drops the legacy 5-arg overloads. Postgres treats different arg lists as separate functions, so mig 00351's `CREATE OR REPLACE` added the new 6-arg version *alongside* the old one. PostgREST would have routed inconsistently → intermittent idempotency. Dropping legacy ensures the V1-01 path is the only path.
- **iOS** — `FundRepository` protocol gains `clientId: UUID?`. `LiveFundRepository` forwards it as `p_client_id`. `MockFundRepository` mirrors server-side dedup so feature tests can verify retry-idempotency without a live backend. `ContributeToFundSheet` + `RecordExpenseFromFundSheet` hold `@State private var clientId: UUID = UUID()` — stable per sheet open, fresh on dismiss → re-open.
- **E2E test** `fund_idempotency.test.ts` — verifies same-key dedup, distinct-key separation, null-key legacy passthrough, and cross-type collision (doctrine: global namespace).

## Why the second migration was needed

After applying mig 00351, prod had TWO overloads:
```
fund_contribute(uuid, bigint, text, text, uuid)           -- legacy (5-arg)
fund_contribute(uuid, bigint, text, text, uuid, uuid)     -- V1-01 (6-arg, p_client_id)
```
PostgREST resolves overloads from the JSON body's keys. A client sending 5 keys would hit the legacy path with no idempotency; a client sending 6 keys would hit V1-01. Inconsistent idempotency defeats the whole point. Mig 00352 explicitly drops the 5-arg overloads. The 6-arg versions handle both call shapes because `p_client_id default null`.

## Design decisions

| Decision | Why |
|---|---|
| `p_client_id` in `metadata` jsonb, not a new column | No schema change; reuses existing `metadata` flexibility |
| Partial unique index on `(metadata->>'client_id')` global, not `(resource_id, client_id)` composite | UUIDs are globally unique by construction. Global index is strictly stricter — catches any iOS misuse that would reuse a UUID across funds |
| Dedup in entry-point RPC, not `record_ledger_entry` helper | Other ledger types (`fine_paid`, etc.) have their own dedup semantics; the helper stays a generic INSERT |
| EXISTS pre-INSERT **+** `unique_violation` catch | Optimistic short-circuit for the normal case; race-safe re-fetch when parallel callers slip between EXISTS and INSERT |
| iOS default `clientId: UUID? = nil` | Backwards-compat; explicit opt-in. Other callers must think about retry semantics rather than implicit-but-fresh UUIDs each call |
| `@State` UUID in the sheet, not coordinator | SwiftUI lifecycle: sheet open → State init → sheet close → State torn down → next open fresh UUID. Perfect retry boundary |
| Mock mirrors server dedup | Lets future feature-level tests verify retry-safety without a backend |

## Test plan

- [ ] SQL review: both RPCs have EXISTS-check + unique_violation handler + p_client_id in metadata jsonb on INSERT
- [ ] Verify `ledger_entries_client_id_unique` index exists and is partial WHERE `(metadata->>'client_id') IS NOT NULL`
- [ ] Confirm only 6-arg overloads remain (mig 00352 dropped the 5-arg legacy)
- [ ] Run `fund_idempotency.test.ts` in CI edge-tests workflow
- [ ] iOS build passes (Xcode 16+ swift 6 strict concurrency) — verified pre-PR via `BuildProject` MCP
- [ ] Smoke in simulator: open ContributeToFundSheet, submit, force network error mid-flight, re-tap → backend returns existing row (UI sees no duplicate balance)

## Verification done at apply time

```sql
select p.proname, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid) as args
from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
where n.nspname = 'public' and p.proname in ('fund_contribute','fund_record_expense');

→ fund_contribute     | p_fund_id uuid, p_amount_cents bigint, p_currency text, p_note text, p_source_event_id uuid, p_client_id uuid
→ fund_record_expense | p_fund_id uuid, p_amount_cents bigint, p_to_member_id uuid, p_currency text, p_note text, p_source_event_id uuid, p_client_id uuid

select indexname, indexdef from pg_indexes where indexname='ledger_entries_client_id_unique';
→ CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... USING btree (((metadata ->> 'client_id'::text))) WHERE ((metadata ->> 'client_id'::text) IS NOT NULL)
```

body:
I have hardened the RBAC path validation in `backend/security/rbac.py` by implementing segment-aware prefix matching, preventing unauthorized access to endpoints that share string prefixes with allowed ones. Additionally, I refactored `PromptGuard.validate_tool_call` in `backend/security/prompt_guard.py` to correctly integrate with the centralized `safe_resolve` utility, fixing a logic error in argument ordering and removing a vulnerable manual jail check. These changes ensure more robust protection against directory traversal and authorization bypasses.

author: millennialperfumer-tech
body:
### 💡 What:
Implemented thread-safe in-memory caching for the Shopify `LocationID` discovery in `backend/internal/client/shopify/client.go`.

### 🎯 Why:
The `DiscoverPrimaryLocationID` method was performing a GraphQL API call to fetch store locations and identify the primary one every time it was invoked (which happens frequently during order synchronization if a specific location ID isn't manually set in the application configurations).

### 📊 Impact:
- **Reduced Latency**: Saves ~300-500ms per order sync by skipping a network roundtrip to Shopify.
- **Resource Efficiency**: Reduces the number of GraphQL requests made to the Shopify Admin API, helping stay within rate limits.

### 🔬 Measurement:
- Verified via `go build ./internal/client/shopify/...` (Compilation).
- Verified via `go test -v ./internal/service/...` (Existing synchronization tests pass).
- Functional verification: Application logs will show the discovery process (e.g., "Matched target location by name") only once per application instance instead of repeatedly during every sync.

---

author: zajalist
body:
## Summary

This branch ships one cohesive session of work across the Hayba MCP toolkit:

### 1. The Sealed Vault — solvability-guaranteed PCGEx dungeon (the showcase)
- New PCG asset `PCG_SealedVault` (`PCGCreatePointsGrid → PCGEx Build Delaunay 2D`) authored and generated live in UE via the Hayba MCP.
- In-engine `python_run` lays out a provably-solvable 14-room / 4-key dungeon: Delaunay → MST spine → 3 loop edges → BFS reachability rank → invariant-safe lock/key placement → `assert_solvable` proof.
- Rendered as a top-down dungeon map: walled rooms (no overlaps — relaxation enforces `min_pair_dist > max_room_size`), corridors clipped to room edges, red doors at locked corridor mouths, color-coded green entrance / red boss / glowing yellow keys.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-sealed-vault-pcgex-dungeon-design.md`
- Driver: `tools/sealed_vault/ue_build.py` + invariant: `tools/sealed_vault/invariant.py` (unit-tested)
- Screenshot: `tools/sealed_vault/validation/sealed_vault_dungeon.png`

### 2. ToolExecutor seam — full architectural refactor (13-task plan, TDD)
- New `executeCommand(cmd, params, opts?)` API at `mcp-tools/hayba-mcp/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`.
- Owns connection lifecycle, 1× transport retry, timeout-from-cost (low=2s/med=10s/high=60s), uniform `UeToolError` with `code` discriminator (`transport | timeout | plan_gate | tool_disabled | ue_error`).
- 15 handlers migrated; 4 retain direct `client.send` with documented reasons (custom side-effects).
- Two adapters: live `tcp-client` sender + `InMemoryToolExecutor` for tests — handler tests no longer need a live UE on `:52342`.
- Companion `tool-meta-registry` populated at startup; 12 tools metaed today, others fall back to medium=10s.
- 18 executor tests + 3 registry tests, all green; full `src/*` suite: 59/59.
- Wire change in C++: optional `code` field on rejection responses (wire-compatible).
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-19-tool-executor.md` · Vocabulary: `mcp-tools/hayba-mcp/CONTEXT.md`

### 3. Five tool bugs found and fixed during the session
1. **\`searchCatalog\` multi-word queries returned \`[]\`** — whole-query substring match. Fixed with token-AND tokenisation; extracted pure \`searchNodes\`; 6/6 regression tests.
2. **Plan-panel step text clipped to one line** — missing \`.AutoWrapText(true)\` on the title \`STextBlock\`. Patched.
3. **Plan panel never advanced step status** — \`MarkStepCompleted\` was dead code. Added \`SetStepStatus\` + \`plan_mark_step\` TCP command + \`hayba_mark_plan_step\` MCP tool.
4. **Cognitive Map mislabelled clusters** — first rule that matched any class hijacked the label (1 light + 105 meshes → "lighting"). Rewrote as semantic-signal classifier (aggregate by label, ≥3 abs or ≥10% share to win, generics ignored).
5. **Scene Map didn't auto-refresh** — added level-actor delegates with 0.5s debounce in both panels.

All C++ changes documented in \`mcp-tools/hayba-mcp/CHANGELOG.md\`; the .cpp files live outside the repo in the geoforge plugin path. **Requires a plugin recompile** to take effect.

### 4. Bugs surfaced (documented, not fixed)
- \`hayba_planet_dynamo_field\` outputs ~5×10⁶ too large for Earth-equivalent inputs. Likely missing unit conversion.
- PCGEx catalog is missing input pins for cluster builders (e.g. \`UPCGExBuildDelaunayGraph2DSettings.In\`). Likely scraper gap.

## Test Plan
- [x] \`cd mcp-tools/hayba-mcp && npx tsc --noEmit\` → exit 0
- [x] \`cd mcp-tools/hayba-mcp && npx vitest run src/\` → 59/59
- [x] \`python -m pytest tools/sealed_vault/\` → invariant + fixtures green
- [x] In-engine \`assert_solvable\` on the generated dungeon → \`SEALED_VAULT_OK\`
- [ ] On reviewer side: recompile geoforge plugin; hit Refresh on the Scene Map — confirm the migrated cluster reads as \`staticmesh\` (not \`lighting\`), and step text wraps on the Plan panel
- [ ] On reviewer side: call \`mcp__hayba-toolkit__actor_list\` after MCP server restart — confirm \`{content:[{type:"text",text:...}]}\` MCP shape

author: othinas
body:
## Summary

Adiciona página `/dashboard` para o operador autenticado com KPIs financeiros, funil de status, ranking de estúdios/narradores/editores, gráfico de receita ao longo do período e badge de capítulos atrasados. Cada admin escolhe quais widgets exibir em `/settings` (auto-save) — preferência persiste por usuário via coluna `user_preference.dashboard_widgets` (jsonb).

Sete user stories (US1–US7) implementadas atrás de Suspense streaming, com cálculo financeiro determinístico (`integer` em cents, fuso fixo `America/Sao_Paulo`) e equivalência SQL ↔ JS validada por property-based test (1000 pares fast-check).

## Changes

### Domínio + DB (Phase 2 — foundational)
- Migration `0010_daffy_wind_dancer.sql`: `chapter.completed_at`, `chapter.paid_at` (timestamps timezone-aware com índices parciais + backfill), `user_preference.dashboard_widgets` (jsonb, default = 9 widgets).
- `ChapterService.update` escreve `completed_at`/`paid_at` na transição (idempotente via `IS NULL` guard).
- Helpers de domínio: `dashboard-widget` (catálogo de 9 widgets + Zod schema), `dashboard-period` (5 presets + parsing de search params em fuso SP), `dashboard-bucketing` (granularidade automática + labels PT-BR), `earnings-aggregations` (densificação + ticket médio).
- `PAID_LOCKED_FIELDS` estendido para incluir `completedAt`/`paidAt`.
- Catálogo de erros: `DASHBOARD_INVALID_PERIOD`, `DASHBOARD_WIDGETS_INVALID_KEY`.

### Backend
- `DashboardRepository` (port) + `DrizzleDashboardRepository` com queries SQL agregadas (\`SUM(ROUND(edited_seconds × price_per_hour_cents / 3600.0))\` em cents); `date_trunc` inlinado via \`sql.raw\` para evitar erro de \`GROUP BY\` com placeholders parametrizados.
- `DashboardService` com 3 use-cases (\`getFinancial\`, \`getOperational\`, \`getRetrospective\`) que pulam queries de widgets desabilitados (FR-032).
- 3 rotas REST: `GET /api/v1/dashboard/{financial,operational,retrospective}` — todas passam por `withApiErrorHandler`, retornam `{ data }` com `Cache-Control: no-store` + `X-Request-Id`.

### Frontend
- Página `/dashboard` em 3 linhas:
  - **Linha 1**: 3 KPIs (A receber agora, Receita do período, Ticket médio) via compound `FinancialKpiCard`.
  - **Linha 2**: Rankings BarChart (lg:col-span-2) + Funil de status PieChart (1 col).
  - **Linha 3**: Receita ao longo do período (AreaChart).
- Badge de **capítulos atrasados** no header (ao lado do `PeriodFilter`) só renderiza quando `count > 0`; click navega para `/books/<id>?focus=week`.
- Filtro de período client component com tabs de presets + Popover Calendar para range customizado; estado vive na URL via `router.replace(scroll: false)`.
- `DashboardWidgetsSection` em `/settings` com 9 checkboxes (auto-save 300ms debounce) — consistente com os outros selectors de tema/fonte/cor primária.
- Charts usam ramp `--chart-1..6` derivada de `--primary` via relative OKLCH (`oklch(from var(--primary) ...)`), respeitando a cor escolhida pelo usuário em ambos os temas.
- Lazy load do AreaChart via `next/dynamic` (~90kb gzipped fora do bundle inicial).

### Tooling
- Nova devDependency `@fast-check/vitest` para property-based tests.
- Nova UI: shadcn `Chart` (Recharts wrapper), `Tabs`, `Skeleton`.

### Seed enriquecido
- 5 estúdios, 8 narradores, 5 editores, 10 livros (clássicos da literatura BR), 104 capítulos com mix de status, `paid_at` espalhado em janelas (alimenta gráfico nas 3 granularidades), 3 livros com capítulos atrasados.
- RNG determinístico (LCG seed `0x428dada`); idempotente por padrão; flag `--force` trunca domain tables e re-popula.

### Testes
- 1197 unit tests (incluindo 1000 pares fast-check para equivalência SQL↔JS).
- 287 integration tests (incluindo `chapter-service-timestamps`, queries do `DrizzleDashboardRepository`).
- 5 E2E tests novos (dashboard-loads, period-filter, overdue-nav, retrospective-granularity × 2).

## Test Plan

- [x] \`bun run lint\` — clean
- [x] \`bun run test:unit\` — 1197 passed
- [x] \`bun run test:integration\` — 287 passed
- [x] \`bun run test:e2e\` — 227 passed (5 novos)
- [x] \`bun run build\` — production build compila sem erros

## Evidence

- Spec: \`specs/028-operator-dashboards/spec.md\` (7 user stories, 47 FRs, 10 SCs, clarifications)
- Plan: \`specs/028-operator-dashboards/plan.md\` (skills consultadas: /tdd, /api-design, /backend-patterns, /frontend-design, /frontend-patterns, /vercel-composition-patterns)
- Tasks: \`specs/028-operator-dashboards/tasks.md\` (123 tasks RED-first, agrupadas por US)
- Contracts: \`specs/028-operator-dashboards/contracts/*.openapi.yaml\` (financial, operational, retrospective)

body:
# Pull Request

## Issue Link
Closes #1016 — slice 3/N (stacked on top of #1104 / `codex/issue-1016-wfs-data-import`).

## Summary
Adds deterministic, render-only OGC migration *planning* for WMS and WMTS sources. Slice 1 inventoried these services; this slice produces classified planning entries that tag layer metadata as `automated`, SLD/SE style references as `assisted` (with diagnostics, no auto-import), tile-set definitions as `automated` for well-known XYZ/TMS-like grids and `manual-review` otherwise, and the render-only/tile-only data path as `unsupported`. Matches the AC requirement that render-only services emit explicit unsupported/manual-review records.

## Changes Made
- `src/Honua.Core/Features/Import/Services/OgcWmsMigrationPlanner.cs` — new deterministic planner for WMS sources.
- `src/Honua.Core/Features/Import/Services/OgcWmtsMigrationPlanner.cs` — new deterministic planner for WMTS sources (recognizes WebMercatorQuad and other well-known WKSS as trivial tile matrices).
- `src/Honua.Core/Features/Import/Domain/MigrationManifestArtifact.cs` — additive: new optional `PlanEntries` and `Diagnostics` fields on `MigrationManifestServicePlan`, plus new `MigrationManifestPlanEntry` and `MigrationManifestPlanDiagnostic` record types. No breaking changes.
- `src/Honua.Core/Features/Import/Domain/ImportCompatibilityCodes.cs` — added stable codes for the new classifications.
- `src/Honua.Core/Features/Import/Services/MigrationManifestTranslator.cs` — wires the WMS/WMTS planners into the existing service-plan translation pass.
- `src/Honua.Server/Features/Import/ImportJsonContext.cs` — registers the new types for AOT JSON serialization.
- `tests/dotnet/Honua.Core.Tests/Features/Import/MigrationArtifactSchemaSnapshots/honua.migration.manifest.schema.json` — updated pinned manifest schema snapshot for the new optional fields.
- `tests/dotnet/Honua.Core.Tests/Features/Import/OgcWmsWmtsMigrationPlannerTests.cs` — new tests covering deterministic planning from WMS and WMTS fixtures, render-only classification, SLD/SE style assisted diagnostic emission, trivial vs non-trivial tile-matrix classification, idempotent re-plan, and translator wire-up.

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated
- [ ] Architecture tests pass
- [ ] Manual testing performed

Local `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` were intentionally not run on the contended host; CI will validate.

## Gate Impact
- [x] PR gates (build, test, governance)
- [ ] Nightly gates (conformance, performance, security)
- [ ] Release gates (packaging, publishing)
- [ ] Deploy gates (promotion, post-apply validation)
- [ ] None — no gate impact

## Docs or Contract Impact
- [ ] OpenAPI spec changed
- [ ] Protobuf/gRPC contract changed
- [x] Control plane SDK surface changed
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] None — no docs or contract impact

`MigrationManifestArtifact` gained two optional fields on `MigrationManifestServicePlan` (`PlanEntries`, `Diagnostics`) and two new record types. The change is additive; existing manifest consumers see empty arrays unless the source is WMS/WMTS.

## Release/Deploy Impact
- [ ] Requires coordinated release across repos
- [ ] Requires database migration
- [ ] Requires infrastructure changes
- [ ] Requires environment variable or secret changes
- [x] None — standard merge-and-release flow

## Breaking Changes
None — purely additive.

## Summary

Full-stack ReviewRadar application — AI-powered review response and reputation manager for South African local businesses, with an immersive, animation-rich landing page.

### Landing Page (NEW)
- **GSAP ScrollTrigger** animations on all sections — parallax, reveals, perspective transforms, staggered word-by-word hero reveal
- **Lenis** smooth scrolling for buttery scroll experience
- **Three.js / React Three Fiber** floating 3D scene — distorted icosahedron spheres, wobble torus, 200-particle field
- **Giant hero typography** (`clamp(3rem,8vw,8rem)`) with gradient accent words and 3D perspective entrance
- **Scrollytelling "How It Works"** section with alternating layouts and abstract SVG/CSS visuals
- **Animated counter stats** section with scroll-triggered number counting
- **Parallax floating gradient shapes** on CTA section
- **Sticky navbar** with gradient scroll progress bar
- **Anti-AI design patterns**: film grain overlay, hand-drawn SVG circle accents, organic blob gradient shapes, imperfect typography spacing, custom scrollbar, noise textures
- Full dark theme (`#0a0a0f`) with cyan/purple accent gradients

### Core App
- **Dashboard** with 4 metric cards, rating trend chart, sentiment pie chart, recent reviews
- **Review management** with filters, search, inline AI response generation (Groq/Llama 3.1)
- **Escalation workflow** — Kanban board (Pending → In Progress → Resolved)
- **Reputation reports** — monthly reports with AI-generated recommendations
- **Settings** — business profile, brand voice, auto-respond, notifications, subscriptions
- **API routes** — AI response, escalation, reports, PayFast ITN webhook, auth callback
- **Supabase schema** — full migration with RLS policies
- **PayFast integration** — ZAR pricing (R499/R999/R2,499)

**Tech stack:** Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, GSAP, Lenis, Three.js/R3F, Supabase, Groq AI, PayFast, Recharts, Lucide React

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Visit the landing page and verify smooth scroll, GSAP animations, 3D floating objects, and all sections render (hero, features, how it works, stats, pricing, CTA, footer)
- [ ] Check the hero typography renders at large size with gradient words and staggered entrance animation
- [ ] Navigate to `/dashboard` and confirm metric cards, charts, and reviews render
- [ ] Test AI response generation on `/dashboard/reviews` (requires `GROQ_API_KEY`)
- [ ] Test escalation workflow on `/dashboard/escalations`
- [ ] Verify mobile responsiveness on all landing page sections

### Notes

- App runs in **demo mode** with SA-localised seed data — no database needed
- `.npmrc` added with `legacy-peer-deps=true` for Three.js/R3F peer dependency compatibility
- Recharts container-size warnings during static build are harmless and expected
- PayFast uses sandbox credentials by default

author: varmabudharaju
body:
## Summary

`teardown -c X` dropped the shadow collection and the cfg row but left X's pending jobs orphaned in `mongosemantic_jobs`. Next `apply` with a different field/mode left those orphan jobs ahead of the new ones in the FIFO queue; the worker silently embedded under the OLD field path and the new config never made progress.

Surfaced by tier 5 of the Atlas verification suite (chunked + inline both actually processed leftover tier-2 title-field jobs because of this).

## Fix

- In `teardown_cmd`: `delete_many({collection: X, status: in [pending, in_flight]})` on `mongosemantic_jobs` BEFORE `drop_data`. Ordering chosen to narrow a worker-in-flight race (commit message explains).
- Completed/failed jobs are intentionally preserved so operators can audit history.
- Only deletes jobs scoped to this collection.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit -q` → 201 passed (198 prior + 3 new):
  - `test_teardown_clears_pending_jobs_for_that_collection`
  - `test_teardown_does_not_touch_other_collections_jobs`
  - `test_teardown_with_no_pending_jobs_does_not_print_cleared_notice`
- [x] `ruff check .` → clean.
- [x] Independent code-review agent: "ship it" + three nice-to-haves; all three applied in commit 2 (reorder + race comment + N=0 test).

## Notes / Out of scope

- Teardown does not block workers from claiming jobs concurrently — that would require coordination machinery this lib doesn't have. Documented in the code comment; orphan in_flight jobs fail and retry/get reset.
- Partial-teardown safety (mid-step DB failure) is unchanged from existing behavior.

author: mhittle
body:
## Summary

Fixes **BUG-021**: the `/` feed was dominated by Philadelphia Inquirer articles across multiple algorithms.

**Root cause:** `feed.index()` ordered by `score DESC` (or `published_at` / `f.trending` per `?sort=`) and took the top 30 with **zero per-source diversification**. Dedup was per-`story_id` (cluster), not per-source. So a source with a recent fetch burst, or with elevated `source_reputation` combined with the multiplicative recency gate (BUG-011 fix) hitting many rows at once, could fill all 30 slots until ~24h decay broke it up. Jitter (BUG-012 fix) only shuffles within a score tier.

**Fix:** new pure `app/feed_diversify.py` (Flask-free / DB-free, mirrors `app/spectrum.py` / `app/firehose_cursor.py`):
- `cap_per_source(rows, cap=N, key="source_id")` keeps at most N rows per source, preserving input order
- `fetch_budget(page, page_size, cap)` sizes the SQL `LIMIT` so the page can still be filled after capping
- `page_slice` returns the requested window of the capped list

`feed.index()` now over-fetches `page * page_size * multiplier` rows from MySQL, caps in Python, then slices the requested page. Pagination is stable across pages because page N+1 sees the same capped sequence as page N.

New `FEED_MAX_PER_SOURCE` config (default **3**, env-tunable; `0` disables the cap entirely without a deploy).

## Scope choices

- **Python cap, not a SQL window function.** `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY source_id ...)` would be cleaner but requires MySQL 8 / MariaDB 10.2+. Staying in Python keeps the fix shared-host-agnostic and unit-testable without a live DB.
- **`/` only.** `/firehose` is intentionally un-deduped; `/search` is relevance-ordered with story-cluster dedup; `/saved` is the user's bookmarks; the digest already caps at `DIGEST_MAX_ARTICLES`. Each can adopt the same helper later.
- **Cap is applied AFTER the existing ORDER BY**, so survivors preserve the ranking that brought them in — the "first N by score" per source are kept regardless of which `?sort=` is active.

## Known limits

- Pathological case where the entire over-fetch window comes from one source: the page can come up short rather than refilling from outside the window. Not reachable at the real catalog size (~768 active sources).
- Documented in `INSTALL.txt` §10.

## Server-side state

None. No DB migration, no cron, no env required to ship. Standard Python App restart on deploy.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_feed_diversify.py` 14/14 pass via sandbox driver (no pytest in sandbox; documented limit). Covers: zero/negative cap = no-op, cap drops overflow preserving order, cap=1 keeps first-only, empty input, missing key, custom key, fetch budget math, pagination stability across pages, 50-row same-source burst regression.
- [x] `py_compile` clean on all changed `.py`
- [ ] Maintainer / CI in real env: reload `/` repeatedly under each algorithm — no single source should occupy more than 3 cards in the visible 30. Verify with `?sort=newest` and `?sort=trending` too. Page 2 (`?page=2`) should be a strict continuation of page 1 (no overlap, no gap).
- [ ] Post-merge: standard Python App restart in cPanel

## Closes

- Resolves BUG-021 (logged in PR #87).

author: copilot
body:
Implements the valid segment workflow: filter starred bike segments to those with power-measured efforts, find segments where two selected bikes both meet a minimum ride threshold, and surface a structured bike-to-bike comparison.

## New page: `app/pages/2_Valid_Segments.py`

**Data pipeline**
- Filters efforts to `average_watts.notna()` only
- Joins to segment metadata post-filter; computes `speed_kmh` via shared `_compute_speed_kmh()` helper
- Counts per-(segment, bike) ride totals; masks to segments where both selected bikes meet the minimum sample size

**Sidebar controls**
- `min_sample_size` — minimum power-measured rides per bike per segment
- `bikes_to_compare` — multiselect capped at exactly 2

**4 segment-type tables** (sprint / flat / ascent / descent)
- Columns: segment name, ride count per bike, distance, elevation gain, grade
- Row selection via `st.data_editor` checkbox column; selected IDs flow into comparison section

**Bike-to-bike comparison (`st.tabs`)**
- Per selected segment: summary stats table (time, avg/max power, speed, HR) + side-by-side power and speed box plots

**Spider/star plot**
- Axes = segment types; radial value = max speed (km/h) per bike
- Both bikes overlaid at 45% opacity using a single `_COLOR_SEQ` palette constant

## Key helpers

```python
def _compute_speed_kmh(df, distance_m=None):
    # uses fixed segment distance when provided; falls back to per-row 'distance' col
    safe_time = df["moving_time"].replace(0, pd.NA)
    if distance_m is not None and distance_m > 0:
        return (distance_m / safe_time * 3.6).where(safe_time.notna())
    dist = df.get("distance", pd.Series(dtype=float))
    return (dist / safe_time * 3.6).where(safe_time.notna() & dist.notna())

def _has_speed(df):
    return "speed_kmh" in df.columns and df["speed_kmh"].notna().any()
```

## Summary
Enhanced the Upload page to detect and handle users with existing paid sessions from previous payments, and improved the session validation logic to gracefully handle server errors.

## Key Changes

- **Paid session recovery banner:** When a user returns to the upload page with an active paid session (detected via `gaslamar_session` token in sessionStorage or localStorage), display an info banner directing them to the download page instead of showing reason-based error notices.

- **Session validation refinement:** Updated the `/check-session` validation logic to only dismiss the recovery banner on explicit terminal states (`deleted` or `pending`), while leaving the banner intact for HTTP errors (401 = no cookie, 5xx = server fault). This allows `download.html` to handle the session state gracefully rather than prematurely clearing it.

- **Improved error handling:** Wrapped session storage checks in a try-catch to prevent exceptions from breaking the flow, and clarified the validation logic with updated comments explaining the rationale for each response code path.

- Session detection checks for tokens starting with `sess_` prefix in both storage layers
- Recovery banner uses Indonesian text ("Kamu sudah upload CV sebelumnya") and links to `download.html`
- Reason-based notices (e.g., `?reason=no_session`) are suppressed when a paid session is detected

body:
### Motivation
- Provide utilities to convert raw per-subject CSVs into aligned PPG/GSR pairs and metadata to enable downstream training.  
- Add on-disk and in-memory dataset classes that produce fixed-length sliding windows for contrastive learning.  
- Introduce a ViT/Transformer-based two-tower CLIP-style model and a training loop to pretrain PPG/GSR encoders end-to-end.  

### Description
- Add `build_dataset.py` which robustly reads varied CSV timestamp formats, aligns GSR to PPG using nearest-neighbor merging with a `--tolerance_s` parameter, writes per-pair aligned CSVs under `out_dir/aligned`, and emits `metadata.csv` and `summary.json`.  
- Add `ppg_gsr_dataset.py` and `dataset.py`: `PPGGSRDataset` builds an in-memory aligned cache from raw CSVs and slices windows; `PPGGSRNpyDataset` loads aligned `.npy` files and constructs sliding-window indices; utility `build_dataloaders` creates train/val `DataLoader`s.  
- Add `config.py` holding structured `CFG` dataclasses for data/model/train settings, and `train.py` which wires `CFG` to CLI overrides, training/validation epochs, checkpoint saving, dataloader inspection, and logging.  
- Replace/refactor `model.py` with a `SignalTransformerEncoder` and `PPGGSRCLIP` two-tower model using patch embedding, sinusoidal positional encodings, `nn.TransformerEncoder`, an L2-normalized projection head, a learnable logit scale, and helpers `clip_contrastive_loss` and `retrieval_accuracy`.  

### Testing
- Ran module import and basic instantiation smoke checks by constructing `CFG`, instantiating `PPGGSRCLIP(cfg.model)`, and running a forward pass with random tensors, which completed without errors.  
- Exercised dataset code with simple synthetic arrays to verify `PPGGSRNpyDataset`/`PPGGSRDataset` indexing and `build_dataloaders` creation, and iterated a single batch through the training `run_epoch` path to validate loss computation and metrics.

author: mellanon
body:
## Summary

Refactors `@metafactory/content-filter` into a two-layer scanner. Tracks **cortex#370** (layered-scanner refactor) and fixes **cortex#367** (base64 false positives).

The `filterContentString` signature and the `FilterResult` shape are **unchanged** — cortex's `scanPrompt()` facade and the signal-collector / pilot consumers need no changes. The new `heuristic` field on `FilterResult` is optional and additive.

## L0 — entropy-aware base64 detection (fixes cortex#367)

The `EN-001` regex `[A-Za-z0-9+/]{21,}={0,2}` is structurally "any 21+ char run of the base64 alphabet". It false-positived on every GitHub URL, every commit SHA, and any long slash-path — which silently blocked review pings across cortex#358/#362/#363 and signal#51/#53 (RCA in cortex#367).

New `src/lib/entropy.ts` adds three gates a regex hit must pass to count as base64 (wired into `encoding-detector.ts`):

- **SHA gate** — hex-only tokens of git object-name length (7/8/40) are rejected.
- **Path / URL gate** — matches inside a `://` URL, or a slash-delimited path of lowercase path-words, are rejected.
- **Shannon-entropy floor** (~3.0 bits/char) — repeated-character junk is rejected.

Real random-bytes base64 (~4.5–6 bits/char, no path structure) still flags. Entropy lives in code, not YAML regex — the YAML rule is unchanged; the gate is a code-side post-filter on the regex hit, mirroring the existing `looksLikeIdentifier` precedent.

## L1 — heuristic prompt-injection scorer (new)

New `src/lib/heuristic-scorer.ts` is a **dependency-free port of [Rebuff](https://github.com/protectai/rebuff)'s heuristic-detection algorithm** (ProtectAI, MIT) — **not** the `rebuff` npm package. It normalizes the input, slides same-word-length windows over it, and computes the maximum Sørensen–Dice bigram similarity against a curated attack-phrase corpus (`config/attack-corpus.json`, seeded from Rebuff's open corpus + this repo's existing `PI-*` patterns). The Dice coefficient is inlined (~15 lines) so **no new dependency** is added. Offline, zero-config, pure CPU.

**Port, not depend** — the published `rebuff@0.1.0` pulls `@pinecone-database/pinecone`, `chromadb`, `langchain`, and `openai` even for heuristics-only use, and is not structured for a lightweight integration (cortex#370 scope-lock comment). Rebuff's vector-DB layer and LLM-judge layer are deliberately **not** ported — out of scope per cortex#370.

L1 is a **heuristic string-similarity scorer, not an ML classifier**, and the docs say exactly that.

## Combined decision

L0 then L1; a `BLOCKED` from **either** layer is `BLOCKED`. L1 score → verdict: `≥0.95` block, `≥0.82` review, else allow. **Only `block` rejects** — the `review` band routes to `HUMAN_REVIEW` *without blocking*, because bigram similarity cannot perfectly separate a paraphrased attack from benign text that reuses attack vocabulary. cortex already treats `HUMAN_REVIEW` as allowed, so a review-band hit never blocks a legitimate message — which is the whole point of cortex#370 (fewer false positives).

## Other

- `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` created — Rebuff (ProtectAI, MIT) algorithm-port attribution + a Presidio PII-pattern note (CLAUDE.md ecosystem rule for incorporated OSS).
- `package.json` `0.1.0` → `0.2.0` (minor — new L1 capability).
- `README.md` documents the two layers.
- Fixed a pre-existing invalid `FileFormat` (`"text"`) in `canary.test.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` green — **651 pass** (was 564). New: `entropy.test.ts`, `heuristic-scorer.test.ts`, `layered-scanner.test.ts`. Extended: `encoding-detector.test.ts` + `canary.test.ts`.
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean.
- [x] False-positive regression: GitHub PR/issue URLs, 40-char commit SHAs, long source paths → all ALLOW.
- [x] True-positive regression: real random-bytes base64, base64-encoded injection, verbatim/paraphrased injection phrasing → BLOCK or REVIEW as designed.
- [x] CLI smoke: `cf check` on a file containing a GitHub PR URL → `HUMAN_REVIEW` (was `BLOCKED`).
- [x] `filterContentString` signature + `FilterResult` shape unchanged — verified by `layered-scanner.test.ts` shape-stability tests.

Refs cortex#370, cortex#367.

author: rutabageldev
body:
## Summary

**Stage 2 of foundation's PLAN-0008.** Migrates ruby-core's dev environment off the mkcert-issued KV bundles at `secret/ruby-core/tls/*` onto Vault PKI direct issuance from `pki_int/issue/ruby-core-<svc>`. Stages 3 (staging) and 4 (prod) land in separate PRs after dev soaks.

**Architecturally distinct from foundation's mosquitto/freeradius migrations.** Those services don't speak Vault, so a Vault Agent sidecar bridges Vault → filesystem. Ruby-core's services *do* speak Vault — adding 21 sidecars (7 services × 3 envs) would have duplicated infrastructure ruby-core already had. This PR refactors `pkg/boot/boot.go` to call PKI directly with an in-process renewal goroutine. Foundation amended ADR-0008 with a direct-issuance exemption in their [PR #78](https://github.com/rutabageldev/foundation/pull/78); this PR adds the corresponding [ADR-0030](docs/adr/0030-direct-pki-issuance-no-sidecar.md) here.

## What's in this PR

### New: `pkg/boot/pki.go` + `pkg/boot/pki_test.go`

- `IssueConfig`, `MaterialHolder` — mutex-guarded TLS material with parsed-cert caching to avoid re-parsing PEM per handshake.
- `appRoleLogin` — reads role-id + secret-id from mounted files, logs in via `auth/approle/login`, returns authenticated client.
- `IssueNATSCert` — writes to `pki_int/issue/<role>`, parses cert/key/issuing_ca into the existing `*TLSMaterial` struct (so `ConnectNATS`'s downstream wiring is unchanged).
- `RenewLoop` — ticks at TTL/2 (clamped to [1m, 24h]), re-issues, atomic-swaps. Logs success/failure; never panics; exits cleanly on context cancel.
- `ConnectNATSDynamicTLS` — wires `tls.Config.GetClientCertificate` to a closure that reads through the holder. Verified via `nats.go@v1.48.0` source: it clones the `tls.Config` per handshake; Go's shallow `Clone` preserves function pointers; reconnect handshakes pick up rotated material without restart.
- `BootstrapNATSTLS` — single entry point used by all 5 services. Picks direct-PKI when `VAULT_PKI_ROLE` is set, falls back to legacy `FetchNATSTLS` otherwise (rollback retained through Phase 17.7).
- Tests cover `parseCertNotAfter` (with generated PEM), `renewIn` (edge cases: expired, 30s, 30d, 1y), `MaterialHolder.Replace` round-trip + bad-cert recovery, and concurrent read/write race (50 readers × 10 replaces). Pass with `-race` in ~11s.

### Modified: 5 service `main.go` files
Each replaces the `FetchNATSTLS` + `ConnectNATS` block with one `BootstrapNATSTLS` call. `ctx` moved to top of `main()` so `RenewLoop` cancels at shutdown.

### Modified: `scripts/fetch-nats-certs.sh`
Adds direct-PKI branch using AppRole login + single JSON-format issuance with `jq` (apk-add inline; vault:1.15 Alpine doesn't ship it). Legacy KV branch retained as rollback.

### Modified: `deploy/dev/compose.dev.yaml`
- Bind-mounts role-id + secret-id from `/opt/foundation/vault/...` into all 6 containers (nats-init + 5 services).
- Sets `VAULT_PKI_ROLE=ruby-core-<svc>` per service.
- `VAULT_TLS_PATH` + `VAULT_TOKEN` retained for the rollback path.
- Engine joins `postgres` network (parity with prod; fixes pre-existing dev drift where engine couldn't reach foundation-postgres for `ada` migrations).

### Fixed: `scripts/verify-tls-stack.sh` — real bug, not "brittleness"

Initial verify-tls-stack.sh runs showed engine failing with `"did NOT connect within 60s"` despite engine actually connecting cleanly. Root-cause investigation found a `set -o pipefail` + `echo "$logs" | grep -q "$pattern"` interaction on a 100MB+ engine log buffer:

1. `grep -q` exits 0 on first match
2. closes its stdin
3. SIGPIPE-kills the upstream `echo`
4. `pipefail` reports the pipeline as failed (rightmost-failed cmd was echo, killed by SIGPIPE)
5. the `!` flips it to true → MISS recorded
6. **every successful match silently turned into a miss** for any service with non-trivial log volume

Two-part fix:
- `start_services` adds `--force-recreate` so log buffers start fresh (matches the script's existing teardown-at-end semantics).
- Polling loop replaces `echo "$logs" | grep -q "$p"` with the here-string `grep -q "$p" <<< "$logs"`. No pipe → no SIGPIPE → no pipefail misreport. Also ~2× faster on 100MB input.
- `EXPECTED_LOGS` extended with the new `"pki: cert issued"` line alongside the legacy `"vault: fetched TLS material"` so both paths verify cleanly.
- Validated: **5/5 consecutive verify runs pass.**

### New: `docs/adr/0030-direct-pki-issuance-no-sidecar.md`
Records the direct-issuance exemption for ruby-core. Pairs with foundation's ADR-0008 amendment. Explicit about when the exemption applies (Vault-native consumers only) and what semantics are required (AppRole, TTL/2 renewal, fail-fast, scoped policy).

### Updated: `docs/ops/vault-dev.md`
The TLS Certificates section told operators to use mkcert for dev and sketched a forward-looking prod-PKI setup. Both are now stale; updated to describe the active direct-PKI flow + rollback path; old block kept as a historical note.

### Updated: `deploy/dev/.env.example`
TLS section refreshed to explain the new default vs. the legacy rollback path.

## Live verification (dev)

- All 5 services issue certs from `ruby-core-<svc>` PKI roles at startup
- NATS server cert issuer = `RubyNet Intermediate CA` (was: `mkcert <user>@<host>`)
- All mTLS connections established; renewal goroutines scheduled
- `bash scripts/verify-tls-stack.sh` passes 5/5 back-to-back runs (post-fix)
- `go build ./...` clean; `go test -tags fast -race ./pkg/boot/...` clean (11s)
- `pre-commit run` clean (gosec G304 on the operator-configured file reads suppressed with `#nosec` + justification)

## Foundation-side prerequisite (already merged)

[foundation PR #78](https://github.com/rutabageldev/foundation/pull/78) created the 6 AppRoles + 6 PKI roles + 6 scoped policies + role-id files on disk. Without it, the AppRole login in this PR fails.

## Drift observations (for tracking)

1. **Foundation needs a Make target to chmod 0644 the ruby-core secret-id files.** I `chmod 0644`'d them manually during the cutover, but the next `make rotate-approle-secret-id ROLE=foundation-agent-ruby-core-*` resets perms to `0600`, which breaks the bind-mount into distroless `nonroot` UID 65532. Tracking as a foundation-side follow-up.
2. **Pre-existing dev engine→postgres network gap** — fixed inline here (engine joins `postgres` network like prod). Was breaking `make dev-verify` independently of PKI.
3. **The `pipefail` + `echo "$big_var" | grep -q` bug pattern** could exist elsewhere — worth grepping any other scripts that combine those.

## Out of scope

- staging + prod migrations (Stages 3 + 4 of PLAN-0008) — separate PRs after dev soak
- Removal of legacy KV bundles, `VAULT_TOKEN`, `FetchNATSTLS` (Phase 17.7)
- Migration of `admin` + `navi-*` external clients (separate effort)

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go test -tags fast -race ./pkg/boot/...` (covers new types + functions)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass
- [x] `make dev-down && make dev-up` brings up full stack
- [x] All 5 services log `"pki: cert issued"` and `"connected to NATS"` at startup
- [x] NATS server cert verified via `openssl x509 -noout -issuer` = `RubyNet Intermediate CA`
- [x] AppRole negative-scope tested via foundation PR #78 (each token can only issue its own role; cannot read legacy KV)
- [x] `bash scripts/verify-tls-stack.sh` × 5 = 5/5 pass

author: hoangtrungnguyen
body:
## Summary

`se download <project>` now downloads only **public** Plane pages by default. Private pages (Plane's `access=1` flag) are skipped unless the operator explicitly passes `--include-private`.

## Behaviour change

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Downloads every page Plane returns | Filters out private pages by default |
| (no filter) | `--include-private` opts back into the old behaviour |

## Plane schema

Plane's page model has an `access` IntegerField with two choices:

```
0 = Public  (visible to every workspace member)
1 = Private (visible only to creator + explicitly shared members)
```

Source: github.com/makeplane/plane → `apps/api/plane/db/models/page.py`.

`is_public_page()` returns True when:
- `access == 0` (explicit public), OR
- `access` is missing/None (older Plane schemas didn't expose the field — default-safe so we don't accidentally hide content on older self-hosted instances)

## Output

```
$ se download STELL
Pages to process: 7 of 10 total (public only; skipped 3 private page(s) — pass --include-private to include them)
WRITE  'Architecture'  →  systems/sportbuddies/STELL/architecture.md
WRITE  'Roadmap'       →  systems/sportbuddies/STELL/roadmap.md
...
7 pages → systems/sportbuddies/STELL
```

When everything's public:

```
Pages to process: 10 of 10 total (public only)
...
```

With `--include-private`:

```
Pages to process: 10 of 10 total (public + private — --include-private)
...
```

## Files

- `download_project_pages.py`: new `is_public_page()` helper, pre-loop filter, summary line, `--include-private` flag
- `cli/se`: plumbs `--include-private` through `cmd_download`; help text mentions the public-only default

## Test plan

- [x] `se download -h` shows new flag + updated help string
- [x] Underlying script `python3 download_project_pages.py -h` shows `--include-private`
- [ ] Live verification: classifier blocks API calls in this session; operator should sanity-check against a project with mixed public/private pages

author: penta2himajin
body:
## Why

You asked me to verify the #179 thread change in my sandbox. I can't
run cpal (no audio device), but I **can** measure the metric that
actually causes underruns: the realtime factor (how fast the chain
processes audio vs wall clock; > 1.0 keeps up, < 1.0 underruns).

The result is the opposite of what #179 assumed. ORT's intra-op pool
busy-waits, so giving it 4 threads on a 4-core box starves the worker
/ cpal / OS threads and makes the chain **slower**:

| intra threads | Solo RTF | Overlap (TSE) RTF |
|--------------:|---------:|------------------:|
| 1 | 2.44× | 1.54× |
| **2** | **2.75×** | **1.64×** |
| 3 | 2.02× | 1.35× |
| 4 (#179) | 1.62× | 1.06× |

2 is the clear optimum; 4 nearly halves Overlap throughput. The
original clamp of 2 was correct — #179's bump to 4 was a regression
on any machine where ORT threads contend with the realtime worker
(i.e. typical 2-4 core consumer laptops, exactly the user's case).

## What

* `ort_threads::intra_op_threads()` clamp restored to **2** (revert
  of #179's bump to 4). The doc comment now carries the benchmark
  table so this doesn't get "optimised" upward again.
* `RING_CHUNKS = 6` from #179 **stays** — it's an independent
  jitter-buffer tweak the benchmark doesn't touch and doesn't
  regress.
* Adds `tests/realtime_factor_bench.rs`, the harness that produced
  the table. Not a pass/fail test (no assertions) — it prints the
  Solo and Overlap realtime factors so future perf work can
  re-measure. Gated on the full ONNX env set + the solo/mix test
  WAVs; skips otherwise.

## The honest read on the user's underruns

Even at the optimal intra=2, my 4-vCPU sandbox gets 1.64× realtime
for the Overlap (TSE) chain **in isolation** — without the ECAPA
refresh stalls, cpal callback contention, GUI rendering, and OS
scheduling the real app adds. The user's laptop underruns because
its effective headroom, after all that overhead, dips below 1.0×.
Thread count can't fix that (more threads make it worse). The real
levers are:

* **int8-quantised TSE export** — roughly halves the Conv-TasNet
  inference cost, directly attacking the Overlap-mode shortfall.
* **async ECAPA/TSE worker** — move the heavy inferences off the
  realtime thread so periodic refreshes don't stall the chain
  (today `async_refresh` rejects TSE: `TseAsyncUnsupported`).
* **coarser ECAPA refresh** — `sv_update_samples` 500 ms → ~1 s.

I'd suggest the int8 TSE export as the highest-impact next step if
the underruns are audible. Want me to look into that?

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p mellonella-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p mellonella-core --lib` (124 passed)
- [x] Benchmark sweep above (intra 1-4) reproduced twice, stable.
- [ ] User rebuilds, confirms underruns are no worse than before
      #179 (and ideally a touch better thanks to the retained
      ring-buffer bump).

author: jeremyjpj0916
body:
## Summary

- Frontend HTTP/2 server builders now use dedicated constants instead of backend pool config: 256 KiB stream window, 2 MiB connection window, 16 KiB max frame size, adaptive window disabled
- Frontend HTTP/3 server defaults lowered to 256 KiB stream / 2 MiB connection windows
- Backend pool configs retain their existing optimized values (8 MiB / 32 MiB)
- Operators can still override H3 frontend values via `FERRUM_HTTP3_STREAM_RECEIVE_WINDOW` / `FERRUM_HTTP3_RECEIVE_WINDOW` env vars

**Replaces closed PR #978** which used RFC 7540 minimum values (65,535 bytes) that would cause severe throughput degradation on legitimate traffic.

## Security Impact

Without this fix, frontend H2/H3 listeners use backend-optimized flow-control windows (8 MiB per stream, 32 MiB per connection). A malicious client could open multiple streams and send data up to these limits, forcing the gateway to buffer far more data than necessary for legitimate requests. The new defaults are 32x smaller per-stream and 16x smaller per-connection while remaining practical for real traffic.

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

author: georgebprice
body:
## AI Player Implemented - API, Routes, Prompts, UI/UX

- **AI opponent with optional LLM policy layer**: Deterministic TypeScript AI remains the source of truth, with an optional Anthropic/OpenAI-backed move selector that respects game rules and card-shedding strategy.
- **Quality-of-life & gameplay polish**: Improved win/lose overlay behavior, “Play Again” affordances, and more natural hand dealing/animation between games.

## Scope of Changes

- **Core AI architecture**
  - Exposed deterministic AI helper functions in `AIGameStrategy.ts`:
    - `getCandidatePlays(hand, lastPlay, gameState)` to enumerate legal plays.
    - `chooseBestPlay` to select a move using improved shedding strategy.
  - Updated deterministic AI heuristic:
    - Prefers **weak singleton cards** that do not break pairs/triples when leading.
    - Avoids splitting valuable combos unless needed for blocking or when few options remain.
    - Keeps the existing five-card and pair logic intact.

- **Shared AI types & tactical helpers**
  - Added `app/lib/ai/types.ts`:
    - Common types for `LLMGameState`, `CandidatePlay`, `TacticalFact`, `AIMoveRequest`, and `AIMoveDecision`.
    - Captures structured metadata such as `isLowSheddingCandidate`, `isPowerCardSpend`, `preservesFutureControl`, `engineBaselineRank`, and `planTag`.
  - Added `app/lib/ai/tactical.ts`:
    - Builds compact `LLMGameState` from `GameContext` (hands, deck size, last play, recent move history, seen/unseen rank counts).
    - Produces `tacticalFacts` (“big moves”) such as:
      - Likely/guaranteed single winners given played cards.
      - Combos to preserve (pairs/triples).
      - Opponent near-out signals.
    - Generates enriched `CandidatePlay` objects with:
      - Shedding vs control indicators.
      - Combo usage information.
      - Strategic guidance strings used only by the LLM.

- **LLM gateway & provider integration**
  - Implemented `/api/ai-move/route.ts`:
    - Accepts `AIMoveRequest` containing `LLMGameState` and optional config.
    - Builds provider-agnostic prompts for:
      - **OpenAI** (`gpt-4o-mini` by default) via `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_MODEL`.
      - **Anthropic** (e.g. Haiku) via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_MODEL`.
    - Reads optional runtime env:
      - `AI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` (e.g. `openai`).
      - `AI_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 8000).
      - `AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (default 350).
      - `ENVIRONMENT` (enables verbose logging in `development`).
  - Prompt behavior:
    - System prompts emphasize:
      - Pusoy Dos shedding rules and that **rules are enforced externally**.
      - “Low-card shedding first” and treating high cards as **control assets**.
      - Never inventing cards or plays outside the provided candidates.
    - User payload includes:
      - Compact `LLMGameState`.
      - `candidatePlays` with metadata and field-meaning hints.
      - Explicit decision priorities (win now, block near-out, shed low, preserve control, avoid breaking combos).
    - Responses must be strict JSON with:
      - `action`, `candidateIndex`, `cardIds`, `confidence`, `planTag`, and `reason`.

- **Strategy guards & deterministic fallbacks**
  - All LLM outputs are:
    - Parsed and validated against the candidate set and rules engine.
    - Rejected if they reference non-candidate cards or mismatched `cardIds`.
  - Additional strategy guard:
    - If the LLM attempts to **lead with a power single** (e.g. A/K/Q) while a weak, safe singleton exists and the opponent is not near-out, the server:
      - Logs the rejection reason.
      - Returns a `fallback` action, causing the client to use deterministic `chooseBestPlay`.
  - Deterministic preflight rules to **reduce LLM calls**:
    - In `llm` mode, the **first AI move** in a game is deterministic.
    - In `hybrid` mode, the **first three AI moves** are deterministic.
    - In all modes, if there is a legal move that **empties the AI hand**, it is taken deterministically without an LLM request.

- **GameContext integration & modes**
  - `GameContext.tsx` now:
    - Tracks `moveHistory` entries (player, cards, type, trick number, control flags).
    - Maintains derived state for building `LLMGameState`.
    - Provides `isComputerThinking` to prevent concurrent AI moves.
    - Supports AI opponent modes via env:
      - `NEXT_PUBLIC_AI_OPPONENT_MODE=deterministic | llm | hybrid`.
    - Calls `/api/ai-move` only when:
      - The mode allows it (post-opening-move in `llm`, post-3-moves in `hybrid`).
      - No deterministic “instant win” or forced-play shortcut applies.

- **Developer observability**
  - When `ENVIRONMENT=development`, `/api/ai-move` logs:
    - Provider/model, timeout, and token settings.
    - Tactical facts and candidate summaries (without secrets).
    - Raw LLM response (truncated), parsed decision, and whether it was accepted.
    - Reasons for any strategic rejections and fallbacks to deterministic AI.

- **Gameplay & UI polish related to AI**
  - Win/lose overlay:
    - Now appears with a **1s delay** after a win so players can see the final play.
    - Includes a top-right “×” close button so the losing player can examine the final cards before starting a new game.
  - New **in-table “Play Again” button**:
    - Appears below the main action bar after a game concludes, providing a second way to start a new game alongside the overlay button.
  - Hand dealing between games:
    - Player hand layout and entry animation are **reset** when a new 10-card hand is dealt after `Play Again`, avoiding bunched layouts and mimicking the original first-deal animation.

## Configuration

- **Environment variables**
  - `.env` / `.env.example`:
    - `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_MODEL`
    - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_MODEL`
    - `AI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` (e.g. `openai`)
    - `AI_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`
    - `ENVIRONMENT` (e.g. `development` to enable detailed AI logs)
    - `NEXT_PUBLIC_AI_OPPONENT_MODE=deterministic | llm | hybrid`

## Risks & Rollout Notes

- **Rule consistency**:
  - All move legality is still enforced by `GameRules.ts` / `GameContext.tsx`.
  - LLM outputs are advisory and can be replaced by deterministic AI at any time.
- **API usage & cost**:
  - Deterministic prefilters for:
    - Opening moves (by mode).
    - Obvious winning/empty-hand plays.
  - Strategy guards reduce pointless power-card spends and replays.
  - Further rate limiting and quota enforcement are planned but not yet implemented.
- **User impact**:
  - Default mode can remain `deterministic` for predictable behavior.
  - `llm` and `hybrid` modes offer more varied, human-like play without compromising rules.

## What’s Next (Follow-up Work)

- **Security & rate limiting**
  - Implement the rate limiting and per-session concurrency controls outlined in the design:
    - Per-IP and per-game limits on `/api/ai-move`.
    - Single in-flight AI request per game/session.
- **Difficulty & personality controls**
  - Expose difficulty options in the UI (`easy`/`normal`/`hard`) and wire them into:
    - Prompt hints (aggressive vs defensive).
    - Sampling parameters.
    - Filtering of candidate plays before they are shown to the model (for “easy”).
- **Prompt evaluation & testing**
  - Build small scenario harnesses to verify:
    - Correct use of card memory and tactical facts.
    - Avoidance of early power-card leads.
    - Proper blocking when the opponent is near-out.
  - Run offline `llm` vs `deterministic` matchups to tune strategy and difficulty.
- **Future integrations**
  - Add account-backed stats and persistent options using a database.
  - Investigate richer “human vs human” style experiences driven by the LLM policy layer (e.g. advisory hints, commentary), still bounded by the core rules engine and guardrails.

# Pull Request

## Issue Link
Fixes #1030 (slice 3 of N — stacked on #1101)

## Summary
Adds the legacy OGC Web Coverage Service (WCS 1.x / 2.x) source import path. Many production stacks still serve coverages over WCS rather than the newer OGC API Coverages, so the migration story for #1030 must cover both. This slice introduces a dedicated `IOgcWcsImportService` that sits on top of the slice-2 coverage ingestion pipeline and handles WCS-specific format negotiation before delegating the actual GetCoverage download and raster store registration.

`image/tiff` (and the common GeoTIFF MIME variants) is the deterministic happy-path. Any other requested format — NetCDF, HDF, GML coverage, vendor-specific — is downgraded to manual-review before the source service is contacted, so the WCS layer never asks the slice-2 ingest pipeline to consume bytes it cannot interpret.

- New core service `IOgcWcsImportService` + `OgcWcsImportService` (delegates to slice-2 `IOgcCoverageImportService` — no duplicate ingest logic).

- New admin endpoint `POST /api/v1/admin/import/ogc-wcs/import` with the same dry-run / explicit-apply contract slice 2 established.

- `Program.cs`, `EndpointRegistry.cs`, and a source-gen JSON context (`OgcWcsImportJsonContext`) registered with the server's JSON registry.

author: mihow
body:
## Plain-language summary

Our ML workers — the "ami workers" that pull jobs off the Antenna queue and run detection + classification on bug images — have a long-running memory leak in the PyTorch DataLoader. Each batch leaves behind a few megabytes of shared memory that PyTorch never reclaims. On big jobs the leak adds up fast: a routine 400-image production job recently used up the entire host's RAM in under 20 minutes and got OOM-killed, which dropped about half its images on the floor.

This PR ships three small, contained changes to how the DataLoader is configured plus an explicit cleanup at end of job. Together they should make worker memory stay roughly flat across batches instead of climbing until the kernel kills the process. All three knobs are env-configurable so an operator can opt any single host out if it surfaces a problem with a specific pipeline.

Motivation (2026-05-19 incident with numbers): https://github.com/RolnickLab/ami-data-companion/issues/140#issuecomment-4493340746

## What changes

### 1. `multiprocessing_context="forkserver"` on the DataLoader

The Linux default is `fork`, which makes each DataLoader subprocess inherit the parent's entire memory state via copy-on-write. When the parent process already has large CUDA buffers and pinned memory loaded (a normal state for a running ML worker), every DataLoader subprocess carries that state along as "shared memory" — and PyTorch sometimes can't clean it up on subprocess shutdown. `forkserver` re-execs subprocesses from a clean intermediate state, sidestepping both the inheritance and the cleanup race.

- New env var: `AMI_ANTENNA_API_DATALOADER_MP_CONTEXT`
- Default: `forkserver`
- Allowed values: `fork`, `spawn`, `forkserver`, or empty (let PyTorch pick its default)

This is the fix listed in both #140 and #145 that nobody has tried in production yet.

### 2. `timeout=300` on the DataLoader

When the shared-memory cleanup race in #140 hits, the main thread currently hangs forever in `multiprocessing.Queue.get()` waiting for a subprocess that's already dead. A non-zero `timeout` converts the silent hang into a `RuntimeError` the worker can log, restart from, and move on. Zero risk to the happy path — workers normally finish a batch in seconds, not minutes.

- New env var: `AMI_ANTENNA_API_DATALOADER_TIMEOUT_S`
- Default: 300 (seconds)
- Set to 0 to disable

### 3. Explicit teardown in `_process_job`

In the `finally:` block of `_process_job`, after the `result_poster.shutdown()` call:

```python
del loader
del batch_source
gc.collect()
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

Right now the DataLoader gets dropped implicitly when the function returns. That can leave child processes' shared-memory segments and pipe FDs alive for an unpredictable amount of time. Explicit cleanup tells Python to release references immediately and asks PyTorch to flush its GPU buffer cache. Cheap insurance regardless of which `multiprocessing_context` ends up active, and directly addresses the per-batch pipe-FD accumulation pattern observed in #145.

## Verification on antenna-dev-arctia (H100 24GB MIG, ~68 GiB host RAM)

Supervisor `ami-worker` (2 procs, `--num_workers 1`, `AMI_NUM_WORKERS=1`) restarted with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at the patched worktree. Ran three back-to-back `test_ml_job_e2e` jobs against `quebec_vermont_moths_2023`:

| Job | Images | Detections | Classifications | Failed | Runtime |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 170 (small) | 10 | 68 | 121 | **0** | 18 s |
| 171 (stress) | 212 | 1343 | 2393 | **0** | 66 s |
| 173 (stress 2) | 140 | 902 | 1380 | **0** | 46 s |

Zero image failures across ~360 processed images on the exact pipeline + parallel-2-workers configuration that lost 49% of images on production on 2026-05-19. No OOM kills in `dmesg`. Both workers stayed `RUNNING` throughout.

RSS / shmem-rss trajectory (sampled every 3s during the stress run):

| Worker | min RSS | peak RSS | final RSS | peak shmem | final shmem |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| worker_00 | 1.9 GB | 3.8 GB | 3.8 GB | 1.9 GB | 1.8 GB |
| worker_01 | 2.8 GB | 5.0 GB | 4.5 GB | 3.1 GB | 2.5 GB |

For comparison, the 2026-05-19 production incident saw single-worker peaks of 17–35 GB shmem-rss on the same pipeline before the OS killed the process. The catastrophic per-job blow-up is gone; the residual growth that remains across multiple jobs is the territory of #144 Part B (out of scope here).

DataLoader subprocesses cleaned up cleanly after each job — `pgrep -c pt_data_worker` returned 0 between jobs.

Test suite on the worktree: **21/21 passed** (`pytest trapdata/antenna/tests/`), including the new 8-test `test_dataloader_hygiene.py` regression suite that guards the configuration surface so a future refactor can't silently remove the fix.

## Pipeline-pickling smoke test

`forkserver` pickles the dataset class when spawning subprocesses. Verified manually that `get_rest_dataloader()` with `num_workers=2` + `forkserver` spawns cleanly using `RESTDataset` (the shared dataset class for all pipelines). End-to-end run above used `quebec_vermont_moths_2023`. Other pipelines (panama, uk_denmark, costa_rica_turing, kenya-uganda_turing, anguilla_turing, global, insect_orders, moth_binary) share the same `RESTDataset` so the pickling path is the same — to be exercised in the staged rollout.

## Out of scope (deliberate)

- **`pin_memory` default not touched.** #138 and #122 disagree on the right default for HTTP-sourced workloads. That needs its own measured ablation, not a guess buried in this PR.
- **LRU model eviction (#144 Part A)** and the **worker drain-and-exit recycler (#147)** are separate follow-ups. The residual-RSS measurement (#144 Part B) is implicit in the new regression test.
- **`AMI_NUM_WORKERS` env-var reuse cleanup (#138 item 8)** — doc-only, deferrable.

## Relationship to other open work

Orthogonal to PR #139 (env-knob plumbing on `feature/uv-migration`). This PR is based on `main` and does not modify the same files in conflicting ways.

## Staged rollout plan (post-merge)

1. Build wheel from the merged PR. Install on **one** prod GPU host first.
2. Pull a heavy job; watch `dmesg`, `ps -o pid,rss,cmd -C ami`, `pgrep -c pt_data_worker` for 30+ minutes.
3. If RSS stays bounded and no `RuntimeError: could not unlink ...` events appear, roll to the rest of the fleet.
4. The pipe-FD leak in #145 surfaces at ~6 days of uptime, so the real verdict on the teardown fix is at 7d. Watch one full 24h cycle before declaring fixed.

body:
## Summary

Bundles 4 deferred backlog items from PR #1063 and #1064 review cycles into one focused PR. All are small defensive/perf improvements to the same recovery code path that the rehydration chain just hardened. Net diff: ~220 LOC across 6 files (3 source + 3 test).

## Items closed

1. **Runtime shape validation on `job.returnvalue`** (filed PR #1063 round-5) — `pollPriorJobState` now routes non-object or success-field-missing returnvalues through `'unrecoverable'` instead of casting blindly. Defense-in-depth against ai-worker contract change or partial-write corruption.

2. **Per-delivery try/catch in deferred-dispatch loop** (filed PR #1063 round-3) — `recoverOne`'s post-adoption loop now catches per-call throws so one slot's `handleJobResult` failure doesn't skip remaining deliveries. Matches the per-slot catch pattern in `multiTagDeliveryFlow.deliverSlot`.

3. **`Promise.all` parallelize per-slot recovery** (filed PR #1064 round-2) — in the pending+accessible-personality branch, persona resolution and BullMQ state poll are now dispatched in parallel. Cuts per-slot recovery latency roughly in half for the dominant path. Terminal and revoked branches preserve the no-BullMQ-read behavior (no test regressions).

4. **`resolvePersonaIdOnly` method on `PersonaResolver`** (filed PR #1064 post-autosquash) — new cheaper variant that runs the cascade without the unused `focusModeEnabled` `findFirst` query. Saves one Prisma round-trip per recovery slot. `MultiTagRecovery` switches to use it.

## Out of scope (intentional)

- **Idempotent re-dispatch in deferred-delivery loop** (filed PR #1063 round-6) — exposure window is microsecond-scale (between in-memory slot mutation and Redis `updateEntry` write), requires a crash *during recovery*, and produces "potentially duplicate message" (graceful) rather than "no message." author: sbond-rise
body:
## Summary

The canonical Cowork workflow: Claude (or any external tool) edits a `CLAUDE.md` / `SKILL.md` while the user has it open in Rise MD Editor. The user just sees the new content. No prompt, no friction.

Behaviour on `folder:file-changed`:

| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Clean tab (`isTabDirty === false`) | Silently re-fetch from disk via `files:openPath` + `refreshTabFromDisk`. No prompt. |
| Dirty tab | Existing "this file changed on disk — reload?" prompt. Same UX as before. |

## Why this depends on RAISE-55

Silent reload only works if `isTabDirty` is accurate. Without RAISE-55 (`editorBaseline` round-trip-aware dirty tracking) and its 1-char-edit regression follow-up, this PR would silently overwrite user edits — because `isTabDirty` would either return `true` for unedited URL-text files (RAISE-55 bug) or return `false` for files where the user typed 1–2 characters (RAISE-55 regression). Both have shipped to `main` before this; this builds on the trusted dirty signal.

## Implementation

Small refactor in `App.tsx`'s existing `onFileChanged` effect. The clean-path swallows transient FS errors (file briefly missing during atomic rename, locked by another process, etc.) via `console.warn` — chokidar will fire again once the write settles, so the next event will succeed.

## Test plan

All 5 scenarios smoke-tested locally:

- [x] Open file in Project Mode (folder open). External write via terminal while editor is clean → silent reload within ~1 sec
- [x] Open + type (tab is dirty) + external write → prompt appears as before
- [x] Open + click in document but don't type (still clean) + external write → silent reload
- [x] Open + Cmd+S + external write (clean again after save) → silent reload
- [x] Type + Save + type again (dirty again) + external write → prompt

## Non-goals (noted in CHANGELOG / ticket)

- Single-file mode (no folder open) has no chokidar watcher today. Could add via `fs.watch` on the active tab's path; tracked as a follow-up on [RAISE-56](https://risepeople.atlassian.net/browse/RAISE-56).
- Conflict-resolution UI ("Keep mine / Take theirs" / "Show diff") for dirty tabs: out of scope. The existing prompt is the v1 UX.

## Docs updates

- `docs/architecture.md`: External-edit detection section updated to describe clean/dirty branching and note Project-Mode-only scope.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased]` `### Added` entry.

author: baladithyab
body:
Three logically separable changes, on a single branch, in 4 commits.

## 1. Blog: Notion CMS → repo-owned Astro content collection

Eliminates a runtime dependency, makes the blog build-deterministic, and removes a class of edge-runtime CJS interop issues we had with the Notion SDK.

- New `src/content.config.ts` with glob loader + zod schema.
- All 5 published Notion posts imported to `src/content/blog/*.md` (frontmatter preserves the original Notion page IDs as `sourceNotionId` for legacy redirects).
- New `src/lib/blog.ts` helpers (sort/filter/format).
- `src/pages/blog/index.astro` rewritten to use `getCollection('blog')`.
- `src/pages/blog/[id].astro` (Notion-id route) replaced by `src/pages/blog/[slug].astro` (clean slug route). The slug route also looks up `sourceNotionId` and 301-redirects old `/blog/<notion-uuid>` URLs — no separate redirect route needed.
- `src/lib/notion.ts` (404 lines) deleted.

## 2. Dependency upgrades: Astro 6 / Tailwind 4 / TS 6

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| astro | 5.17.2 | 6.3.5 |
| @astrojs/cloudflare | 12.6.12 | 13.5.2 |
| @astrojs/react | 4.4.2 | 5.0.5 |
| @astrojs/mdx | — | 5.0.6 |
| @astrojs/check | — | 0.9.9 |
| tailwindcss | 3.4.19 | 4.3.0 (via @tailwindcss/vite) |
| typescript | 5.9.3 | 6.0.3 |
| lucide-react | 0.564.0 | 1.16.0 |
| react / react-dom | 19.2.4 | 19.2.6 |
| wrangler | 4.65.0 | 4.93.0 |

Notable workarounds for the Astro 6 + Cloudflare adapter combo:

- Pinned vite to v7 via `overrides` ([withastro/astro#16029](https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/16029)).
- Custom Vite plugin in `astro.config.ts` pre-bundles app deps (React, Radix, lucide-react, astro-navbar, nanostores, etc.) for the workerd SSR environment ([withastro/astro#16248](https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/16248)).
- Switched session driver from `'memory'` (removed in v6) to `sessionDrivers.lruCache({ max: 500 })`.

Tailwind v4 specifics:

- Replaced `@astrojs/tailwind` + `tailwindcss-animate` + `postcss.config.js` with `@tailwindcss/vite` + `tw-animate-css` (CSS import only).
- `src/styles/globals.css` rewritten using `@import 'tailwindcss'` + `@theme inline { ... }` projecting all shadcn HSL tokens through `--color-*`/`--radius-*`/`--font-sans`/animations.
- `tailwind.config.ts` and `postcss.config.js` deleted (Tailwind 4 needs neither).

## 3. Deploy: Cloudflare Pages → Cloudflare Workers (Workers Static Assets)

Cloudflare's recommended path for new Astro projects post-acquisition.

- `wrangler.toml` (Pages-style) → `wrangler.jsonc` (Workers-native), using the Astro 6 unified entrypoint `@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server` so the `main` field resolves at config-time.
- `Astro.locals.runtime.env` (removed in Astro 6) → typed `getRuntimeEnv<T>()` helper in `src/lib/runtime-env.ts` wrapping `import { env } from 'cloudflare:workers'`. Migrated 8 call sites.
- CI workflow renamed `cloudflare-pages-deploy.yml` → `cloudflare-deploy.yml`. Now runs `wrangler deploy` (Workers) + a type-check step. Dropped legacy `NOTION_*` env wiring.
- Dead `functions/` dir removed (was for Pages Functions, never used).
- Docs (`README`, `ARCHITECTURE`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT`, `docs/GITHUB`) rewritten for the Workers model.

## Verification

`bun run build` ✅ clean • `bun run astro check` ✅ 0/0/0 (40 files) • `bun run preview` (workerd via Miniflare) smoke test against the rebuilt artifact:

| Route | Status |
|---|---|
| `/` | 200 |
| `/blog` | 200 |
| `/blog/<slug>` | 200 |
| `/profile` | 200 |
| `/status` | 200 |
| `/protected` | 200 |
| `/api/github/summary` | 200 |
| `/api/auth/session` | 200 |
| `/api/auth/login` | 503 (correct: OIDC not configured) |
| `/blog/<notion-uuid>` × 3 | 301 → `/blog/<slug>` |

`bun audit`: 53 → 9 dev-tooling-only transitives (rollup, picomatch via Vite/Astro/Wrangler chain). No production-runtime exposure.

Source scan: no secrets, no `eval`, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

## Known limitation

`astro dev` may throw `"Astro is not defined"` on first request in some setups — confirmed upstream issue, not introduced by this change ([withastro/astro#16248](https://github.com/withastro/astro/issues/16248) and similar). `astro preview` works correctly and runs the same workerd runtime as production, so it's the recommended local check.

## Post-merge

If the production custom domain is currently attached to the old Cloudflare **Pages** project, follow [Migrate from Pages](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migration-guides/migrate-from-pages/) once the new Worker is healthy.

author: zajalist
body:
Closes the cookbook-classification sprint. New CLIMATE_CLASS_FRAG reads (lat, T, P, continentality, hemisphere, distance-to-ocean) and emits two channels:

- **.r = class id 0..14** (simplified Köppen-Geiger; we lack monthly T/P so this is a coarse 15-class approximation, not full 30-class KG): Ocean, Af, Am, Aw, BWh, BWk, BSh, BSk, Csa, Cfa, Cfb, Dfa/b, Dfc, ET, EF.
- **.g = cookbook precip** per class: Af=0.95, Am=0.88 (tropical monsoon wet), BWh=0.08, BWk=0.10, Cfb=0.78, etc. Overrides the zonal-only CLIM.g for the Precipitation map mode.

Monsoon override: tropical-coastal cells (lat 5-25°, continentality<0.30, T>18°C) are reclassified to Am — captures the cookbook 'east+south coast of large landmass' rule without needing seasonal precip data we don't have. India, SE Asia, Indonesia, NE Brazil, Caribbean → Am wet.

New 'Climate' map mode shows the discrete Köppen palette (ramp id=7) matching the Beck et al. 2023 KG colour key: blue tropics, red deserts, green humid temperate, teal humid continental, grey polar.

Precipitation map mode REPOINTED from CLIM.g (zonal) to CLASS.g (cookbook). The bar's Precipitation chip now shows the cookbook-corrected precip: India/SE Asia wet, Sahara/Arabia dry, Western Europe wet, Mediterranean drier, polar dry.

7 files, ~150 lines. 12/12 equirectMapModes + 19/19 climate-wind green. tsc 0.

author: buildkate
body:
## Summary
- Fix cloud function source artifact being published as a tar archive instead of a real zip, which Cloud Build's gcs-fetcher rejects (blocks `elastic-ci-stack-for-gcp` deploys with autoscaling).
- Root cause: `tar -a -cf foo.zip ...` — GNU tar ignores `-a` and the `.zip` extension, producing a tar with files nested under `cloud_function/`. Replaced with `zip` run from inside `cloud_function/` so `main.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum` land at the archive root where Cloud Functions Gen 2 expects them.


Fixes [A-1239](https://linear.app/buildkite/issue/A-1239).
