author: brucedu521
body: ## Summary 让 Zeabur CLI 跟 dashboard 一样可以切到 team workspace —— 操作 team 拥有的 project / service / deployment。 Closes [PLA-1590](https://linear.app/zeabur/issue/PLA-1590)。 依赖：[PLA-1589](https://linear.app/zeabur/issue/PLA-1589) (`Team.myRole` backend field — backend PR [zeabur/backend#2131](https://github.com/zeabur/backend/pull/2131))。 ## 客户场景 Discord ives.0629 (2026-05-15)：team 成员 alice 想用 CLI deploy team 的 project，但 `zeabur project list` 永远只看到她个人的项目。表象是"team workspace 建的 API key 指向个人"，真实诉求 = **"让 CLI 能操作我所属 team 的 project"**。 取代 [PLA-1542](https://linear.app/zeabur/issue/PLA-1542) / [zeabur/backend#2115](https://github.com/zeabur/backend/pull/2115)（"给 API key 加 team scope"误判方向，详见两个 issue 的 cancellation 说明）。 ## 新增命令 ``` zeabur workspace list # 列 personal + 所有 team（带 role） zeabur workspace current # 显示当前 workspace zeabur workspace switch # 切到 team workspace zeabur workspace clear # 切回 personal（唯一切回个人的方式） ``` 加 global `--workspace ` flag，一次性 override 当前 workspace（不改 persistent state）。 ## 解析规则 ``` workspace switch : arg 是 24-char hex → 当 team ID（必须在 caller 的 memberships 里） arg 不是 hex → 当 name 查 memberships: 0 个匹配 → "no workspace named ..." 1 个匹配 → 切 ≥2 个匹配 → 拒绝并列每个候选的 `zeabur workspace switch ` 命令 ``` `switch personal` **不是**回到个人的快捷方式 —— 它永远是去找名叫 `personal` 的 team（team 名字无限制）。回 personal 用 `workspace clear`。 `--workspace` flag 用同样解析。 ## Switch / clear 副作用 切换 workspace 会**清** project / environment / service context（不同 workspace 的 resource ID 不重叠，留旧 context 必然 stale）。每次 switch / clear 输出都会明示清了什么。 ## 哪些命令受 workspace 影响 只有"目录级"： | 命令 | 用 workspace | |---|---| | `project list` | ✓ | | `project create` | ✓ | | `deploy`（没 link project） | ✓（带 `→ Creating new project in team workspace "xxx"` 提示） | | `service list -p ` | ✗ projectID 自带 owner | | `service deploy -s ` | ✗ serviceID 自带 owner | | `variable create ...` | ✗ | | `deployment log ...` | ✗ | 绝大多数命令对 workspace 透明 —— 跟 dashboard 一致。 ## Startup lazy verify 每次进程启动调一次 `teams` query 验证 persisted workspace 还在不在 caller 的 memberships 里。被删 / 被踢出 → warning + auto fallback personal。Transport error 不动 workspace（offline 不应该静默切人）。 ## 兼容性 - 新 commands 都是 additive - 新 `--workspace` flag 默认 empty（= personal，等同今天） - `ListProjects(ownerID, ...)` / `CreateProject(ownerID, ...)` API 签名改了 —— **内部 caller 全部更新**，外部没有人 import 这两个签名 - Backend `projects(ownerID)` / `createProject(ownerID)` 已经在 prod 跑了一段（team plan PLA-1160 系列），CLI 这边走的是已经存在的 schema 路径 - `Team.myRole` 是 PLA-1589（[zeabur/backend#2131](https://github.com/zeabur/backend/pull/2131)）提供。一起 review、merge 后 deploy。本 PR 的 GraphQL query `teams { _id name myRole }` 在 backend 部署前会报字段不存在 —— prod 用户拿到这个 CLI 的时间一定晚于 backend deploy（CLI 发版需要打 v* tag），所以发版前 backend merge 即可。 ## Tests `internal/cmdutil/workspace_test.go` 覆盖： - 空参数 → required error - ID 命中 / ID 不在 memberships - Name 唯一命中 - Name 无匹配 - **Name 重名 → ambiguous 错误，含每个候选的 switch 命令 + role**（Bruce 明确要求） - `isObjectIDHex` 各种 edge case ``` $ go test -run TestResolveWorkspaceArg|TestIsObjectIDHex ./internal/cmdutil/ === RUN TestResolveWorkspaceArg_EmptyArg --- PASS === RUN TestResolveWorkspaceArg_ByID_Match --- PASS === RUN TestResolveWorkspaceArg_ByID_NotAMember --- PASS === RUN TestResolveWorkspaceArg_ByName_Unique --- PASS === RUN TestResolveWorkspaceArg_ByName_NotFound --- PASS === RUN TestResolveWorkspaceArg_ByName_Ambiguous --- PASS === RUN TestIsObjectIDHex --- PASS PASS ``` 全套 `go test ./...` 通过。 ## 文件清单 新增： - `pkg/zcontext/workspace.go` — Workspace 结构 + Personal/Team 判断 - `pkg/model/team.go` — Team / TeamMemberRole models - `pkg/api/team.go` — ListTeams API - `internal/cmdutil/workspace.go` — `ResolveWorkspaceArg`（核心解析逻辑，flag + switch 共用） - `internal/cmdutil/workspace_test.go` — 7 个 unit test - `internal/cmd/workspace/{workspace,list,current,switch,clear}/` — 4 个子命令 + 父命令 修改： - `pkg/zcontext/{interface,context}.go` — Context 接口加 Workspace - `pkg/api/{interface,project}.go` — ProjectAPI 加 ownerID 参数 - `pkg/selector/selector.go` — `New` 加 ownerIDFn 闭包 - `internal/cmdutil/factory.go` — Factory 加 `Workspace` flag + `CurrentOwnerID()` / `SetWorkspaceOverride()` - `internal/cmd/root/root.go` — 注册 workspace 命令 + `--workspace` global flag + PreRunE 里解析 flag + lazy verify + 用闭包构造 selector - 4 个 caller 更新：`project list` / `project create` / `deploy` / `template deploy` 传 ownerID（`deploy` 多加 team workspace 提示） ## Out of Scope（备查） - ❌ Team-scoped API key（"team service account"）—— 真有需求时单开 issue 做完整 IAM 系统设计，参考 AWS IAM / GCP Service Account / GitHub fine-grained PAT - ❌ 跨 team 聚合 query（"列我所有 team 的 service"）—— 没真实需求 - ❌ Team 命名限制（用户起名自由，"personal" 也允许） 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? ## Summary

Operator screenshot review of the Cuisine TMA map flagged two control-layout problems:

1. **Colour/Greyscale-mode pill was in the wrong place** — the right-side navigation
   cluster. It must sit in the top-left **quick-toggle row**, beside "🚌 Bus Stop".
2. **The quick-toggle pills' dark/near-black OFF background** clashed with the clean
   white navigation buttons.

### Root cause of #2 (a real bug)
`MapControls.jsx` carried its own local `toggleStyle()` with a fixed palette
(`OFF #1F2937` dark slate). CR7 (v0.61.51) made the shared `giaToggleStyle`
theme-aware (light-mode `OFF` = white `#FFFFFF`) but **missed this divergent copy** —
so the quick row never received the CR7 light palette.

### What lands here
- **`MapControls.jsx`** (byte-identical ×3) — imports `giaToggleStyle` and deletes
  the local `toggleStyle`; the `⋯` menu button + `rowToggles` pills now use the
  shared palette (OFF renders white in light mode). New optional **`colourToggle`**
  prop renders the Colour pill **after** the `rowToggles` in the existing `flex-wrap`
  row — beside Bus Stop. Styled `giaToggleStyle(false)` always (CR8: neutral, no
  on/off colour flip; state shown in the label text).
- **`MapPanel.jsx` / `HawkerMapPanel.jsx` / `MrtMapPanel.jsx`** — the Colour
  `<button>` is removed from each `top-12 right-2` nav cluster (now Reset/＋/－/expand
  only); each passes the `colourToggle` prop to `<MapControls>`; the now-unused
  `giaToggleStyle` import is dropped.

Quick row now: `⋯ | 🚉 Train Line | 🅿️ Carpark | 🚌 Bus Stop | 🎨 Colour mode`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build:cuisine` / `build:hawker` / `build:transport` — green
- [x] `npm test` — 1928/1928 passed
- [x] `MapControls.jsx` byte-identical ×3 (md5 `949b2574…`)
- [ ] Manual: Colour pill renders after Bus Stop; OFF row pills render light/white,
  not dark slate; nav cluster is just Reset/＋/－/expand; Colour pill toggles greyscale
  and flips its label; narrow webview wraps the row cleanly.

## Notes
- The quick row gains a 5th pill; its container is already `flex flex-wrap`, so it
  wraps to a second line on narrow viewports rather than overflowing.

author: pranjali-2501
body:
This PR add support for on-premises clients using Google Cloud Interconnect to connect to GCP services via DirectPath by enabling a forced xDS/C2P resolver path.
  
Changes:
  - **Query Parameter Handling:** Updates the `google-c2p` resolver to parse call target URLs for the `force-xds` query parameter.
  - **Metadata Server Bypass:** When executing off-GCP, GCE Metadata Server queries for locality zone and IPv6 capability are bypassed.
  - **Bootstrap Config:**
    - Omits the GCE locality zone structure from the bootstrap configuration.
    - Hardcodes the `TRAFFICDIRECTOR_DIRECTPATH_C2P_IPV6_CAPABLE` node metadata flag to `true` since Interconnect is planned exclusively for IPv6 clients.
    - Formats the xDS Client Node ID using a prefix: `"C2P-non-gcp-UUID"`.
    
RELEASE NOTES:
- xds/googlec2p: enable DirectPath over Interconnect support for on-premises clients via the `force-xds` query parameter in target URI.

author: rajkumar-rangaraj
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3163 — constructing a second `TelemetryClient` against a `TelemetryConfiguration` that has already been built (e.g. by the ASP.NET classic `ApplicationInsightsHttpModule` or by a prior `TelemetryClient` instantiation) no longer throws `InvalidOperationException: "Configuration cannot be modified after it has been built."`

It also fixes the related correctness issue introduced in 3.1.0 (#3137) where the first `TelemetryClient`s `Context` leaked to every subsequent client because it was registered globally as an OTel pipeline processor.

## Root cause

Prior to this PR, the non-DI `TelemetryClient` constructor called `configuration.PrependOpenTelemetryBuilderConfiguration(...)` to register `TelemetryContextActivityProcessor` and `TelemetryContextLogProcessor` *every time it ran*. After the first `Build()` the configuration is sealed, so the second constructor call threw. Even when that issue was worked around, every subsequent `TelemetryClient` would be silently shadowed by the first clients `Context` because the processors were keyed to the first clients `TelemetryContext` instance.

## Approach (Path A — source-level per-call enrichment)

Move `TelemetryContext` enrichment from a pipeline-wide processor to the call site of every `Track*`/`StartOperation*` method on `TelemetryClient`. This is the architecturally clean fix:

- Each `TelemetryClient` carries its own `Context`. At every `Track*`/`StartOperation*` invocation, the clients `Context` (typed fields + `GlobalProperties`) is applied to the outgoing properties dict or `Activity` tags with **skip-if-present** semantics, so item-level values continue to take precedence.
- The non-DI constructor now just calls the idempotent `configuration.Build()`. No pipeline mutation. Constructing N additional `TelemetryClient` instances against the same configuration is safe and cheap.
- Precedence at the emission site is **item dict > GlobalProperties > typed Context**, matching the existing behavior expected by `TelemetryClientTests`.
- The DI path (`UseApplicationInsightsTelemetry` for ASP.NET Core / Worker Service) is **unchanged** — it still registers pipeline-wide `TelemetryContextActivityProcessor`/`TelemetryContextLogProcessor` so OTel-native signals (`ActivitySource`, `ILogger`) emitted *outside* a `TelemetryClient.Track*` call continue to be enriched.

## Changes

### BASE/src/Microsoft.ApplicationInsights/TelemetryClient.cs
- Non-DI constructor no longer calls `PrependOpenTelemetryBuilderConfiguration`; it just calls `Build()` (idempotent, thread-safe).
- New static helpers:
  - `BuildClientContextProperties(TelemetryContext, IDictionary<string,string>)` — returns a mutable, client-context-enriched properties dict (used by `Track*` overloads that dont take an item-level telemetry object).
  - `EnrichActivityWithClientContext(TelemetryContext, Activity)` — applies client context to an activity (used by `StartOperation`).
- Refactored `ApplyContextToProperties` / `ApplyContextToActivity` to take an `overwrite` flag. When `overwrite=false` they implement skip-if-present (preserving caller-set keys/tags).
- All 10 `Track*` methods and all 3 `StartOperation` overloads now thread the clients `Context` through.

### BASE/src/Microsoft.ApplicationInsights/TelemetryClientExtensions.cs
- All 3 `StartOperation` overloads enrich the freshly-started `Activity` with `telemetryClient.Context` via `EnrichActivityWithClientContext`.

### WEB/Src/Web/Web/ApplicationInsightsHttpModule.cs
- Added `static TelemetryClient sharedTelemetryClient` (one host-blessed client per AppDomain).
- Creation is **lazy** on first `OnBeginRequest` so `Init()` no longer triggers `Build()` (which can fail when no connection string is configured).
- `Dispose` is unchanged (the shared instance lives until the AppDomain unloads).

### Tests
- New `BASE/Test/.../TelemetryClientMultiInstanceTests.cs` (6 tests):
  - `SecondTelemetryClient_AgainstBuiltConfiguration_DoesNotThrow` — direct #3163 regression.
  - `ParallelTelemetryClientConstruction_DoesNotThrow` — 32 parallel ctors.
  - `EachTelemetryClient_HasIsolatedContext` — verifies per-instance `Context` isolation.
  - `TrackTrace_FromDifferentClients_CarriesEachClientsContext` — verifies log path enrichment is per-client.
  - `ItemLevelContext_TakesPrecedenceOverClientContext` — verifies skip-if-present precedence.
  - `TrackDependency_FromDifferentClients_CarriesEachClientsContext` — verifies activity path enrichment is per-client.
- New tests in `WEB/Src/Web/Web.Tests/ApplicationInsightsHttpModuleTests.cs` (2):
  - `Init_AllowsAdditionalTelemetryClientsToBeConstructedAfterInit` — #3163 regression in the HttpModule scenario.
  - `Init_AdditionalTelemetryClients_HaveIsolatedContext` — per-client `Context` isolation in the same scenario.

## Test results

- **BASE** (`Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.Tests`, net8.0): 225/225 pass — including the 6 new tests.
- **WEB HttpModule** (net462): 16/16 pass — including the 2 new tests.
- **NETCORE Integration** (net8.0): 39/39 pass — confirming the DI path is unchanged.

## Diff stat

```
 BASE/src/Microsoft.ApplicationInsights/TelemetryClient.cs           | 297 +++++++++++++--------
 BASE/src/Microsoft.ApplicationInsights/TelemetryClientExtensions.cs |  12 +
 WEB/Src/Web/Web/ApplicationInsightsHttpModule.cs                    |  23 +-
 WEB/Src/Web/Web.Tests/ApplicationInsightsHttpModuleTests.cs         |  73 +++++
 BASE/Test/.../TelemetryClientMultiInstanceTests.cs                  | new
 CHANGELOG.md                                                        |   1 +
 6 files changed, 499 insertions(+), 115 deletions(-)
```

## Backward compatibility

- Public API: no changes (no edits to `.publicApi/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`).
- DI scenarios (ASP.NET Core, Worker Service): unchanged behavior; pipeline-wide context processors remain.
- Non-DI scenarios (classic ASP.NET, console, NLog): now per-client `Context` is correctly scoped to that client. The only observable difference for non-DI users is that raw `ActivitySource.StartActivity(...)` / `ILogger.Log(...)` calls (not routed through `TelemetryClient`) no longer get auto-enriched with the first `TelemetryClient`s `Context`. This was an undocumented side effect of the 3.1.0 design; restoring v3.0.0 behavior is arguably correct.

## CHANGELOG

Added an `Unreleased` entry. The placeholder `/pull/0000` URL will be replaced with the real PR number after this PR is opened.

Closes #3163.

## Summary

- **Admin/Member roles** on users with a built-in `default-administrator` that cannot be deleted or demoted
- **Per-space access grants** — Members only see spaces they created or were explicitly granted; Admins see all
- **Actor resolution middleware** centralises `X-User-Id` → `Actor` lookup (role + accessible space IDs) across all routes; soft-deleted actors get 400
- **SSE filtering** — stream events are now scoped to the subscriber's accessible spaces at connect time
- **Frontend affordance hiding** — role selector (Admin-only), space management controls (Owner/Admin only), empty state for Members with no spaces

## What changed

**Backend**
- DB: `role` on `users`, `created_by` on `spaces`, new `user_space_access` table (migration 0007)

author: staspisockij
body:
## Root Cause

`get_heroku_logs()` holds a Redis lock with `expire=30` but makes 2 HTTP calls inside:
1. `call_heroku_api("POST", ...)` — has 5 retries with exponential backoff, **no timeout on `requests.request()`** (could hang indefinitely)
2. `requests.get(log_url, timeout=30)`

Total possible time inside lock: unbounded. Lock expires before `__exit__` calls `release()` → `NotAcquired` crashes the autoscaler thread.

**Sentry:** FLOSHIP-SHIPPING-1FE

## Changes

1. **Add `timeout=30` to `requests.request()`** in `call_heroku_api` — prevents indefinite hangs (was missing entirely)
2. **Increase lock expire** for `get_heroku_logs` from 30s → 90s — covers 2 HTTP timeouts + margin
3. **Catch `NotAcquired`** at all 5 `cache.lock` sites — log warning instead of crashing:
   - `check_for_sibling_zombie_dynos` (L1002)
   - `upscale_formation_to_next_level` (L1052)
   - `downscale_formation_to_original_size` (L1207)
   - `restart_dyno` (L1245)
   - `get_heroku_logs` (L1321)
4. **Import `redis_lock.NotAcquired`** with fallback class for envs without redis_lock
5. **5 new tests** covering lock expiry at each site

## Tests

325/325 pass (including 5 new lock expiry tests).

## Summary
- COMPLETED 영역에서 같은 트리에 속한 부모와 자식이 시간상 인접한데도 서로 다른 그룹으로 분리되어 "부모 라벨 + 자식 행" / "부모 행"이 따로 보이던 어색한 표시를 해결.
- 그룹 키를 `parent.id` → **트리 root.id**로 변경. 인접한 같은 트리 항목들을 한 그룹으로 묶고, 그룹 안에서 depth 오름차순 정렬로 부모 → 자식 순으로 트리 형태 표시.
- 그룹 안에 부모(parent=nil)도 들어 있으면 그룹 헤더 라벨 없이 부모 행 + 자식 행을 들여쓰기 트리로 렌더링. 자손만 있으면 출처 부모 경로를 그룹 헤더로 한 번만 노출.
- `CompletedRowView`에 `depth: Int` 파라미터 추가 — `12 + depth*24` leading padding으로 들여쓰기.

## Before / After

**Before** (`parent.id` 그룹 키):

```
COMPLETED
  ...
  데이터 체크 >          ← 자식 그룹 헤더 (parent=데이터 체크)
  ● 지정인 중에 …  13:31
  ● 데이터 체크    13:31  ← 부모 자기 자신은 별도 그룹 (parent=nil)
```

**After** (트리 root.id 그룹 키):

```
COMPLETED
  ...
  ● 데이터 체크          13:31    ← 부모 행 (depth=0)
      ● 지정인 중에 …    13:31    ← 자식 행 (depth=1, 들여쓰기)
```

## Test plan

author: dichovsky
body:
## Summary

Adds full Confluence v2 `admin-key` resource coverage — the tenant-scoped, time-bound privileged credential needed for admin-only operations (permanent page/space deletion, etc.). The new `AdminKeyResource` exposes `get` / `create` / `delete`, wires it under `ConfluenceClient.adminKey`, surfaces the same three actions via the `atlas confluence admin-key …` CLI namespace, and documents both the surface and the matrix in the bundled Claude Code skill.

## Backlog tasks closed

- **B047** — Confluence: expose `DELETE /admin-key`
- **B048** — Confluence: expose `GET /admin-key`
- **B049** — Confluence: expose `POST /admin-key`

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Class method | CLI invocation |
| ------ | ---- | ------------ | -------------- |
| GET    | `/wiki/api/v2/admin-key` | `client.adminKey.get()` | `atlas confluence admin-key get` |
| POST   | `/wiki/api/v2/admin-key` | `client.adminKey.create(data?)` | `atlas confluence admin-key create [--duration-hours <1-24>]` |
| DELETE | `/wiki/api/v2/admin-key` | `client.adminKey.delete()` | `atlas confluence admin-key delete` |

Reference: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-admin-key/

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean (only 2 pre-existing unrelated `no-problems-reported` warnings in `install-skill.test.ts` / `version.test.ts`)
- [x] `npm test` — 1667 passed / 0 failed
- [x] `npm run codemap` then `npm run validate` — full chain (`codemap:check`, coverage, `format:check`, `build`, `test:exports`) green
- [x] Coverage on changed files
  - `src/confluence/resources/admin-key.ts` → 100% stmts/branches/funcs/lines
  - `src/confluence/client.ts`, `src/cli/commands/confluence.ts`, `src/cli/router.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts` → 100% maintained
  - Overall project coverage: **100%** (2059 stmts, 1320 branches, 409 funcs, 1852 lines)
- [x] New unit tests in `test/confluence/admin-key.test.ts` (9 cases) assert exact request method/path/body/query per method, plus an error-propagation guard
- [x] New CLI dispatcher cases in `test/cli/commands.test.ts` (7 cases) cover happy path, all option-validation branches, and the unknown-action branch
- [x] New E2E rows in `test/e2e/cli-confluence.test.ts` (4 cases) drive the full `runCli → ConfluenceClient → HttpTransport → fetch` pipeline
- [x] `test/cli/skill-content.test.ts` and `test/cli/help.e2e.test.ts` allow-lists / dispatcher maps extended for the new resource (drift guard would otherwise fail)

## Files changed

- **Resource:** `src/confluence/resources/admin-key.ts` (new)
- **Types:** `src/confluence/types.ts` (new `AdminKey`, `CreateAdminKeyData`)
- **Client wiring:** `src/confluence/client.ts` (new `adminKey` readonly property)
- **CLI:** `src/cli/commands/confluence.ts` (new `executeAdminKey` + `admin-key` switch case), `src/cli/router.ts` (new `--duration-hours` flag), `src/cli/help.ts` (RESOURCES line)
- **Skill docs:** `skill/reference/confluence.md` (matrix row + dedicated section + CLI examples)
- **Tests:** `test/confluence/admin-key.test.ts` (new), `test/cli/commands.test.ts` (mock + 7 cases), `test/e2e/cli-confluence.test.ts` (4 matrix rows), `test/e2e/helpers/fixtures.ts` (`adminKey` fixture), `test/cli/skill-content.test.ts` (drift allow-list), `test/cli/help.e2e.test.ts` (dispatcher map)
- **Backlog:** `BACKLOG.md` (removed B047/B048/B049 entries), `BACKLOG-ARCHIVE.md` (new `🧩 Confluence` section; closed entries appended with Impl/Rat)
- **Generated:** `CODEMAP.md` (regenerated)

## Notes for reviewer

- **No `durationInHours` client-side range check.** The Confluence API server validates 1-24; replicating it in the SDK would just create drift if Atlassian changes the cap. The CLI only enforces "positive integer" (via the existing shared `asPositiveInt` helper), and the resource passes the payload through verbatim. If you prefer client-side validation, happy to add it.
- **`create()` with no body.** When the caller passes no payload, the transport receives `body: undefined` (i.e. no request body), matching the Confluence "use server default duration" contract. An explicit `{}` is also accepted and passed through — there's an explicit unit test for that branch.
- **Archive structure.** `BACKLOG-ARCHIVE.md` previously lacked a `🧩 Confluence` section; I added one between `Core` and `Jira` to mirror the live backlog's section order. No existing entries were moved.
- **E2E rows.** Followed the existing pattern: routes table → captured method/path/body/query assertions. The `admin-key create` no-flag row asserts `body == null` because the fetch-mock harness reports an empty body that way.
- **No out-of-scope additions.** The 3 backlog tasks are exactly the 3 methods on the new resource; no adjacent endpoints were touched.

author: avalarin
body:
## Summary

- **Batch unread loading**: replaces 1840 individual `GET /channels/{id}/unread` calls (all hitting 429 rate limit) with 2 batch requests — `GetMyChannelMembersForTeam` + channel list already fetched at startup. Unread count = `channel.total_msg_count - member.msg_count`. No more missing badges.
- **markReadCmd fix**: `handleKeyChannels` was setting `m.activeChannelID` to the new channel before emitting `MsgChannelSelected`, so `prevChannelID == msg.ChannelID` in the handler and `markReadCmd` never fired. Now captured and called correctly before the assignment.
- **Cursor preservation in `WithSortAndFilter`**: previously reset `selectedIdx = 0` on every call, which broke navigation when `MsgUnreadsLoaded` arrived mid-scroll (~1s with the new batch approach). Now restores cursor by channel ID, same as `openIdx` was already handled.

## Test plan

- [ ] Launch app — unread badges appear in channels sidebar within ~1s (no more rate limit errors)
- [ ] Navigate channel list with ↑/↓ — cursor does not jump to top after badges load
- [ ] Open channel A, switch to channel B — A's badge disappears (markReadCmd fires correctly)
- [ ] `--headless` mode prints per-channel unread counts and tests MarkChannelRead flow; Ctrl+C cancels the diagnostic goroutine cleanly

## Summary

Closes #349. Correct the cache-fingerprint description on the response-caching tutorial: the caller key is intentionally excluded from the cache fingerprint (the code documents this explicitly in a module-level comment), but the tutorial prose claimed the opposite at two places — line 19 (conceptual explanation) and line 119 (verification recap). Fixed both.

Operational consequence (security-relevant): two callers issuing the same prompt to the same model alias hit the same cache entry. An operator reading the prior text would assume per-caller cache isolation that does not exist, with downstream consequences when choosing what to cache.

Doc-only diff (2 lines edited). No code, schemas, configs, or test fixtures touched.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/tutorials/enable-response-caching.md` | **Line 19** (How It Works): replaced the incorrect "fingerprint built from the resolved model alias, the caller key, and the request body" sentence with an accurate fingerprint description that enumerates the fields actually hashed (model alias + normalized messages + `temperature` + `top_p` + `max_tokens` + tool-calling extras), explicitly bolded the caller-key exclusion, and added an operational callout warning operators that prompts cross caller boundaries (so prompts and responses that should not be visible to other callers in the deployment should not be cached). **Line 119** (What Just Happened): removed the "caller key" reference from the verification recap so it matches the conceptual explanation. |

Net diff: 1 file, +2 / −2. Source: `git diff --stat`.

## Test plan

Doc-only diff — no `.rs` files, schemas, configs, or test fixtures touched. The cargo trio was still run end-to-end as the canonical pre-merge gate. Used `-j 2` for parallel compile cap per the locked workaround on this 8 GB VPS.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — PASS (exit 0).
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -j 2 -- -D warnings` — PASS (exit 0, 0.62s incremental, no warnings).
- [x] `cargo test --workspace -j 2` — PASS (exit 0; 33 suites all green; 1067 tests passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored).
- [x] `grep -rln docs/tutorials/enable-response-caching.md tests/e2e/` returns empty. `pnpm test` under `tests/e2e/` is not applicable for this diff. The cache contract this tutorial describes IS exercised by `tests/e2e/src/cases/cache-policy-e2e.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/src/cases/cache-scenarios-e2e.test.ts` (already referenced in the tutorial's closing paragraph), but those exercise the `x-aisix-cache` header values and upstream `receivedRequests.length` counts — neither touches the caller-key-exclusion property, which is verified at the unit-test layer in the cache crate.

### `cargo clippy` tail

```text
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.62s
```

### `cargo test` summary

```text
33 test-suite-result lines, all 'ok'. Aggregate: 1067 tests passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored across the workspace.
```

## Affected pages

- `docs/tutorials/enable-response-caching.md`

## Pre-merge-check verification log

Issue #349 called out two pre-merge checks. Both resolved as follows:

1. **At PR open time, re-verify the module-level comment at `crates/aisix-cache/src/key.rs:4-6` still says the caller's ApiKey is excluded.** Verified on current `origin/main` HEAD `2c1d485`:

   ```rust
   //! Canonical cache-key fingerprint.
   //!
   //! The key is a stable hash of the *request fingerprint* — the fields
   //! that materially affect the upstream response. Anything else (request
   //! id, deadlines, the caller's ApiKey, custom headers) is excluded so
   //! two callers asking the same question hit the same entry.
   ```
   ✓ Verbatim match. Caller's ApiKey explicitly listed in the exclusion set.

2. **Re-verify `CacheKey::from_request` does not read the caller's API key into the fingerprint.** Verified on the same HEAD at `crates/aisix-cache/src/key.rs:45-57`:

   ```rust
   pub fn from_request(req: &ChatFormat) -> Self {
       Self {
           model: req.model.clone(),
           messages: req.messages.iter().map(message_pair).collect(),
           temperature_milli: req.temperature.map(quantise_milli),
           top_p_milli: req.top_p.map(quantise_milli),
           max_tokens: req.max_tokens,
           extras: canonical_extras(&req.extra),
       }
   }
   ```
   ✓ Six fields read from the request: `model`, `messages`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `extras`. No caller-API-key read site.

3. **Line-number drift check.** Issue body's draft referenced `:394`, which exceeds the file's actual length (144 lines on `2c1d485`). Located the two actual problematic statements via `grep -n 'caller key'` against the current file: lines 19 (conceptual explanation) and 119 (verification recap). Both fixed in this PR; line-number correction also recorded in the issue body's Walkthrough evidence.

4. **CLAUDE.md §7 — N/A**. This PR documents an internal cache mechanic, not an upstream-provider wire-format claim. No reference-implementation or upstream-spec citation required.

## Summary

Sixth Phase 3 schematic sub-phase. Wires the 8 MCU PWM pins (Phase 2e bdshot-locked) to 8 motor solder-pad pairs.

## hwdef.dat-cited authoritative pin map (Phase 2e lock)

| PWM # | Net | MCU pin | hwdef.dat line | Timer + Channel | BIDIR |
|---:|---|---|---|---|:---:|
| 1 | MOT1 | PB0  | 165 | TIM3_CH3 | ✓ |
| 2 | MOT2 | PB1  | 166 | TIM3_CH4 | — |
| 3 | MOT3 | PA0  | 167 | TIM2_CH1 | ✓ |
| 4 | MOT4 | PA1  | 168 | TIM2_CH2 | — |
| 5 | MOT5 | PA2  | 169 | TIM5_CH3 | ✓ |
| 6 | MOT6 | PA3  | 170 | TIM5_CH4 | — |
| 7 | MOT7 | PD12 | 171 | TIM4_CH1 | ✓ |
| 8 | MOT8 | PD13 | 172 | TIM4_CH2 | — |

## Three topology forks resolved inline

| Fork | Resolution | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Connector type | **SOLDER PADS** (16 pads = 8 signals + 8 GND returns). 8× Conn_01x02 in schematic. | MatekH743 reference convention + Phase 2.5 P0.4 "TBD" note. Pads smaller than JST-SH → Phase 2.5 fit assessment only improves. |
| DShot series-R | **NONE** | MatekH743-bdshot/hwdef.dat:23-30 declares bare PWM. BIDIR-correct (R affects both directions on the 4 BIDIR channels). Phase 6g sim validates ringing. |
| Power passthrough | **SIGNAL + GND only** | Standard multirotor topology (ESCs powered from battery, not FC). CLAUDE.md §3.4 logic-level 3.3V. |

## Pipeline result

| Metric | Before (3a-3e) | After (3a-3f) | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SKiDL ERC errors | 0 | **0** | 0 |
| SKiDL ERC warnings | 83 | **75** | **−8** (all 8 MCU PWM pins newly connected) |
| Netlist-gen errors | 0 | **0** | 0 |
| Netlist-gen warnings | 88 | 104 | +16 (more parts → harmless random-tag warnings) |
| Rail-uniqueness guard | PASS | **PASS** | unchanged |
| Unique cross-sheet nets | 15 | **23** | +8 (MOT1..MOT8) |

## Files changed (8)

New:
- `hardware/kicad/novapcb/sheets/esc_3f.py` (~145 lines, hwdef-cited + MatekH743 ref + datasheet reasoning)
- `tasks/phase-3f-esc.yaml`

Modified:
- `hardware/kicad/novapcb/generate.py` — `import sheets.esc_3f`
- `hardware/kicad/novapcb/fp-lib-table` — `+Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm` (Phase 4 swaps to production solder-pad footprint)
- `hardware/kicad/novapcb/novapcb.net` — regenerated
- `hardware/kicad/novapcb/generate.erc` — regenerated
- `docs/CONFIDENCE_MAP.md` — row 8 (MEDIUM-HIGH ~88% → ~89%)
- `docs/DESIGN_PHASES.md` — Phase 3: 3a-3f done

## SOTA self-audit

1. **SOTA?** Yes. The BIDIR-correctness reasoning behind the no-series-R call ("R would affect both directions on the 4 BIDIR channels") is the kind of design-judgement that should be explicit. Solder-pads-over-connectors matches MatekH743 reference + lowers BOM/profile. No-power-passthrough honors standard multirotor topology.
2. **Skipped cheap verification?** No DShot signal-integrity sim (Phase 6g) — ringing on bare lines, BIDIR-line return-path. Within scope: hwdef cite + MatekH743 inheritance + topology decisions all done.
3. **Future trap?** No series-R might mean ringing on long traces — Phase 6g will catch + recommend a properly-sized R if needed. Mitigation: flagged in CONFIDENCE_MAP row 8 evidence note + esc_3f.py docstring. Phase 4 layout pad-geometry placeholder noted (Conn_01x02 with 2.54mm header footprint is just for SKiDL; production swaps to proper solder-pad land pattern).

## Verified vs NOT verified

**Verified:**
- hwdef.dat:165-172 grep'd + cited (matches Phase 2e bdshot lock exactly)
- MatekH743-bdshot/hwdef.dat:23-30 cited (no series R in reference)
- CLAUDE.md §3.4 cited (logic level + standard topology)
- 8 unique MOT1..MOT8 nets in `novapcb.net` (no `_N` duplicates)
- Guard PASS

**NOT verified:**
- No DShot signal-integrity sim (Phase 6g) — ringing margin, BIDIR SI
- No silicon (Phase 9) — actual ESC arming + spin-up + BIDIR telemetry
- No reference cross-check (Phase 3.5)
- No production solder-pad footprint (Phase 4 layout) — current footprint is placeholder PinHeader 2.54mm

- [x] hwdef.dat lines 165-172 cited

- [ ] Phase 9 bench (8-motor arming, BIDIR telemetry reads)

- **What**: Added `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` attributes to the mobile menu button and accordion submenu links. Updated JavaScript to dynamically toggle `aria-expanded` state.
- **Why**: To ensure keyboard and screen reader users have proper context about the mobile menu and its submenus' open/closed states.
- **Before/After**: The mobile menu toggle and submenu links previously lacked ARIA attributes conveying their state. Now they correctly communicate their expanded/collapsed state to assistive technologies.
- **Accessibility**: Improves WCAG compliance by providing explicit state information (via `aria-expanded`) and structural relationships (via `aria-controls`) for interactive expanding components.

## Summary

Press ⌘K (or Ctrl+K on non-Mac) anywhere on the site to open a modal Pagefind search, instead of navigating to `/search`. The Header search icon now opens the same modal while keeping `/search` as a no-JS fallback.

### What's new

- **`src/components/SearchModal.astro`** (new): terminal-styled overlay with lazy-loaded Pagefind UI
  - Opens on ⌘K / Ctrl+K (toggle) or click on `[data-search-trigger]`
  - Closes on ESC / backdrop click / close button / clicking a result
  - Arrow Up/Down navigates between results, Enter opens
  - `astro:page-load` initialization + `AbortController` cleanup → compatible with Astro view transitions
  - DEV mode shows a friendly "build the project to enable search" notice (Pagefind needs build)
  - Empty state placeholder when input is empty
- **`src/layouts/Layout.astro`**: inject `<SearchModal />` globally inside `<body>`
- **`src/components/Header.astro`**: existing `/search` link gains `data-search-trigger` + `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K"` + tooltip "Search (⌘K)"

### What's not changed

- **`src/pages/search.astro`** stays untouched — direct URL access still works as a fallback, and the `SearchAction` JSON-LD target still points there
- No new dependencies (Pagefind + default UI already installed)

### Design notes

Inspired by [astro-devosfera's SearchModal](https://github.com/0xdres/astro-devosfera/blob/main/src/components/SearchModal.astro), simplified to fit our terminal aesthetic:
- Removed: aurora orbs, sparkles, cursor-follow glow, animated conic-gradient border
- Kept: modal core logic, Pagefind UI overrides, keyboard navigation
- Adjusted: uses our CSS variables (`--background`, `--accent`, `--font-app`), matches the same `border-2 border-accent/50` + `bg-muted/40` look as code blocks

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run build` — 243 pages, 0 errors
- [x] `astro check` — 0 errors
- [x] ESLint / Prettier — pass
- [x] Pagefind indexing succeeds (83 pages indexed)

  - [ ] ⌘K opens modal from any page
  - [ ] ESC / backdrop click / X button closes it
  - [ ] Search returns results, click result → navigates + closes modal
  - [ ] Arrow keys navigate between results
  - [ ] Mobile menu search icon also opens the modal
  - [ ] `/search` direct URL still works (fallback / SEO)
  - [ ] Dark + light theme both render correctly

author: k-junior-claw
body:
## Summary

S10 cleanup slice for #2509: removes two `colonial_pressure.dart` peace-target predicates that became no-ops after the goal-phase refactor, plus the constant they fed and their call sites/tests. **Behavior is unchanged** — this is pure dead-code retirement aligned with the issue's S10 directive to "retire `colonial_pressure.dart` peace-target ratchet" in favor of EXPAND/COLONIAL/DEVELOP phase imperatives (`SPEC/ai/ai-architecture.md` § Observer goal phases).

## Changes

- **`shouldSkipBelowQuotaGpOnlyBlockerPeacePass`** always returned `false`. The two `if (!shouldSkip(...))` guards in `domain_planner_orchestrator.dart` and `diplomacy_planner.dart` always passed, so the helper and the conditional wrapping are removed (call bodies are unconditional now).
- **`plateauMutualInvadableBlockerPeaceTargets`** always returned `const []`. Five `.isNotEmpty` / `.contains(...)` / spread call sites simplify accordingly:
  - `diplomacy_planner_peace_targets.dart` — drops a disjunct from `_hasStalledExpansionDistractionWar`, a `yield*` from `_expandRatchetGreatPowerPeaceTargets`, and a spread from `preserveBlockerPeace`.
  - `diplomacy_planner.dart` — simplifies `allowBlockerPeace` to the surviving `unwinnableSoleGpFrontierPeaceTarget` check.
  - `diplomatic_candidate_scoring_offer_peace.dart` — drops the dead `if` branch that added `kOfferPeacePlateauMutualBlockerBonus`; the surviving `else if` (now `if`) is unchanged.
- **`kOfferPeacePlateauMutualBlockerBonus`** in `ai_victory_config.dart` is removed (orphan after the scoring branch above).

The dead `colonial_pressure.dart` exports in `diplomacy_planner.dart`'s `show`-list are also cleaned up.

## Why this is safe

Both removed helpers are provably no-ops on every input:

- `shouldSkipBelowQuotaGpOnlyBlockerPeacePass(...)` had a single `return false;`.
- `plateauMutualInvadableBlockerPeaceTargets(...)` had a series of guards that all bailed with `const []` and a final `return const [];` past the guards (the trailing comment already noted "Mutual below-quota peace on the sole GP blocker stalls turn-100 conquest").

Inlining `false` and `const []` is behavior-preserving — no AI scoring, peace target set, or order suggestion changes. Risk to the seed-42 turn-100/150 observer gates is zero by construction.

## Scope vs deferred (Refs #2509)

| Acceptance criterion | Status |
|----|----|
| S10: observer goal phases (EXPAND/COLONIAL/DEVELOP) implemented | Already on `origin/dev` (#2552–#2579) |
| S10: retire `colonial_pressure` peace-target ratchet | **This PR** retires two clearly dead predicates + their fed constant. Remaining `colonial_pressure.dart` helpers (`belowQuotaPeerGpPeaceTargets`, `nearQuotaHoldPeaceTargets`, `quotaMet*`, etc.) still have non-trivial bodies that the EXPAND/COLONIAL-lite phase ratchet relies on; further retirement is a separate slice gated by observer evidence. |
| S10: tune until nightly green on seed 42 | Out of scope (no scoring changes here) |
| Other systemic / observer / CI ACs | Out of scope |

No SPEC update required: `SPEC/ai/ai-architecture.md` § Observer goal phases already directs this retirement, and behavior is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd packages/colonizethis_ai && dart test` (276 tests, including all surviving `colonial_pressure`, `diplomacy_planner_below_quota_peace*`, and `observer_goal_phase` cases).
- [x] `cd packages/colonizethis_data && dart test` (253 tests).
- [x] `dart run tool/run_workspace_analyze_errors_only.dart` — no analyzer errors workspace-wide.
- [x] `cd packages/colonizethis_ai && dart analyze` — same 24 pre-existing warnings/info as on `origin/dev` (no new diagnostics introduced by this change; e.g. unused-import warnings in `diplomacy_planner_below_quota_peace*_test.dart` exist on `dev` and are out of scope).

Refs #2509

author: adamlu123
body:
## Summary

Adds the bits needed to actually train the web-agent on the harder om2w split on a 4-GPU box, plus a second prompt mode where the agent orchestrates Browserbase sessions itself.

### Training
- `configs/qwen35_4b_web_agent_hard_4gpu.yaml` — hard om2w parquets, 4 GPUs, Browserbase paid-tier concurrency.
- `configs/qwen35_4b_web_agent_hard_4gpu_self_launch.yaml` — same, but `prompt_mode=self_launch_persistent_browser`.
- `scripts/run_web_agent_hard_4gpu.sh` — self-contained launcher (conda env, cred sourcing, SkyRL entrypoint).
- `scripts/run_web_agent.sh` — source `cred.sh` + `cred_gateway.sh`, unset stale `OPENAI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, export browserbase / HF / data env, point at the hard config by default.
- `data/web_agent/om2w_hard_{train,val}.parquet` — small task fixtures.

### Prompt + environment
- `prompts.py` — rewritten `default` mode to drive Playwright via `python -c '...'` (page/context/browser/task already in scope); added `self_launch_persistent_browser` mode that exposes the persistent Browserbase session descriptor and an exploration-session workflow.
- `dataset.py` + `entrypoint.py` — thread `prompt_mode` through the config so `WebAgentTaskDataset` picks the registered prefix.
- `web_environment.py` — remove the `web` CLI shim (returns rc=127 with a hint to use `python -c`). Drop a `.persistent_session.json` descriptor in the workspace at Playwright start. Export `WEB_AGENT_WORKSPACE` / `WEB_AGENT_POLICY_URL` / `WEB_AGENT_POLICY_MODEL` / `WEB_AGENT_PERSISTENT_*` to subprocesses. On cleanup, `REQUEST_RELEASE` every Browserbase session the rollout opened (persistent + any `*session*.json` the agent created), so concurrency quota returns immediately instead of after the 20-minute timeout.
- `web_agent_generator.py` — resolve SkyRL's inference-engine HTTP endpoint and pass it to the env as `policy_endpoint_url` so the in-rollout tools can call the *current* policy. Rename `_compute_reward` → `_score_via_reward_fn` for clarity.

### Policy-as-judge tools
- `echo_rl/web_agent/tools/policy_chat.py` — tiny httpx wrapper that posts OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` to `$WEB_AGENT_POLICY_URL`.
- `echo_rl/web_agent/tools/image_qa.py` — ask the policy a grounded question about screenshots.
- `echo_rl/web_agent/tools/self_reflection.py` — webwright-style per-image scoring + aggregated success/failure verdict, but using the policy itself as the judge.
- `pyproject.toml` — register `image_qa` / `self_reflection` / `web_agent_policy_chat` as console scripts.

### Tests
- `tests/test_web_agent_e2e.py` — scripted-rollout commands switched from the removed `web` CLI to `python -c` snippets.

## Test plan
- [ ] Smoke run: `bash scripts/run_web_agent_hard_4gpu.sh` on a 4-H100 box.
- [ ] Self-launch run: `CONFIG_NAME=qwen35_4b_web_agent_hard_4gpu_self_launch.yaml bash scripts/run_web_agent_hard_4gpu.sh`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_web_agent_e2e.py -k scripted_rollout` (uses stub Playwright).
- [ ] Verify Browserbase sessions are released within ~30s of rollout end (check dashboard).

author: aleksanderem
body:
Auto-generated by Claude in response to issue #603.

Closes #603

---

## Claude summary

Committed. Summary:

I tightened `SupabaseDb.get` and `SupabaseDb.getMany` with typed overloads that mirror the existing `query()` pattern: calling `db.get("users", id)` now returns `SupabaseRow<"users"> | null` instead of `Record<string, unknown> | null`. The original loose signatures stay as fallback overloads for explicit-generic call sites and Supabase-only tables.

I fixed the ripple in the `.filter((x): x is Record<string, unknown> => x !== null)` predicates the issue called out — four sites in `convex/gabinet/appointments.ts` and two in `convex/gabinet/nudges.ts`. Each now uses the concrete row type as the type guard.

I did *not* tighten `insert` / `patch`. The natural `row: Partial<SupabaseRow<TableName>>` overload triggers TS2589 ("type instantiation excessively deep") in every caller of the `SupabaseDb` interface — 1474 errors across the whole convex tree, not just at insert/patch call sites. The issue is `Doc<TableName>` distributing over the full Convex schema union inside a generic-overload constraint. The code comment now documents this limit so future work doesn't re-tread the same path.

All three `tsc` passes (`convex/tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.app.json`, `tsconfig.node.json`) succeed. Unit tests show 18 pre-existing failures in `automation.test.ts` that are present on `c6e3a3b` (parent commit) without my changes — unrelated.

## Follow-ups
- Investigate TS2589 from `Partial<SupabaseRow<TableName>>` in SupabaseDb overloads: the natural tightening for `insert`/`patch` ripples a "type instantiation excessively deep" error to every caller; needs either a non-distributive helper, a per-call typed wrapper, or a schema-shape simplification before insert/patch can be tightened.
- Fix 18 pre-existing automation.test.ts failures: tests like "createRule persists the expected rule shape" and "send_sms_request action stays compatible with legacy SMS execution path" are failing on main, unrelated to type tightening.

author: bestter
body:
💡 What: Replaced `new FileInfo(path).Extension.ToUpperInvariant()` with static string operations like `Path.GetExtension(path)` and `path.EndsWith(..., StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` in `Mp3PropertyGetter.cs` and `PdfPropertyGetter.cs`.
🎯 Why: Creating `FileInfo` instances in a hot loop (like scanning every file in a directory) causes unnecessary heap allocations and triggers expensive file system validation/normalization under the hood. Using static string parsing avoids this entirely.
📊 Impact: Reduces memory allocations per file scanned and improves CPU efficiency when iterating through large directories. Local benchmark shows ~85% reduction in execution time for this specific path check.
🔬 Measurement: Run a large directory scan using the app and observe reduced memory churn/faster directory traversal in a profiler. Added a learning entry to `.jules/bolt.md`.

### [`v0.132.0`](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.132.0): 0.132.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.131.0...rust-v0.132.0)

#### New Features

- The Python SDK now supports first-class authentication, including API key login, ChatGPT browser and device-code flows, account inspection, and logout APIs. ([#​23093](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23093))
- Python turn APIs are easier to use for text-only workflows: you can pass a plain string as input, and handle-based runs now return a richer `TurnResult` with collected items, timing, and usage data. ([#​23151](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23151), [#​23162](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23162))
- `codex exec resume` now accepts `--output-schema`, so resumed automations can keep session context while still enforcing structured JSON output. ([#​23123](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23123))
- TUI startup is faster because terminal capability probes are now batched instead of waiting on several serial checks before the first interactive frame. ([#​23175](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23175))
- Remote executor registration can now use standard Codex auth instead of a separate registry credential flow. ([#​22769](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/22769))
- App-server turns can preserve requested image fidelity, including original-resolution local images, across user inputs and image-producing tools. ([#​20693](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/20693))

#### Bug Fixes

- Goal continuations now stop when they hit usage limits or a repeated blocker instead of looping and burning more tokens, and completion responses phrase usage more naturally. ([#​23094](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23094), [#​22907](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/22907))
- The session picker is easier to trust: renamed threads now show `name (thread-id)` in resume hints, and pasted text works in the picker search box. ([#​23234](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23234), [#​23338](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23338))
- Multi-session TUI flows are more reliable: in-progress MCP calls stay marked as active during replay, and elicitation replies are sent back to the thread that requested them. ([#​23236](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23236), [#​23241](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23241))
- Remote sessions now keep websocket connections alive and show repo-relative diff paths again instead of `/tmp/...`-prefixed paths. ([#​23226](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23226), [#​23261](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23261))
- Windows installs are more robust: `codex doctor` now detects npm-managed installs correctly, and MSVC release binaries no longer depend on separately installed VC++ runtime DLLs. ([#​22967](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/22967), [#​22905](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/22905))
- TUI polish fixes include immediate shutdown feedback on exit, hiding the ChatGPT usage link for non-OpenAI providers, and keeping a cleared Fast tier from reappearing after side-thread resume. ([#​23323](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23323), [#​23127](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23127), [#​23121](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23121))

#### Documentation

- The Python SDK docs, FAQ, and examples were refreshed around the new auth flow and turn APIs, with clearer setup guidance and simpler text-only examples. ([#​22941](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/22941), [#​23093](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23093), [#​23151](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23151), [#​23162](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23162))

#### Chores

- Memory summaries are now versioned and rebuilt when the stored format is stale, which should keep long-lived memory context leaner and more predictable. ([#​23148](https://redirect.github.com/openai/codex/issues/23148))

author: metalboyrick
body:
## What

Adds a Claude Code / Cursor / etc. agent-skill that tells coding agents how to integrate `@q3labs/pact-sdk@0.1.0` into a user's project.

**New file:** [`packages/sdk/skills/pact-sdk/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/pactnetwork/pact-monitor/blob/docs/sdk-integration-skill/packages/sdk/skills/pact-sdk/SKILL.md)

The skill is a library-integration skill (modifies the user's source code to add the SDK), structurally modelled on the existing tool-wrap skill [`packages/cli/skills/pact-pay/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/pactnetwork/pact-monitor/blob/main/packages/cli/skills/pact-pay/SKILL.md) — same voice, same opinionation, same do-NOT-list discipline.

## Why

The SDK shipped on 2026-05-20 (`sdk-v0.1.0`, PR #212). A coding agent reading the README can install it, but is one step removed from the *integration decision*: which fetch to replace, where to construct the instance, whether to gate calls on `setup()`, what to do about devnet's missing default program ID, and what *not* to do around the golden-rule fallback. The skill encodes that decision tree so an agent doesn't have to derive it from prose.

## Skill contents

Frontmatter `description` covers the trigger phrases ("integrate Pact", "add agent insurance", "wrap fetch with pact", paid-API agent projects) and the explicit non-uses (don't pass `programId` on mainnet, don't gate on `setup()`, don't wrap unrelated fetches, don't conflate with the Monitor SDK).

Body sections:

1. **Rule** — one load-bearing sentence (`import { createPact }`, replace `fetch` with `pact.fetch`).
2. **Install** — `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`, Node ≥ 18, ESM-only, `@solana/web3.js` pulled in transitively.
3. **Integrate (canonical diff)** — before/after of an agent's fetch call. `createPact` is `async`, construct once, reuse.
4. **Where the signer comes from** — server Keypair, browser wallet adapter, quick prototyping.
5. **One-time on-chain setup** — `pact.setup({ allowanceUsdc: 5 })`, idempotent, install-time only, never per request.
6. **B1 — devnet / localnet** — explicit warning that `programId` is REQUIRED on devnet/localnet, with the historical context from the SDK README's Operator notes.
7. **The golden rule** — `pact.fetch` is fall-through safe; never re-throw on `degraded`, never gate the call on coverage. Listen to the event out-of-band.
8. **What this skill is NOT for** — free APIs / localhost / Pact CLI invocations / Monitor SDK / already-proxied fetches.
9. **Verification** — one-line `node --input-type=module` check.
10. **Links** — npm, GitHub release, SDK README, landing-page Agent SDK overview.

## Also in this PR

- `packages/sdk/README.md` — adds a short "For coding agents" pointer just before the "Build & test" section.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry under `[Unreleased]` noting the new skill file.

## Companion PR

Landing-page cross-reference: [metalboyrick/pact-network-landing#27](https://github.com/metalboyrick/pact-network-landing/pull/27) (existing agent-SDK launch PR, updated in the same branch — adds a Starlight `<Aside type="tip">` on `/docs/agent-sdk/overview/` pointing readers at the skill).

## Scope

Docs-only. No code changes, no schema changes, no protocol changes. No tests added (the skill file is text). CI should pass.

author: etimotheo1
body:
## Summary
Two budget-composer fixes from the same review session:

### 1. Keep salaries + guard out of the Utilities budget
Household-staff salaries (helper / gardener / driver, category `salary`) and the guard (category `security`) are people costs that belong to **Payroll**, not Utilities. Added a shared `isUtilityBill()` predicate (`src/lib/pantry.ts`) and applied it to:
- the **Utility cap composer** recurring-bills list + cap math, and
- the **Finances** utilities roll-up (previously only excluded `salary`).

So only real recurring bills (power, water, internet, TV, gas, rent) feed the Utilities budget.

### 2. Clean, editable cadence math with per-line commentary
Lines converted `/day` and `/week` to monthly using calendar-exact averages (`×30.44`, `×4.348`), producing opaque figures — e.g. **100,000/wk showed as 434,821/mo**. Now:
- Clean "times per month" counts: **day 25, week 4, month ×1, year ÷12**, plus two new cadences **2×/week (8)** and **2×/month (2)**.
- Each line shows the **derivation inline** — e.g. `100,000 × 4 = 400,000/mo`.
- The times-per-month count is an **editable input per line**, so a parent can set `/day × 25`, `26` or `30` themselves (default 25).
- Applies to **every module composer** (shared `LineEditor`), including the utility Luku top-ups.

`BudgetLine` gains an optional `periodsPerMonth` override; `toMonthlyCents` = `(unit price × qty) × times-per-month`.

## Notes
- Existing saved caps recompute to the new (cleaner) numbers when a composer is next saved.
- Salary/guard rows still exist in the utilities management list; they're just excluded from the **budget**.

## Test plan
- [ ] Utility cap composer: helper/gardener/driver salaries + Public Security no longer appear in recurring bills; cap drops accordingly.
- [ ] Finances utilities card excludes the same.
- [ ] A `/wk` line of 100,000 now reads `× 4 = 400,000/mo` (not 434,821).
- [ ] Switching a line to 2×/wk → `× 8`; 2×/mo → `× 2`; editing the count updates the monthly live.
- [ ] `/day` defaults to ×25 and can be edited to 26/30 inline.
- [ ] Drivers qty lines (`2 × 75,000/wk`) still compute correctly with the new commentary.

author: benpayne
body:
## Summary

PR #2 shipped `config/wc2026_teams.csv` as a "best-guess" UEFA-16 (and other slots) compiled from traditional footballing powerhouses rather than verified qualification results. That's how Italy ended up in the published rankings despite their elimination by Bosnia & Herzegovina in the European playoff final on penalties — their third consecutive World Cup miss. Same root cause put Denmark, Hungary, Serbia, Ukraine, Venezuela, Costa Rica, Jamaica, Honduras, Nigeria, and Cameroon on the list, while missing Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sweden, Czechia, Cape Verde, Curaçao, Haiti, Iraq, and DR Congo.

This is a **data bug I introduced**, not a model bug.

## What changed

Replaced the file with the verified 48 nations, sourced from FIFA's and Wikipedia's coverage of the completed 2026 qualification cycle (May 2026):

| Slot | Teams |
|---|---|
| Hosts (3) | USA, Canada, Mexico |
| UEFA (16) | Spain, France, England, Portugal, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, Croatia, Switzerland, Austria, Turkey, Scotland, Norway, **Bosnia and Herzegovina**, **Sweden**, **Czechia** |
| CONMEBOL (6) | Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay |
| CONCACAF (3 direct) | Panama, **Curaçao**, **Haiti** |
| CAF (9) | Morocco, Senegal, Egypt, Algeria, Tunisia, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, South Africa, **Cabo Verde** |
| AFC (8) | Japan, Korea Republic, Iran, Australia, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Uzbekistan, Jordan |
| OFC (1) | New Zealand |
| Inter-confederation play-off winners (2) | **Iraq** (beat Bolivia, AFC pathway), **DR Congo** (beat Jamaica, CAF pathway) |

Bold = new vs the previous list.

### Removed (didn't qualify)
Italy, Denmark, Hungary, Serbia, Ukraine, Venezuela, Costa Rica, Jamaica, Honduras, Nigeria, Cameroon.

### New aliases
- `Türkiye` / `Turkiye` → `Turkey`
- `Democratic Republic of the Congo` / `Congo DR` → `DR Congo`
- `Curacao` → `Curaçao`

So a user-supplied qualified-teams CSV using any of these variants still matches the martj42 results.

## Verification

End-to-end against real martj42 data (49,257 matches, cutoff 2026-06-11):

- Exactly 48 teams ranked ✓
- Every team in the CSV matched to a real team in the dataset (no `min_matches` drops) ✓
- Italy, Denmark, Hungary, Serbia, Ukraine, Venezuela, Costa Rica, Jamaica, Honduras, Nigeria, Cameroon — none present in `outputs/full_rankings.csv` ✓
- All 8 new entrants (Bosnia, Sweden, Czechia, Cabo Verde, DR Congo, Curaçao, Haiti, Iraq) appear with real scores ✓

## Summary
Phase 1 of the 3-phase FR-C13 plan (owner-authorized casc-fr#23 R3, 2026-05-20). Delivers the foundation: `PowerDefinition.ScriptFormulas` — the positional slot table the engine resolves through `[SF_N...]` placeholders in localized Description format strings.

body:
## What

Tick-mod 16 sites across 6 final-sweep actors:

- **En_In** (Ingo — Lon Lon Ranch worker) — `blinkTimer`
- **En_Kz** (King Zora) — `blinkTimer`
- **En_Okarina_Effect** (ocarina-note visual effect) — `timer`
- **En_Part** (generic particle effect actor) — `timer` x4 sites
- **En_Takara_Man** (castle-town Treasure Box Shop owner) — `eyeTimer`
- **En_Weiyer** (Stinger water-Tektite variant) — `timer` x8 sites

## Why

At stock 30 fps all of these animate/cycle 1.5× too fast. Ingo's blink rhythm is off, King Zora blinks wrong, ocarina-note visual fades too quickly, particles spawn/despawn faster than intended, treasure-shop owner's eye glance is off, and Stingers (the alternate water Tektite-like enemy) attack/recover faster than intended.

## Pattern

All read via simple `== 0` / `!= 0` gates. Tick-mod via the global `frame_phase` byte (`Pattern E` from `FIX_PATTERNS.md`).

## Verification

- Assembly clean
- All 16 injections verified op=0x0C (JAL)
- 20 fps mode untouched (every hook gates on `fps_switch`)

## Test

### Primary tests

**1. Ingo (En_In) — Child**

🚀 **Instant warp**: `tools/ares-gdb.sh warp 0x157 child` (Lon Lon Ranch).

🐛 **Bug is real**: load `oot-redux-30fps-stock.z64`, Map Select → entry **19** (Lon Lon Ranch), press **B** for Child. From spawn, walk into the corral — Ingo stands near the horse stable. His blink rhythm runs ~1.5× too fast (eyes close-and-open in a noticeably rapid rhythm).

✅ **Fix works**: same steps on `oot-redux-30fps.z64`, blink cadence matches 20 fps. Hold **L+Z** while watching to live-toggle 20↔30 fps and confirm both look identical.

**2. King Zora (En_Kz) — Child**

🐛 **Bug is real**: `oot-redux-30fps-stock.z64`, Map Select → entry **8** (Zora's Domain), press **B** for Child. From spawn, climb the staircase at the back of the room to King Zora on his throne. His blink rhythm runs ~1.5× too fast.

✅ **Fix works**: same on `oot-redux-30fps.z64`, blink matches 20 fps. **L+Z** to A/B.

**3. Ocarina-note effect (En_Okarina_Effect) — any age**

🐛 **Bug is real**: `oot-redux-30fps-stock.z64`, Map Select → entry **1** (Hyrule Field), Child. Pull out the Ocarina (C-button), play any song — watch the rising note-particles spawning from the ocarina. The note-fly-up + fade-out animation runs ~1.5× too fast.

✅ **Fix works**: same on `oot-redux-30fps.z64`, note rise/fade matches 20 fps. **L+Z** during note playback to A/B.

**4. Treasure Box Shop owner (En_Takara_Man) — Adult**

🐛 **Bug is real**: `oot-redux-30fps-stock.z64`, Map Select → entry **64** (Mask Shop / castle-town interior area; if the Treasure Shop scene is on a different entry the tester can take entry **15** Hyrule Castle and run into Hyrule castle-town market), Adult. Walk up to the Treasure Box Shop owner (small man behind counter). His eye-glance animation runs ~1.5× too fast.

✅ **Fix works**: same on `oot-redux-30fps.z64`, eye-glance matches 20 fps. **L+Z** to A/B.

### Also covered by the same tick-mod pattern

- **En_Part** (generic particle actor) — spawns during many dungeon and cutscene effects; e.g. break a pot in entry **2** (Kakariko), Child, to see particle bursts
- **En_Weiyer** (water-Stinger variant) — entry **79** (Water Temple), Adult; the floating water-Tektite enemies in flooded rooms

author: mose09
body:
## 문제

`analyze-legacy --extract-screen-layout` 가 search_panel / data_table_columns 를 LLM 응답에만 의존. 자식 컴포넌트 분할 화면(`index.js` → `<PropsRouter component={Sviddeling}/>` → SearchSection / `<DataGrid columns={COLUMNS}/>` 분할)에서 통째로 빈 배열. `--closure-llm` 켜도 depth 2+ 가 signature 모드라 LLM 한테 JSX skeleton (`<Table columns={...}/>`) 만 도달.

## 수정

1. **`legacy_screen_extractor.extract_screen_layouts()`** — events 와 동일 원칙으로 search_panel / data_table_columns 도 파서 ground truth 로 덮어쓰기.
   - `_build_screen_closure` 가 화면당 closure 한 번만 빌드 → LLM markdown + 파서 fill 양쪽 공유.
   - `_parser_fill_layout` 가 `screen_spec.extractors.extract_form_fields` / `extract_grid_columns` 호출 → ScreenField/TableColumn 변환.
   - 파서 0건이면 LLM 결과 유지 (회귀 회피). tree-sitter 미설치 시 LLM-only 경로 (warn 1회만).
   - 통계 로그: `parser_screens / parser_fields / parser_grids`.
   - 캐시 무효화: `SCREEN_SCHEMA_VERSION v3 → v4`.

2. **`screen_spec.extractors._resolve_array_in_closure`** 신규 — `<DataGrid columns={COLUMNS}/>` 의 COLUMNS 가 별도 파일(`./columns.js`)에 정의된 const 일 때 closure 전체에서 해석. same-file 먼저, 실패 시에만 fallback (회귀 0). `screen-spec` 커맨드도 동일 혜택.

3. **`legacy_react_closure.DEFAULT_DEPTH_MODE`** — depth 2 도 `full` 로 완화 ({0:full, 1:full, 2:full, 3:signature, 4:meta}). `--closure-llm` markdown 품질 보조.

## 검증

테스트 fixture (`hypm_svidModeling/index.js` → Sviddeling → SearchSection/GridSection → columns.js) E2E:

- **before**: search_panel=0, data_table_columns=0
- **after**: search_panel=3 (DatePicker/Select/Input), data_table_columns=5 (LOT/공정/조회일자/수량/비고, hidden 컬럼 hide=True 정확 마킹)

`screen-spec` 커맨드 동일 fixture: form_fields=3, grid_columns=5 — 기존 못 잡던 별도 파일 const 케이스 같이 해결.

body:
🎨 Palette: Keyboard Shortcuts & Focus Management

💡 **What:** 
- Added a `focusHistory` stack to track the previously focused element when navigating into overlays (neighborhood list, collection details).
- Added an `Escape` key handler to dismiss overlays in reverse visual order (`s-nbhd` -> `exploreDetail` -> expanded items).
- Automatically restores focus to the triggering element (e.g., the location button or collection card) when the overlay is closed via `Escape` or the back buttons.

🎯 **Why:** 
Keyboard users were previously trapped in full-screen overlays without a way to dismiss them intuitively (`Escape`), and returning to the previous screen left their focus lost at the top of the document. This resolves a major WCAG violation for focus management.

📸 **Before/After:** 
Before: Pressing Escape did nothing. Dismissing a list via the back button reset focus.
After: Pressing Escape predictably steps backward through the UI hierarchy, and focus reliably returns to the originating button.

♿ **Accessibility:** 
Complies with WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard) by providing predictable escape routes and preserving focus state during view transitions.

body:
## Summary

- `FissionLineageRecord { parent_id, child_id, property_id, template_idx }` emitted by `execute_fission`, accumulated on `BoundaryProtocol` across boundaries.
- `ThresholdBuilder::build_with_lineage` adds one `FusionTrigger` registration per lineage record, watching the child's activating-property Intensity column at `template.fusion_intensity_threshold`, direction = Upward.
- `execute_fusion` applies the scar before tombstoning: parent's activating-property Amount in the shadow is multiplied by `(1 - fusion_scar_coefficient)`. Lookup misses (tombstoned property, missing slot, no Amount sub-field) skip silently.
- Lineage pruned on fusion (`lineage_removed`) and on any allocator tombstone at boundary start, so no `FusionTrigger` ever points at a vanished slot.

**Design call:** lineage lives in `BoundaryProtocol` as an in-memory `Vec`, not in the delta log. This was the simplest path that keeps fusion correctness independent of replay; the replay v2 task in `docs/worklog.md` will close the loop by recording lineage in the log.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — 145/145 passing (was 140), zero warnings.

- [x] `fusion_applies_scar_to_parent_amount_and_tombstones_child` — direct unit: feeds a synthetic `FusionTrigger` event, asserts parent Amount goes 1.0 → 0.95.
- [x] `fusion_lineage_emits_one_intensity_threshold_per_record` — lineage record yields a registration on the child's Intensity (col 2), threshold 0.85, direction Upward.
- [x] `fusion_lineage_skipped_when_child_has_no_slot` — tombstoned child gets no `FusionTrigger` registration.
- [x] `fission_then_fusion_applies_scar_and_tombstones_child` (GPU integration) — drives fission, patches the child's velocity to +0.21, runs ticks until Pass 2 builds Intensity past 0.85, runs boundary, asserts parent scarred + child gone + lineage pruned.

author: mrsimpson
body:
## Summary

- **Fix**: Add `ripgrep` to the homelab Dockerfile's `apk add` command
- **Root Cause**: The glob tool depends on ripgrep (`rg`) for file searching, but the homelab Dockerfile extends from a pre-built opencode base image that may not have ripgrep installed
- **Impact**: Ensures the glob tool always works in Docker containers spawned by the opencode router

## Changes

- Added `ripgrep` to the `apk add` command in `deployment/homelab/images/opencode/Dockerfile`
- Updated the comment block to document ripgrep as a required dependency

## Context

The glob tool (`packages/opencode/src/tool/glob.ts`) uses ripgrep via the Ripgrep service for file finding. The ripgrep service first checks if `rg` is in the system PATH via `which("rg")`, then falls back to downloading from GitHub releases if not found.

While the opencode base Dockerfile (`packages/opencode/Dockerfile`) already installs ripgrep, the homelab Dockerfile extends from a pre-built image (`ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:${BASE_VERSION}`) that may not have ripgrep if it was published before the ripgrep installation was added to the base Dockerfile.

This is a minimal, low-risk fix that adds one dependency to ensure consistent behavior across all image versions.

## Summary

author: jacobqvisth
body:
## Why

`processUnsubscribe` in `src/app/api/tracking/unsubscribe/[trackingId]/route.ts` had **six** writes that silently discarded `.error`:

1. `unsubscribes` upsert
2. `suppressions` insert (the primary workspace-wide compliance gate)
3. `email_events` insert
4. `contacts.status` update
5. `sequence_enrollments` update
6. `email_queue` cancel update

The route wraps `processUnsubscribe` in a try/catch that logs to console.error — but **nothing inside throws**, so any failure rendered "You've been unsubscribed" while the underlying state stayed broken.

Worst case: the `suppressions` insert fails silently. Page shows success. Recipient thinks they're off the list. Future sequence enrollments don't find them in `suppressions` → they keep getting email. Compliance gap that nobody knows about.

## What

Every write now checks `.error` and throws with rich context (`tracking_id`, `email`, plus contact / enrollment counts where relevant). The existing outer try/catch picks up the throw and logs to Vercel logs so on-call sees the failure. The user still sees the 200 success page — that's the RFC 8058 one-click-unsubscribe contract — but we no longer pretend the state is consistent when it isn't.

Two layered compliance gates remain (`suppressions` + `contacts.status='unsubscribed'`), and any failure of either now lights up in logs.

- [x] `eslint src/` clean

author: armanobosyan
body:
## Summary

- Adds Starlette CORS middleware to the HTTP transport so browser-based MCP clients (ChatGPT Connectors UI) can complete the OAuth discovery flow.
- Without CORS, \`OPTIONS /mcp\` preflight hit AuthMiddleware and returned 401 with no \`Access-Control-*\` headers, so the browser blocked every actual request before it left the page. Claude.ai, Codex, stdio Claude Desktop, etc. were unaffected because they call MCP server-to-server (no preflight).
- Default allowlist: chatgpt.com, chat.openai.com, platform.openai.com, claude.ai, claude.com, cursor.sh, app.cursor.sh. Override with new env var \`SUGRA_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS\` (comma-separated, or \`*\` for any).

## Why this fixes ChatGPT

Reproducer (production probe before this PR):
\`\`\`
curl -i -X OPTIONS https://app.sugra.ai/mcp \
  -H 'Origin: https://chatgpt.com' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, content-type, mcp-session-id'
# -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# -> no Access-Control-* headers
# -> www-authenticate present but browser cannot read it without Expose-Headers
\`\`\`

After this PR the preflight returns 200 with the right allow-headers, allow-methods, and expose-headers (including \`WWW-Authenticate\` so the browser-side JS can pick up the OAuth metadata URL from a 401).

## Middleware order

Starlette applies \`add_middleware\` calls in reverse order. \`AuthMiddleware\` is added first (innermost), \`CORSMiddleware\` second (outermost) - that puts CORS in front of auth, so preflight responses do not require a Bearer token.

## Tests

\`tests/test_cors.py\` covers:
- preflight allows each of chatgpt.com / chat.openai.com / claude.ai / cursor.sh
- preflight blocks unknown origins (no Allow-Origin echoed back)
- preflight does not return 401 from the auth layer
- 401 responses still include the \`WWW-Authenticate\` header and expose it through CORS along with \`Mcp-Session-Id\` and \`MCP-Protocol-Version\`
- POST without Origin (server-to-server clients) is unaffected
- \`load_allowed_origins\` default / env-override / wildcard / empty-string-fallback

Full suite: 63 passed (12 new + 51 existing).

## Deploy

GH Actions \`Deploy MCP to APP VM\` runs on push to main, executes \`sudo /usr/local/bin/sugra-mcp-deploy\` which pulls main + reinstalls the package + restarts the systemd unit. After merge verify with:
\`\`\`
curl -i -X OPTIONS https://app.sugra.ai/mcp \
  -H 'Origin: https://chatgpt.com' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, content-type'
# -> 200 + Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://chatgpt.com
\`\`\`

## Companion PRs

- prod-sugra-ai-APP: adds RFC 9728 path-suffix discovery \`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp\` (separate PR, opens next).
- sugra-internal-docs: ENV_REFERENCE adds \`SUGRA_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS\`, INFRASTRUCTURE documents the CORS layer (separate PR).

## Test plan

- [x] \`pytest\` 63/63 pass locally (Python 3.14)
- [x] \`ruff check\` clean
- [x] Tools registered smoke check passes (5 tools)
- [ ] CI green on Python 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14
- [ ] Codex code review round
- [ ] Post-deploy curl verification on app.sugra.ai/mcp
- [ ] Arman adds MCP server in ChatGPT Settings -> Connectors successfully

```
        Trello API secret (also TRELLO_API_SECRET; never printed in --help)
  -trello-api-token string
        Trello API token, used by the Go SDK to talk to api.trello.com (also TRELLO_API_TOKEN; never printed in --help)
```

## Why this happened

Go's `flag` package renders the **current value of the variable backing each flag** as the `(default ...)` hint in `-h` output. `LoadConfig` was seeding the three secret-bearing fields from `os.Getenv` **before** passing them to `fs.StringVar`, so the env-derived value became the visible "default" in the rendered usage.

This is a classic Go config-loader footgun. Any of:

- shoulder-surfing
- screen-sharing
- screenshot pasted into an issue / Slack / Stack Overflow
- shell history file
- terminal-recording tool

…now has a complete Trello API credential.

## Fix (3 small commits in 1)

### `internal/app/config.go`

- Register the three secret flags with an empty default (`""`) so the flag package's auto-generated usage can never echo any env value.
- Add `overlaySecretFromEnv` helper that runs **after** `flag.Parse`: if the operator did not supply the corresponding `--flag` on the command line (`fs.Visit` reports it as unset), fall back to the matching env var.
- Update the flag usage strings to advertise the matching env var name so an operator reading `-h` still knows the env var exists as an alternative input.
- Split `LoadConfig` into a thin wrapper plus a package-private `loadConfigWithOutput(args, w io.Writer)` so the test below can capture the flag-package's help output without touching `os.Stderr`.

**Precedence is unchanged** (`CLI > env > required-no-default`); only the *mechanism* by which an env-derived value reaches the variable is reordered so the flag default never sees it.

### `internal/app/config_test.go` (3 new tests)

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `TestHelpDoesNotLeakSecretsFromEnv` | Sets the three `TRELLO_*` env vars to obvious leak markers (`"DO-NOT-LEAK-secret-..."`), runs `--help` through the new helper, asserts none of the marker strings appear anywhere in the rendered usage. **Reproduces the exact bug pattern from the operator report.** |
| `TestHelpAdvertisesEnvOverridesForSecrets` | Guards the usage-text affordance: the new help output must still mention each env var name so operators reading `-h` know the alternative inputs. |
| `TestEnvOverlayHonoursCLIPrecedence` | Locks in `CLI > env > default` precedence for the secret flags after the refactor; without this, the post-Parse overlay could accidentally clobber a CLI-supplied value with an env value. |

## Behaviour matrix

| Operator pattern | Resolved config | `-h` output |
|---|---|---|
| Env vars only | Unchanged | No longer shows `(default "<secret>")` |
| CLI flags only | Unchanged | Unchanged (flag value still wins, no env in the picture) |
| Mixed CLI + env | Unchanged (CLI wins per pre-existing contract) | No longer shows `(default ...)` for the three secret flags |

Zero functional change for any operator. Pure leak-prevention.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` — all packages pass, including the three new config tests.
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- `go build ./...` — clean.
- `golangci-lint run --timeout=5m` — 0 issues.
- **Manual reproduction**: with `TRELLO_API_SECRET=MUST-NOT-LEAK-1234567890` (etc.) set, `go run . -h` shows zero occurrences of any `MUST-NOT-LEAK-*` marker string in the help output. Before this PR, those values were front-and-centre.

## Out of scope

- The startup-time `event=gateway_starting` audit line already redacts these three fields via `Config.Redacted()` and was unaffected by this bug.
- The `--callback-url`, `--router-dir`, `--kanban-board-id` etc. flags continue to render env-derived values as `(default ...)` because those values are not secrets. If a future audit decides they should also be hidden, the same `overlaySecretFromEnv` mechanism extends trivially.
- This PR does not introduce the `internal/app/sysevent` callback abstraction tracked in #37; that's still the right longer-term home for "everywhere a secret could leak". This is the surgical fix for the one channel that was leaking today.

body:
## Phase 5 of the dashboard mockup integration

The biggest remaining chunk. Adds a real notification feed and message thread to every user, wires them into the topbar bell and the dashboard cards, and finishes the \`/benefits\` page with a working refer-a-friend.

## What ships

### Database (Drizzle migration 0005)
- \`notifications\` — id, user_id, kind, title, body, href, read_at, created_at, indexed on (user_id, created_at). Append-only.
- \`messages\` — id, user_id, from_team, author_name, body, read_at, created_at. Single thread per user (v1).

### Notification triggers
| Trigger | Kind |
|---|---|
| First sign-in (via \`/auth/callback\` \`onSuccess\`) | \`welcome\` |
| Stripe webhook fires \`subscription.created\`/\`updated\` and status transitions into \`active\` or \`trialing\` | \`subscription_active\` |
| \`/api/provision\` SSE done event | \`birdeye_provisioned\` |

Welcome path also seeds a Growth Hub Team message so the inbox isn't empty for new users.

### API
| Route | Method | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| \`/api/notifications\` | GET | last 20 |
| \`/api/notifications/unread-count\` | GET | Returns 0 for unauthed (no 401 — bell poller stays silent) |
| \`/api/notifications/[id]/read\` | POST | idempotent |
| \`/api/notifications/mark-all-read\` | POST | returns flipped count |
| \`/api/messages\` | GET / POST | GET full thread (oldest first); POST appends a customer reply, 4000 char cap |

### UI
- **Topbar**: new \`useUnreadCount()\` client hook polls every 60s + on window focus. Static gh-dot replaced with conditional render. Initial count comes from a server-side fetch in \`(app)/layout.tsx\` so the first paint matches reality. Bell now links to \`/dashboard\`.
- **\`/dashboard\`**: Notifications card renders real rows from Neon with kind-based tone/icon and friendly relative timestamps ("Just now", "5m ago", "3d ago"). Each linked notification wraps a Link. Messages preview reads the latest team message; empty state when the thread is empty.
- **\`/messages\`**: real two-pane inbox. Auto-marks the thread read on open. Distinct bubble layout for team (cream, left) vs user (lime, right). Date dividers between days. Composer is a client component with optimistic send + \`router.refresh()\`.
- **\`/benefits\`**: refer-a-friend hero shows the user's real \`referCode\` and a Copy-link button (\`ReferralCopyButton\` — clipboard API with 2-second "Copied ✓" feedback). Email-a-friend mailto pre-fills the invite link. 6 benefit cards matching the mockup.

### Auth callback enhancement
- \`ensureUserRecord\` now exposes \`ensureUserRecordWithStatus\` which reports \`created: boolean\`. Used by the callback to seed welcome content exactly once per user (no double-welcomes on subsequent sign-ins).

### Smoke tests
- \`/messages\`, \`/benefits\` — auth redirect
- \`/api/notifications\`, \`/api/messages\` — 401 unauth
- \`/api/notifications/unread-count\` — 200 with \`count:0\` unauth (no 401)

## Reviewer notes

- The Stripe webhook handler now reads the existing subscription row before the UPDATE so it can detect the \`active\` transition. Idempotent: stays a no-op if the prior status was already \`active\`/\`trialing\`.
- Provisioning notifications use the \`onboardingId\` (which IS the user id — set in the wizard layout). Failure to notify never breaks the SSE done event.
- The unread-count endpoint is **deliberately not auth-gated** with a 401 — it polls in the background from every authed page and silent failures are nicer than console errors when the session expires.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` clean
- [x] Drizzle migration 0005 applied to Neon
- [ ] Vercel preview build green
- [ ] Smoke tests pass on preview
- [ ] Manual: sign up a fresh account → \`/dashboard\` shows 1 welcome notification, Messages preview shows the welcome thread
- [ ] Manual: \`/messages\` → thread displays, send a reply → it appears in the right-aligned lime bubble
- [ ] Manual: \`/benefits\` → "Copy invite link" copies the right URL; "Email a friend" opens a pre-filled mailto
- [ ] Manual: complete a Stripe checkout → a \`subscription_active\` notification appears (will need a real test customer in Stripe live mode)
