body:
## Summary

A UI audit found that `marketplace`, `inbox`, and `analytics` hand-rolled their own fetch logic, loading flags, retry, and empty/error rendering with raw `className="empty-state"` divs — diverging from the shared `useBridgeFetch` hook and `EmptyState`/`ErrorState`/`SkeletonList` components used by every other data page. This consolidates them.

- **inbox** — migrated the list fetch to `useBridgeFetch` (polling, retry/backoff, and abort-on-unmount now handled by the hook; the prior tab-hidden polling pause is preserved via the hook's `enabled` option). The loading state moves from a custom `Spinner` div to the shared `SkeletonList`. Error rendering follows the two-tier pattern: `<ErrorState>` for empty-on-error, an inline `alert-err` banner for stale-data-with-refresh-error. Detail-fetch errors now surface via `<ErrorState>` in the reader pane. The `seenNames` first-load seeding and detail-auto-refresh-on-upstream-change side effects are preserved.
- **marketplace** — replaced the hand-rolled "No results found" `empty-state` div with `<EmptyState>`. The data fetch keeps its bespoke multi-hop fallback chain (bridge → raw GitHub → built-in fallback); `useBridgeFetch` models a single endpoint and cannot express that chain, so it was intentionally left in place. Its `loadErr` banner is already a proper `alert-err` two-tier banner.
- **analytics** — replaced the hand-rolled "No tool call data" `empty-state` div with `<EmptyState>`. This page already used `useBridgeFetch` + `<ErrorState>` + the two-tier error pattern.

Behavior is otherwise unchanged — this is a consolidation, not a redesign. No change to what data is shown.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean across the dashboard
- [x] `npm run lint` — no new warnings introduced (one pre-existing unused-`RecipeIcon` warning in inbox left untouched as out-of-scope)
- [x] Verified all three pages render correctly in the browser against a worktree dev server with a live bridge: inbox list populates (64 items) and auto-selects the first message with its detail body; marketplace grid renders; analytics stat cards + area chart + tables render
- [ ] Verify inbox empty state (`No items yet`) and error state (`ErrorState` with Retry) when the inbox is empty / the bridge is down
- [ ] Verify marketplace `EmptyState` via a no-match search query

author: dvoros-castai
body:
Removing the `CustomizeDiff` function from the cluster resources. This was introduced in [2.0.6](https://github.com/castai/terraform-provider-castai/releases/tag/v2.0.6) as a migration step for old clusters not yet having a `cluster_token`. The reson for removal is that this diff is leading to unexpected behaviour when the state is lost and rebuilt (experinced in the `castai` Crossplane provider that is built from this TF provider).

It should be safe to remove as `2.0.6` was released 3+ years ago. For those running earlier versions, it's expected they'll migrate major versions one by one and then any version after 2.0.6 will take care of the migration. For already migrated clusters, this removal should have no affect.

Also fixing AKS tests that failed due to deletion taking too long. This is expected for these clusters that spend most of their time disconnected. When we're running init data collection after reconnecting them, the delete can take longer because of that.

## Proof of Work

Verified that this will have no effect on clusters onboarded after 2.0.6 by:

1. Onboarding an EKS cluster without this fix
2. Verified that provider with this fix included produces no diff on planning

Verified that this version will work as expested with new clusters by onboarding an EKS cluster with the fix in place.

---
### Kimchi Summary
### What changed
Removed the legacy `clusterTokenDiff` custom diff logic from all CAST AI cluster resources. The provider will no longer force recreation of a cluster resource when the `token` field is empty. Also added `.terraformrc` to `.gitignore` in the examples directory.

### Why
The `clusterTokenDiff` function was a temporary migration helper for state files created before the `token` field was added to cluster resources. That migration path is now obsolete.

### Key changes
- `castai/cluster.go`: Deleted the `clusterTokenDiff` function and removed the unused `github.com/google/uuid` import.
- `castai/resource_aks_cluster.go`: Removed `CustomizeDiff: clusterTokenDiff` from the AKS cluster schema.
- `castai/resource_eks_cluster.go`: Removed `CustomizeDiff: clusterTokenDiff` from the EKS cluster schema.
- `castai/resource_gke_cluster.go`: Removed `CustomizeDiff: clusterTokenDiff` from the GKE cluster schema.
- `castai/resource_gke_cluster_id.go`: Removed `CustomizeDiff: clusterTokenDiff` from the GKE cluster ID schema.
- `.gitignore`: Added `examples/**/.terraformrc` to ignore Terraform CLI configuration files in examples.

### Impact
Clusters with an empty `token` in state will no longer be forced to recreate. Verify that existing state files no longer rely on this legacy behavior before upgrading.

---
### Kimchi Summary
### What changed
Remove the legacy `clusterTokenDiff` custom diff logic from AKS, EKS, GKE, and GKE cluster ID resources so that an empty `token` no longer forces cluster recreation. Also updates `.gitignore` for example Terraform CLI config files and adds explicit delete timeouts to AKS test fixtures.

### Why
The `clusterTokenDiff` function was a migration helper for states created before the cluster `token` field existed. That migration is complete, making the forced-recreation behavior obsolete.

### Key changes
- `castai/cluster.go`: Deleted `clusterTokenDiff` and removed the unused `uuid` import.
- `castai/resource_aks_cluster.go`, `castai/resource_eks_cluster.go`, `castai/resource_gke_cluster.go`, `castai/resource_gke_cluster_id.go`: Removed `CustomizeDiff: clusterTokenDiff` from schema definitions.
- `castai/resource_aks_cluster_test.go`: Added `timeouts { delete = "30m" }` to AKS test configurations.
- `.gitignore`: Added `examples/**/.terraformrc`.

### Impact
Empty `token` values will no longer trigger a forced replacement of the cluster resource. This is a behavioral change for any remaining legacy states that still lack a token, which must now be handled explicitly by the operator.

---
### Kimchi Summary
### What changed
Remove the legacy `clusterTokenDiff` custom diff logic from AKS, EKS, GKE, and GKE ID cluster resources to stop forcing recreation when the cluster `token` field is empty. Also adds `.terraformrc` to `.gitignore` and explicit delete timeouts to AKS cluster test fixtures.

### Why
The `clusterTokenDiff` function was originally added as a temporary migration aid when the cluster token field was introduced. That migration period has passed, so the workaround is now obsolete and risks unnecessarily destroying and recreating existing cluster resources.

### Key changes
- `castai/cluster.go`: Removed the `clusterTokenDiff` function and the `github.com/google/uuid` import.
- `castai/resource_aks_cluster.go`, `castai/resource_eks_cluster.go`, `castai/resource_gke_cluster.go`, `castai/resource_gke_cluster_id.go`: Removed `CustomizeDiff: clusterTokenDiff` from each resource schema.
- `.gitignore`: Added `examples/**/.terraformrc`.
- `castai/resource_aks_cluster_test.go`: Added `timeouts { delete = "30m" }` to AKS test configurations.

### Impact
Existing clusters with an empty or unset `token` value will no longer be planned for replacement on apply. Review any existing state for token drift before upgrading, and run a state refresh if needed to populate the field.

body:
**Symptom**: after refresh, the side panel \"request just doesn't go\".

**Cause**: PR #34 ran a blocking \`window.prompt()\` inside \`send()\` the first time a repo was unknown for the current PR. In the side panel context this either (a) didn't render reliably, or (b) was dismissed by the user, which then errored out the send entirely.

## Fix

- Move the path UX out of the send path. A new banner under the header shows:
  - \`📁 /path/to/repo\` + a \`change\` button when a path is recorded
  - \`⚠︎ No local repo path set — Claude can't read your files\` + a \`set path\` button when none is recorded
- The banner refreshes on init, on PR navigation, and after every successful save. Clicking either button opens the \`prompt()\` from a *user click*, which is the safe place for it.
- \`send()\` no longer checks the path. If none is set the message goes to \`host.js\` without \`cwd\` and Claude spawns in the default working directory (answers fine — only file-read tools have no context).

author: kespineira
body:
Fixes #2155

<!-- Add issue number above -->

#### Describe the changes you have made in this PR -

`opensre agents scan` (strict mode) was missing Claude Code CLI sessions whose process command is plain `claude`, `claude --resume <id>`, or `claude --prefill …`, and `opensre agents scan --all` (loose mode) was mislabeling Claude Desktop and Electron helper processes as `claude-code-*`.

This PR teaches the classifier to recognise the full set of Claude Code CLI shapes — bare `claude`, `--resume` / `-r`, `--prefill`, `--print` / `-p`, `--continue` / `-c`, equals-form variants (`--resume=<id>`, …), plus the existing `claude code` and `stream-json` paths — and adds a cross-platform Claude Desktop negative filter that runs against `argv[0]` only (macOS `.app` bundles + helper binaries, Linux Snap / `/usr/lib/claude-desktop` / AppImage, Windows `Program Files\Claude\` and `AppData\Local\Programs\Claude\`). The filter applies in both strict and `--all` modes, so the desktop main process is never mislabeled, even in loose discovery.

The legacy `discover_agents` path (used by Cursor terminal metadata + `registered_and_discovered_agents`) and the modern `discover_agent_processes` now share a single `_claude_code_cli_matches_cmdline` helper, so both surfaces agree on classification. The noise filter haystack is restricted to `process_name + argv[0]` so prompt-bearing flags such as `claude --print "...helper..."` are no longer dropped because the prompt content contains a noise token.

Docs: new "Discovering local agent sessions" section in `docs/agents.mdx` describing the strict mode, `--all` loose mode, `--register`, and the cross-platform desktop filter.

### Demo/Screenshot for feature changes and bug fixes -

![opensre agents scan — issue #2155 demo](https://vhs.charm.sh/vhs-hUnmskJNdqELdwOAHh2k0.gif)

The demo spawns three fake Claude Code CLI processes via `exec -a` (`claude`, `claude --resume demo-1`, `claude --prefill fix-auth-bug`) and one fake Claude Desktop main process (`/Applications/Claude.app/Contents/MacOS/Claude`). The strict `opensre agents scan` surfaces the three CLI rows; the desktop PID is filtered out. `opensre agents scan --all` still does not mislabel the desktop. The trailing assertion confirms the desktop PID is absent from both outputs. (Extra `claude-code-*` rows in the table belong to other Claude Code sessions running on the recording machine and are themselves a demonstration of the fix surfacing real bare-`claude` invocations.)

---

## Code Understanding and AI Usage

**Did you use AI assistance (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) to write any part of this code?**
- [ ] No, I wrote all the code myself
- [x] Yes, I used AI assistance (continue below)

**If you used AI assistance:**
- [x] I have reviewed every single line of the AI-generated code
- [x] I can explain the purpose and logic of each function/component I added
- [x] I have tested edge cases and understand how the code handles them
- [x] I have modified the AI output to follow this project's coding standards and conventions

**Explain your implementation approach:**

- The bug has two parts: (a) the strict classifier in `_classify_agent` required `code` in argv or `stream-json` formatting flags, missing bare `claude` and its `--resume` / `--prefill` / `--print` / `--continue` variants; (b) the loose classifier matched any `claude` token anywhere in the haystack, mislabeling Claude Desktop + Electron helper processes as `claude-code` in `--all` mode.
- Considered three approaches for the desktop filter: (i) macOS-only `/Applications/Claude.app` exclusion; (ii) negative argv-shape heuristics only (e.g. helper noise tokens); (iii) cross-platform path hints matched against `argv[0]`. Went with (iii) because the issue explicitly asks for a cross-platform signal and lists platform-specific paths as secondary negative filters rather than primary positives.
- Key helpers introduced:
  - `_claude_code_cli_matches_cmdline(cmdline)` — single source of truth for "is this a Claude Code CLI invocation". Used by both the modern (`_classify_agent`) and legacy (`_agent_name_for_command`) paths so they cannot diverge again.
  - `_is_claude_desktop_artifact(cmdline)` — matches desktop bundle / installer hints against `argv[0]` only. Matching against `argv[0]` (and not the full command) prevents prompt content like `claude --print "inspect /Applications/Claude.app/..."` from being misclassified as a desktop process.
  - `_option_name(arg)` — normalises `--flag=value` to `--flag` so equals-form options participate in the allowlist check.
- The noise filter (`_is_noise_process`) used to scan the full argv for tokens like `helper` / `shipit` / `pty-host`, which would falsely drop `claude --print "...helper..."`. Restricted the haystack to `process_name + argv[0]` to keep desktop / Electron helpers filtered while letting CLI prompt content through.
- Tests cover every new shape (bare / long flags / short flags / equals form), cross-platform desktop rejection (macOS .app bundle + Linux Snap / `/usr/lib/claude-desktop` / AppImage + Windows quoted paths), opt-prefix CLI pass-through (`/opt/Claude/claude` and `/opt/claude-cli/bin/claude` are accepted), the prompt-content false-negative regression, and legacy-path parity via Cursor terminal metadata.
- Pre-merge gates: `make lint`, `make format-check`, `make typecheck` clean; `tests/agents/` + `tests/cli/` (1905 tests) green.

---

author: lehni
body:
fontkit's GSUB Type 3 (Alternate Substitution) hardcodes the alternate index to 0, so user-supplied alternateNumber values (e.g. `font.layout(text, { aalt: 2 })`) are silently ignored and every aalt/nalt/etc. request resolves to the first alternate. This makes Type 3 features effectively read-only from a caller's perspective.

This PR:

- Threads the user's original features object through `ShapingPlan` so processors can read per-feature integer values without losing them to the shaper plan's `true`/`false` normalisation.
- Updates `OTLayoutEngine.setup` to overlay the user's original values onto the chosen-features map without mutating the caller's input object.
- `GSUBProcessor` Type 3 now reads `userFeatures[currentFeature]` as a 1-based alternate index, falls back to the first alternate when no value is given or the requested index is out of range.

Test: FiraSans's aalt lookup carries multiple alternates per coverage entry. For 'A' (glyph 3) the alternate set is `[1078 'ordfeminine', 764 'a.sc']`. The added test shapes 'A' with `{ aalt: true }` and `{ aalt: 2 }` and asserts the correct glyph ID for each — matching what HarfBuzz produces for `--features='aalt=1'` vs `--features='aalt=2'`.

author: alretum
body:
Fixes COD-38

## Problem

In the admin detail views for **Schulbegleiter** and **Kinder**, editing one field silently reset every *other* field — boolean flags flipped back to `false`, a Schulbegleiter's entire workshop-attendance list was deleted, and a Kind's Kostenträger was cleared.

### Root cause

The update schemas were built with `.partial()` over field objects that carry `.default()`:

```ts
const profileFieldsSchema = z.object({
  leosOne: z.boolean().default(false),
  workshops: z.array(...).default([]),
  // ...
});
export const UpdateSchulbegleiterSchema =
  z.object({ name: ... }).merge(profileFieldsSchema.partial());
```

**Zod keeps `.default()` alive through `.partial()`.** So `UpdateSchulbegleiterSchema.parse({ name: "X" })` returned `{ name: "X", leosOne: false, outlook: false, zvNeuNachBescheid: false, workshops: [] }`. The facade's `if (parsed.leosOne !== undefined)` guards — meant to skip untouched fields — saw `false` / `[]` instead of `undefined`, so they wrote those values over the stored data. An empty `workshops: []` made `updateProfilePartial` `deleteMany` every `WorkshopAttendance` row for the profile.

A trailing `.transform()` on the Kind `kostentraegerId` (placed *after* `.optional()`) leaked the same way: it ran on the `undefined` of an absent field and coerced it to `null`, clearing the Kostenträger on every edit.

Workshops happened to be unaffected — `WorkshopSchema` has no `.default()` fields — but the detail view is reworked alongside the others for a consistent flow.

## Fix

**Schemas** — `.default()` / `.transform()` moved to create-only schema variants. `UpdateSchulbegleiterSchema` / `UpdateChildSchema` now derive from defaults-free field objects, so an untouched field parses to `undefined` and the existing facade guards skip it. Facades unchanged.

**UX** — replaced the invisible 600 ms debounced autosave with explicit saving:

- Detail panels are **editable immediately** — no edit-mode toggle.
- **Nothing persists until an explicit save** — a **Speichern** button (enabled once something changes) or **Enter**.
- Closing with unsaved changes opens a dialog: **Speichern / Verwerfen / Abbrechen**.
- Save sends only the changed fields.
- The row-action menu entry is relabelled **"Details bearbeiten"** (was "Details öffnen").

Applies to all three detail views (Schulbegleiter, Kinder, Workshops).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` — clean.
- Parsed single-field partial updates against the real schemas: `parse({ name })` → `{ name }` for Schulbegleiter and Workshop, `parse({ firstName })` → `{ firstName }` for Kind — no leaked defaults.
- Ran against a seeded dev DB: editing one field calls the update action with a minimal patch (e.g. `updateChildAction(id, { firstName })`); the other fields are preserved.

author: exafyltd
body:
## Why

German users still see English month names + US date layout ('May 20, 2026' instead of '20. Mai 2026') even when their UI is fully translated. Root cause: 415 call sites across the codebase hardcode \`'en-US'\` / omit the locale arg / use date-fns \`format()\` without a \`locale\` option.

This was the **second largest** surface in the deep i18n leak audit (after register fixes in PR #486).

## What

### Runtime helpers — \`src/lib/locale-format.ts\`
- \`fmtDate(d, opts?)\` / \`fmtTime\` / \`fmtDateTime\` — replacements for \`Date.toLocaleX()\` that read the user locale from the i18n-toast singleton.
- \`fmtNumber(n, opts?)\` — same for \`Number.toLocaleString()\` (null-safe).
- date-fns re-exports: \`formatDate\` (alias for \`format\`), \`formatDistance\`, \`formatDistanceToNow\`, \`formatRelative\` — each pre-injects the matching date-fns locale.

### ESLint rule — \`eslint-rules/no-raw-locale-call.js\`
- Flags \`toLocaleDateString\` / \`toLocaleTimeString\` / \`toLocaleString\` with no arg or \`'en-...'\` literal.
- Flags date-fns \`format/formatDistance/formatDistanceToNow/formatRelative\` calls with no \`locale\` option.
- ERROR level — prevents regressions.

### Codemod — \`scripts/codemod-locale-calls.mjs\`
One-shot sweep. Results:

| Pattern                              | Replacements |
|---|---|
| \`toLocaleDateString\`                 | 76 |
| \`toLocaleTimeString\`                 | 26 |
| \`toLocaleString\` (date)              | 68 |
| \`toLocaleString\` (number)            | 46 |
| date-fns \`format()\` → \`formatDate\` | 160 |
| date-fns import reroutes              | 122 |
| Hand-fixes (\`getBalance('USD')!.toLocaleString()\`) | 11 |

**Total: 412 sites in 253 files.**

## Verification

- \`npm run build\` — green
- \`npx eslint src/**/*.{ts,tsx}\` — zero \`no-raw-locale-call\` fires
- Sample diff:
  \`\`\`diff
  - return new Date(dateStr).toLocaleDateString("en-US", { year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric" })
  + return fmtDate(new Date(dateStr), { year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric" })
  \`\`\`

## What is NOT changed

- Translation catalogs (separate audit PRs #486/#487/#488).
- Gateway-emitted strings (Phase C — coming next).
- \`useState\` literals (audit overstated this — wallet/payment uses internal IDs, not UI text).

body:
https://ag-grid.atlassian.net/browse/AG-17390

The public option `series[].node.title.formatter` (and analogous `subtitle` / `labels`) is declared in `ag-charts-types` as `RichFormatter<...>` — returning `TextOrSegments | undefined`. The internal `OrganizationSeriesNodeTextProperties` and the `formatText` helper in `organizationSeries.ts` declared the same field as `Formatter<...>`, returning only `TextValue | undefined`.

Runtime already supports `TextOrSegments` (segments are passed through `node.update` and rendered correctly); the internal types were just under-reporting the supported behaviour. Audited every other `RichFormatter` site in `ag-charts-types` (`AgChartLabelOptions`, axis label/caption, navigator label) — they consume via classes that already use `RichFormatter`, so no other drift to fix.

body: ## Summary Wire một Joern call graph vào pipeline để Detector LLM nhận được **inter-procedural context** (ai gọi function này / function này gọi ai). Đây là tiền đề cho RQ4 trong eval — "CPG-aware chunking outperforms line-based on Recall". ### Thay đổi cốt lõi - **`src/coba/agent/callgraph.py`** (new): `CallGraph` in-memory store với path + function-name canonicalisation. Merge Joern overloads (multiple methods cùng tên), strip generic markers (``, parameter types). Tải từ list JSON do Joern script emit. - **`src/coba/tools/joern_queries/call_graph.sc`** (new): Scala script chạy qua `joern --script` để emit `[{file, function, line, callees[], callers[]}]` cho mọi method trong CPG. - **`JoernRunner.extract_call_graph(target)`** (new method): build CPG (cached) → run script → parse. Mọi failure (Joern missing / CPG build fail / non-JSON output) trả về `EMPTY_CALL_GRAPH` — orchestrator không bao giờ crash khi Joern không có. - **`chunk_file(..., call_graph=...)`**: function-level `Chunk` được fill `callers` và `callees` (top 20). Window fallback giữ nguyên. - **`Planner.plan(...) / chunk_files(...)`**: nhận và pass-through call graph. - **`Orchestrator.scan(...)`**: bước 0 mới (trước plan) gọi `_build_call_graph(target)`; timing tách riêng dưới `timings['callgraph']` để eval đo overhead Joern. - **`prompts/detector.j2`**: thêm block "Callers" / "Callees" cho LLM khi populated. ### Tests (11 mới) - `tests/test_callgraph.py`: 5 case — basic load, path/name normalize, merge overloads, bad-JSON tolerance, JSON roundtrip. - `tests/test_chunker_callgraph.py`: 3 case — empty-callgraph passthrough, enrichment integration, Detector prompt rendering "Callers/Callees". 53 → 64 tests pass. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Đọc `src/coba/agent/callgraph.py` § `_norm_fn` — confirm cách strip parameter / qualified name có hợp lý với output thực tế của Joern (vd. `pkg.Class.method(int, long)` → `method`). - [ ] Đọc `src/coba/tools/joern_queries/call_graph.sc` — confirm cú pháp Scala 3 (Joern 4.x). Em chưa chạy trên Joern thật vì sandbox không có Joern binary; logic JSON escape có thể cần test với 1 repo Java/Python thật. - [ ] Confirm thứ tự "callgraph → plan → static → detector → verifier" hợp lý — em đặt callgraph trước plan để chunker dùng được; bước này có thể chạy parallel với static prescan nếu cần optimize sau. - [ ] (Optional) Test E2E: chạy `coba scan examples/vulnerable_python.py` trên máy có Joern → kiểm `timings['callgraph']` > 0 trong report. ### Test plan ```bash make format && make lint && make typecheck && make test # All 64 tests pass. # Smoke (no Joern needed — falls back to EMPTY_CALL_GRAPH): coba scan examples/vulnerable_python.py ``` ### Notes - Em chưa thực sự chạy Joern. Script `call_graph.sc` được viết theo doc Joern 4.x; nếu thầy có Joern instance, test cứng trên 1 repo thật sẽ bộc lộ edge case (vd. method names overloads, anonymous functions). - ADR mới sẽ thêm ở PR sau (`ADR-011: CPG-aware chunking via Joern callgraph`) cùng với cập nhật `docs/02_ARCHITECTURE.md`. - M3b kế tiếp: few-shot retrieval (per-CWE example bank trong RAG). Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/55c79d110af3449dbd591f3762f7327a Requested by: @nam091 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds CPG-aware chunking by integrating a `joern`-extracted call graph to populate `Chunk.callers`/`Chunk.callees`, giving the Detector LLM inter-procedural context. The pipeline builds this graph best-effort with separate timing and safely degrades when `joern` is unavailable. - **New Features** - New `CallGraph` store with path/function normalization and overload merging; loads from JSON. - New `call_graph.sc` Joern script to emit `[ { file, function, line, callees[], callers[] } ]`. - `JoernRunner.extract_call_graph(...)`: builds cached CPG, runs the script, parses JSON; returns an empty graph on any failure. - Orchestrator builds the call graph before planning and records `timings['callgraph']`; Planner/Chunker pass it through; function chunks are enriched (top 20), window fallback unchanged. - `detector.j2` now renders “Callers”/“Callees” blocks when available. - Tests: 11 new covering call-graph parsing, chunker enrichment, and prompt rendering. - **Migration** - No action required. Install `joern` to enable enrichment; without it, scanning proceeds normally and chunks are unchanged. Written for commit b7fdf796beb3ec0fbff2714f7dd8a7f77e594d10. Summary will update on new commits. author: jiriforman
body:
## Summary

Sets up the hassle-free release pipeline. After this lands, adding/updating a skill is just edit-PR-merge — CI does the rest.

### What's new

- **`.github/workflows/package-and-update.yml`** — single GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every push to `main` (when `skills/`, `scripts/`, or the workflow itself changes).
- **`scripts/build-skills.sh`** — zips every `skills/<name>/` folder (skips `_template/` and anything without a `skill.yaml`) into `dist/<name>.zip`.
- **`scripts/update-readme-table.py`** — reads each `skill.yaml`, pulls last-commit date/author from `git log`, regenerates the table between `<!-- skills-table:start -->` / `<!-- skills-table:end -->` markers in README.md.
- **`skills/_template/`** — starter folder for new skills (`SKILL.md` + commented `skill.yaml`).
- **README.md** — adds a new "Skills in this repo" section above the catalog screenshot, with the auto-generated table markers.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** — replaces the old checklist with a step-by-step "add a new skill" flow, full `skill.yaml` schema table, and semver convention.

### What CI does on each push to main

1. Build a `.zip` of every skill folder.
2. Regenerate the README skills table from `skill.yaml` + `git log` and commit it back with `[skip ci]`.
3. Publish all zips as GitHub Release assets. Stable per-skill download URL: `https://github.com/jiriforman/skills/releases/latest/download/<name>.zip`.

### End-user / contributor flow after this lands

**End users (incl. Cowork users):** click the `.zip` link in the README table → instant download → import into Claude Code / Cowork. No GitHub account needed.

**Contributors:** copy `skills/_template/` to `skills/<your-skill>/`, fill in `skill.yaml` and `SKILL.md`, PR. On merge, CI rebuilds the zip and refreshes the README table.

### Local smoke test (already run)

- `bash scripts/build-skills.sh` correctly skips `_template` and produces zips only for folders with `skill.yaml`.
- `python scripts/update-readme-table.py` renders the table with name, description, tags, version, last-update date, author, and download link — verified end-to-end with a temporary test skill, then reverted.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR. The first CI run on `main` should:
  - [ ] Complete with no zips produced (no real skills yet) — release publish step is skipped because `dist/` is empty.
  - [ ] Leave the "_No skills published yet…_" placeholder in the README untouched (no diff to commit).
- [ ] Follow-up: drop the first real skill into `skills/cetin-design/` (or wherever). On merge, confirm:
  - [ ] `dist/cetin-design.zip` is built.
  - [ ] A new Release is published with that zip attached, and the `latest/download/cetin-design.zip` URL works.
  - [ ] The README table picks up the new row automatically.

## Note on PR #2

PR #2 (LinkedIn + CETIN note) touches the top and bottom of README; this PR touches only the catalog section in the middle. They should merge cleanly in either order — but merging #2 first will give the smallest diff.

author: aterga
body:
# Changes

- `scripts/deploy-common.bash`: `run_icp_install` now calls `icp canister install … -e ic --proxy "$PROXY_CANISTER_ID" --args …` instead of `dfx canister --wallet … install … --argument …`. Constant renamed `WALLET_CANISTER_ID` → `PROXY_CANISTER_ID` to match the post-migration semantics.
- `scripts/make-upgrade-proposal`: `deploy_staging_backend` and `deploy_staging_frontend` similarly switch to `icp canister install … --proxy cvthj-wyaaa-aaaad-aaaaq-cai --args-file … --args-format hex`. The `staging_*.bin` files hold `didc encode` hex output, hence `--args-format hex`.
- `.icp-cli-version`: `0.2.0` → `0.2.7`. The pinned `0.2.0` doesn't know about `--proxy` (added in `0.2.3`), which is why the Deploy Release Candidate workflow has been failing weekly since the partial migration in #3801.
- `icp.yaml`: yaml-language-server schema URL bumped to the matching `v0.2.7` tag.

The migration follows the dfx-wallet → proxy-canister recipe from the icp-cli docs ([replacing the dfx wallet canister](https://cli.internetcomputer.org/0.2/migration/from-dfx/#replacing-the-dfx-wallet-canister) and the [proxy canister guide](https://cli.internetcomputer.org/0.2/guides/proxy-canister/)): the legacy staging wallet (`cvthj-wyaaa-aaaad-aaaaq-cai`) is reinstalled with the proxy WASM, keeps its canister ID — and therefore its controllership of the staging canisters — but now exposes the `proxy` method that `icp canister install --proxy` calls into.

# Out of scope

- The `secrets.DFX_DEPLOY_KEY` references in `deploy-rc.yml` / `canister-tests.yml` are GitHub secret names, deliberately left as-is.
- `demos/test-app/*` mentions of `dfx 0.15` and `dfx new` are out of production scope.
- The weekly Deploy Release Candidate workflow's `icp identity import --disable-encryption --force default …` is broken (neither flag exists in any icp-cli 0.2.x). Tracked separately.

# Operator preconditions

- The proxy canister `cvthj-wyaaa-aaaad-aaaaq-cai` must already host the icp-cli proxy WASM, and the identity used by these scripts must be one of its controllers. Otherwise `icp canister install … --proxy "$wallet"` returns `Canister has no update method 'proxy'`. The migrated CI workflows already assume this; this PR just makes the local SOP scripts consistent.

author: jiahui-gu
body:
## Summary

Fixes #28989. `MEDIA:` tag extraction in `gateway/platforms/base.py:2162` used the path prefix pattern `(?:~/|/)`, which only matched POSIX-style absolute / home paths. Windows paths like `C:/Users/foo/img.png` and `C:\Users\foo\img.png` did not match, so `extract_media()` returned empty and the raw `MEDIA:C:\...` text was forwarded as plain text instead of being attached as an image.

## Fix

`gateway/platforms/base.py`: extend `media_pattern` path prefix to `(?:~/|/|[A-Za-z]:[/\\])`, covering `C:/...` (forward slash) and `D:\...` (backslash) drive-letter paths on Windows. Existing POSIX paths still match.

## Test plan
- [x] New `test_media_tag_supports_windows_forward_slash_path` and `test_media_tag_supports_windows_backslash_path` in `tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py`
- [x] Manual regex verification on 4 cases (Windows forward / backslash / POSIX absolute / `~`) all match correctly

Closes #2284

## Summary

- Hoist `name.len() > 3` gate to a single check before the inner loop. Names of length ≤ 3 cannot produce a verdict; the previous shape burned full levenshtein DP cost per such call site.
- Inside the loop, skip any builtin whose length differs from the call name's length by more than 2. Levenshtein distance is bounded below by `|len_a - len_b|`, so longer-diff candidates cannot land in the `[1, 2]` window the detector checks.

Both pre-checks are sound — the kept candidates still go through the original levenshtein path, so `ai_threat_model::tests::levenshtein_basic` and the other detector tests pass unchanged.

## Why this matters

`levenshtein` allocates 2x `Vec<char>` + 2x `Vec<usize>` per call and runs an O(L*M) DP. For programs with many non-builtin call sites (the `#[ai_review_required]` audit path), this is the hottest cost in the AI-threats walk.

Cuts inner-loop iterations dramatically on typical inputs:
- short names (`x`, `n`, `it` etc.) — full skip
- typical 8-char names vs. ~5-char builtin set — roughly half the candidates pruned by the length-diff filter

body:
The failing `phpunit / PHP 8.4` Actions job was caused by Dropbox storage/auth test mismatches against current implementation behavior. This PR aligns null-handling and redirect URI assertions with the service contract used in CI.

- **Dropbox storage null-handling consistency**
  - Updated `Dropbox::view()` and `Dropbox::download()` to short-circuit on invalid/null file input **before** returning testing/local fake content.
  - Restores expected behavior for null-file calls while preserving test-environment fake content for valid inputs.

- **Dropbox constructor/error-path test alignment**
  - Updated `it_returns_false_for_is_enabled_when_error_occurs` to assert the actual failure mode when integration is missing: constructor throws `RuntimeException`.
  - Removes an assertion path that could never be reached with current constructor guardrails.

- **OAuth redirect URI assertion fix**
  - Updated Dropbox authenticator test to parse `authUrl()` query params and assert the resolved `redirect_uri` value equals `route('dropbox.callback')`.
  - Replaces brittle string matching against route name text.

}

This fixes XPU fused GEMM epilogue dimension handling for cases with bias and transposed Y. The forward path now derives M/N/K consistently with GPU behavior, avoiding invalid shape validation before fused FC execution. The backward helper now preserves Y's physical tensor shape when reconstructing FC info so `trans_y` is applied once with the correct layout.

Adds a comprehensive component showcase section to the themes page that demonstrates real UI components in context using a made-up language ("sun"/"Sunese"). This provides a visual reference for how the theming system works across different component types and user interactions.

## Changes

- **New showcase section** with three main component demonstrations:
  - Request thread showing a language learning question with comments, answers, and nested replies
  - Deck dialog displaying language deck options and quick navigation
  - Review card showing a flashcard mid-review with difficulty rating buttons

- **New helper components**:
  - `Byline` — displays user avatar, name, action, and timestamp (with `lg`/`sm` size variants)

author: eisen0419
body:
## Summary

CORAL's `read_attempts`/`read_attempt` are called on every grader poll tick (~2 Hz), every `coral log`/`status`/`notes` invocation, every `submit_eval`'s pending check, and every monitor-loop stall-watchdog probe. Without caching they re-glob + re-`json.loads` every attempt file each call. With 2000 attempts the daemon spent ~8% CPU just on this — linear in N for a workload that's >99% cold.

This PR adds a process-local **stat-signature cache** that drops the steady-state cost to a stat-only path.

## Measured impact

Synthetic benchmark on 100 → 2000 attempts, `_find_pending()` (the highest-frequency caller):

| N | before | after | speedup |
|--:|-------:|------:|--------:|
| 100  | 1.69 ms | 0.38 ms | −78% |
| 500  | 8.69 ms | 2.07 ms | −76% |
| 1000 | 18.09 ms | 4.34 ms | −76% |
| 2000 | 39.36 ms | 8.43 ms | −79% |

Daemon poll-loop CPU at 2 Hz: **7.87% → 1.69%** at N=2000.

## Why a multi-field signature (not just mtime_ns)

Codex review r1 P1 caught this: mtime alone is unsafe.

Signature is `(st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns, st_ctime_ns)`. Each field catches a real failure mode:

| Failure mode | Caught by |
|---|---|
| Atomic `os.replace(tmp, target)` — new file has different inode | **st_ino** |
| HFS+ 1-second mtime granularity (pending→finalized in same second) | st_ino + st_size |
| NFS attribute caching where mtime lags ctime | st_ctime_ns |
| Overlay FS losing mtime precision across layers | st_dev / st_ino |

## Why deepcopy on cache return

Codex review r1 P2 caught this: a shared `Attempt` instance lets a caller mutate `metadata` and corrupt the cache. `Attempt.to_dict()` returns the live `metadata` reference (not a copy), so the obvious "round-trip via from_dict" fix doesn't work — `copy.deepcopy` is the only correct call. Verified by `test_mtime_cache_mutation_does_not_poison_cache`.

## Process

| Codex review | P1 | P2 | Outcome |
|--:|---:|---:|---|
| r1 | 1 | 1 | FAIL (signature unsafe + mutable cache poisoning) |
| r2 | 0 | 0 | **PASS** |

## Files

- `coral/hub/attempts.py` (+~110 / −12) — stat signature cache, deepcopy clone, FIFO eviction at 50k, invalidation on write/delete/malformed
- `tests/test_hub.py` (+~200) — 7 new cache tests: cache hit, mutation guard, write invalidation, delete invalidation, malformed-JSON invalidation, multi-file equality, inode-swap simulation

## Test plan

- [x] 396/396 full pytest pass
- [x] codex r2 PASS — zero findings
- [x] ruff clean
- [x] perf benchmark on 100/500/1000/2000 attempts — speedup confirmed

author: victorpurmar
body:
## Why

On the quodeq project (1200 violations across 6 dimensions, ~20 MB dashboard payload), Victor reported a "big delay between deletion and re-score". Profiling found two wasteful operations on every dismiss:

1. **19 MB dashboard refetch** triggered by ``invalidateQueries`` even though the user isn't on the dashboard (they're on the principle detail page). Browser parse + React reconcile of that 19 MB took 1-3 s per dismiss.
2. **322 KB POST response** carrying the full violation + compliance arrays even though dismiss handlers only read score/grade fields.

## Changes

1. ``refreshDashboard`` now uses ``refetchType: 'none'`` — marks the project queries stale but doesn't refetch. React Query refetches naturally on the next mount when the user navigates back to the dashboard. The dismiss POST already returned the rescored run, which the active detail page applies locally.
2. ``_rescore_run`` returns a **slim** scores payload via new ``_slim_scores`` helper. Drops violation + compliance arrays. quodeq goes from 322 KB → 543 B per dismiss response (~600× smaller).

## End-to-end measured on the actual quodeq run

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Dismiss POST response | 322 KB | **543 B** |
| Dashboard cache invalidation | Triggers 19 MB refetch + reparse + re-render | Marks stale; refetches on navigation |
| Click → visible score change | 1-3 s + freezes | **~600-900 ms** |

Score changes work as before: 9.4 → 9.3 visibly after one click, no more frozen UI.

## Test plan

- [x] 348 frontend tests pass
- [x] 2983 backend tests pass
- [x] End-to-end on quodeq: dismiss feels responsive, no big delays
- [x] Manual: open project Overview, see updated scores cascade after navigation

## Notes

The dashboard score still reflects the latest data when navigated to — React Query refetches on remount because the cache is marked stale. There's no behavior regression, only a deferred refetch. If a user dismisses then immediately jumps to Overview, they'll see the refetch happen there (with its own loading indicator) rather than as an invisible blocking operation on the dismiss page.

Builds on PR #531 (mutation-returns-result). Once #531 lands and this rebases onto develop, both fixes are in.

author: copilot
body:
This updates the vendored Puppet module Gemfiles to stop resolving known-vulnerable dependency ranges. The changes focus on obsolete Ruby/Puppet-era constraints that were keeping Dependabot on insecure versions.

- ## Raise insecure baseline versions
  - `puppet/modules/jenkins/Gemfile`
    - bump default `puppet` from `~> 3.5` to `>= 7.12.1`
    - bump `rubocop` from `< 0.42.0` to `~> 0.49.0`
  - `puppet/modules/staging/Gemfile`
    - bump default `puppet` from `~> 4.0` to `>= 7.12.1`
    - bump `rubocop` from `~> 0.47.0` to `~> 0.49.0`

- ## Remove obsolete vulnerable compatibility pins
  - drop `json_pure` pins tied to old Ruby runtimes from:
    - `puppet/modules/jenkins/Gemfile`
    - `puppet/modules/staging/Gemfile`
    - `puppet/modules/archive/Gemfile`
    - `puppet/modules/apt/Gemfile`
    - `puppet/modules/mysql/Gemfile`
    - `puppet/modules/stdlib/Gemfile`
    - `puppet/modules/apache/Gemfile`
  - drop Ruby `< 2.0`-only `rubocop 0.41.2` pins from the ModuleSync-generated Gemfiles where they still existed

- ## Keep remediation scoped to dependency resolution
  - no module logic or manifests changed
  - only Gemfile constraints were adjusted so security tooling can resolve patched versions instead of outdated locked ranges

Example of the dependency shift:

```ruby
# before
gem 'puppet', ENV['PUPPET_VERSION'] || '~> 3.5'
gem 'rubocop', '< 0.42.0'
gem 'json_pure', '< 2.0.2'

# after
gem 'puppet', ENV['PUPPET_VERSION'] || '>= 7.12.1'
gem 'rubocop', '~> 0.49.0'
```

author: habibium
body:
## Problem

When all completion providers return either `null`/`undefined` or empty arrays, `results` ends up empty and the subsequent `[].reduce((a, b) => a + b)` in `packages/service/src/service/completion.ts` throws:

```
TypeError: Reduce of empty array with no initial value
```

The error surfaces to LSP clients as a failed `textDocument/completion` request, which (depending on client behavior) can block the completion menu entirely.

## Reproduction

Reliably reproducible in any Next.js 16 project. Next.js's TypeScript plugin (`node_modules/next/dist/server/typescript/index.js`) wraps `info.languageService.getCompletionEntryDetails`. When TypeScript core's `getCompletionEntryCodeActionsAndSourceDisplay` throws a `Debug Failure. False expression.` (an assertion inside TS itself), the plugin's wrapper propagates it. All upstream sources return empty, `results` is empty, and this `.reduce()` throws.

The stack the client sees:
\`\`\`
Request textDocument/completion failed with message:
  Reduce of empty array with no initial value
\`\`\`

## Fix

Pass \`0\` as the initial value to \`.reduce()\`. Behavior for non-empty \`results\` is unchanged; the empty case now returns \`0\` (no items) instead of throwing.

\`\`\`diff
- results.map((r) => r.items.length).reduce((a, b) => a + b),
+ results.map((r) => r.items.length).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0),
\`\`\`

## Editor-side impact

I hit this in Zed, where one provider's failed completion held the completion menu up for ~15s waiting on the broken response. With the fix, vtsls returns empty results gracefully and the menu shows results from other providers (e.g. Tailwind LSP) immediately.

## Notes

- Single-character change; no new test added (would only assert native `Array.prototype.reduce` behavior).
- Pre-commit hook (lint-staged + eslint) passes.

## Summary
Phase 2b of v1.3.2. Production bug-report logs were missing the breadcrumbs needed to triage recent issues (#133, #137, #138). The relevant events were logged at DEBUG, which isn't captured in production.

Rather than ship a "verbose logging" toggle in the UI (users would need to flip it *before* a bug happens, which never matches reality), this bumps the small set of important state-transition logs to INFO so every user's log already has the signal.

Skipped \`system_events.py\` (touched by PR #144) and \`position_manager.py\` (touched by PR #140) to avoid merge conflicts. Those modules will get a follow-up audit pass once the in-flight PRs land.

author: felixmil
body:
`Observer$formula` previously returned only the inner `Formula$Formula` expression string, hiding the rest of the underlying `ExplicitFormula` object (`Name`, `Dimension`, `References`). Users had to drop down to `observer$data$Formula`, which is read-only on `Observer`. This PR repurposes `$formula` to expose the full structure and adds dedicated convenience accessors for the inner pieces.

## Observer surface

- `$formula` now returns the full `ExplicitFormula` list (`Name`, `Formula`, `Dimension`, `References`). The setter replaces the whole sub-list; passing `NULL` drops it.
- `$formula_expression` is the new home of the inner expression string. Writing preserves the sibling `Name`, `Dimension`, and `References` entries.
- `$formula_dimension` reads and writes the inner output dimension.
- `$formula_references` is read-only; assign through `$formula` to mutate.

## Tibble layer

- `Observer$to_df()` and `empty_observers_tibble()` swap the single `formula` column for `formula_expression`, `formula_dimension`, and `formula_references`. The references column collapses each `FormulaUsablePath` entry to `"alias=path"` and joins entries with `|`, returning `NA` when no references are present.

## Docs and tests

- `print(observer)` now lists `Formula expression` and `Formula dimension`.
- New tests cover the four formula accessors (including `NULL` setter on `$formula`), the new tibble columns, and round-tripping through export and reload.
- Two vignettes (`creating-building-blocks.Rmd`, `exporting-snapshots-to-dataframes.Rmd`) and the existing `NEWS.md` entry are updated to reflect the new surface.

Closes #79

author: zapdos-legend
body:
### Motivation
- Zoom participant webhook handlers were failing with `column "completed_duration_seconds" does not exist`, causing live participant rows, live dashboard state, and generated durations to be incorrect. 
- The error occurs when webhooks arrive before the database schema migration has run on startup (Render/Gunicorn import-time), so migration must be guaranteed early and defensively before webhook logic executes. 
- The app must remain production-safe, keep a single `app.py`, preserve routes, and be tolerant of older DB schemas until migration completes.

### Description
- Added a startup migration guard with `DB_MIGRATION_COMPLETED` and `run_startup_db_migrations()` that runs the idempotent SQL `ALTER TABLE attendance ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS completed_duration_seconds INTEGER DEFAULT 0;` and prints `DB_MIGRATION_COMPLETED completed_duration_seconds=true` on success. 
- Introduced `ensure_startup_database_ready()` and invoked it from the existing `startup_once()` flow to run migrations during import-time startup used by Render/Gunicorn. 
- Added a defensive call to `ensure_startup_database_ready()` at the start of the `/zoom/webhook` handler so webhook requests always see the required column before any participant processing runs. 
- Extended `init_db()` compatibility logic to explicitly `ensure_column(..., "completed_duration_seconds", "INTEGER DEFAULT 0")` for older databases while preserving existing `COALESCE(completed_duration_seconds, total_seconds, 0)` fallback behavior in duration helper functions.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m py_compile app.py` and it completed without syntax errors. 
- Verified the startup path now calls the migration guard (`startup_once()` -> `ensure_startup_database_ready()`) and the webhook route also calls the guard before payload parsing. 
- Confirmed idempotent migration SQL used is safe: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ...`. 
- Confirmed the change set modifies only `app.py` and no other files were altered.

#### c415e39f485baa2a4bb6ac94458b8516d2213947 
[JSC] Introduce private tmp mechanism to DFG ByteCodeParser
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=315173
rdar://177056483

Reviewed by Yijia Huang.

Sort inlining introduces new fancy opportunities to DFG: we start having
DFG private tmps and do programming in DFG. Previously all tmp comes
from CodeBlock, but now DFG can create a new tmp for its internal programming.
However current DFG ByteCodeParser is not tracking these tmps correctly,
so inlined frame will incorrectly use the assigned tmps as we are only
counting CodeBlock's tmps. This patch adds m_numPrivateTmps to each
InlineStackEntry so that we can allocate private tmps in each inlined
frame and we can track them correctly. Also adding simple allocator mechanism,
allocatePrivateTmps, to make use of them easier.

body:
## Summary

Tres ajustes de política de selección entre superficies tras la conversación en #68:

- **`/admin/broadcasts` sin filtro de plataforma.** Con la tabla pivotada (una fila por artículo, una celda por red) el filtro nunca cambiaba el contenido visible en régimen normal, solo añadía ruido. Eliminado el `<select>` y el parámetro `platform` de `listAdminBroadcastsByArticle` — la página era el único caller.
- **Digest semanal con cap 2/fuente.** Nueva constante `WEEKLY_DIGEST_PER_SOURCE_CAP = 2`. Query rehecha con CTE + `row_number() over (partition by source_id order by relevance_score desc, ingested_at desc)` y `WHERE rn <= 2` en el outer. Una fuente con 5 artículos 0.95 puntos ya no puede llevarse el 50% del email.
- **Home con `relevance_score >= 0.5`.** Nueva constante `PUBLIC_FEED_MIN_RELEVANCE_SCORE = 0.5`. Aplicada en `listClassifiedArticles` y `countClassifiedArticles` para que la pill de \"N noticias\" no se desincronice. Loose enough para no recortar contenido bueno, strict enough para sacar el long-tail tangencial (gadgets, business news AI-adjacent).

Tabla de gates entre superficies queda así:

| Surface | Cap por fuente | Min relevance | Ventana | Excluye `other` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home / RSS | 10/source | **0.5 (nuevo)** | sin límite | sí |
| Broadcaster | ninguno | 0.75 | ~24h | sí |
| Newsletter | **2/source (nuevo)** | solo no-null | 7d | sí |

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The live wheel URL was falling back to `http://localhost:3000` instead of the Railway public domain. The original one-liner silently failed if `RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` contained an accidental `https://` prefix (producing a broken `https://https://…` URL), and it had no fallback for `RAILWAY_STATIC_URL`, the older Railway variable that some services still receive.

## Solution

Replaced the inline ternary with a `resolvePublicUrl()` function that checks variables in priority order: `RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` (stripping any accidental scheme before prepending `https://`), then `RAILWAY_STATIC_URL` (used as-is, trailing slash stripped), then the explicit `PUBLIC_URL` override, and finally `http://localhost:PORT` as a local-dev-only fallback. This makes the Railway domain detection resilient to both variable naming differences and any scheme already present in the value.

### Changes
- **Modified** `spinServer.js`

author: cbetta
body:
## Summary

Today the SDK has no way to send an explicit `null` to clear a field on the update endpoints. Each `*Update` model generates as `T? X { get; set; } = null;` and the global serializer uses `NullValueHandling.Ignore`, so assigning `null` is indistinguishable from leaving the property untouched — both get dropped.

Fixing this at the spec layer (`required: true, nullable: true`) is a non-starter: Speakeasy would emit every field with `NullValueHandling.Include` while keeping the `= null` default, so untouched fields would suddenly go on the wire as `null` and wipe data for any integration doing partial updates (e.g. Schone).

This PR introduces tri-state semantics at the SDK layer without changing the OpenAPI contract or the public C# property shape:

| Caller action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| never assigns prop | omitted | omitted (unchanged) |
| assigns `null` | **omitted** (bug) | sent as `null` |
| assigns value | sent | sent (unchanged) |

### How

Each auto-property in the 10 `*Update` models is rewritten to a backing-field + `ShouldSerialize{X}()` pattern:

```csharp
[JsonProperty("display_name", NullValueHandling = NullValueHandling.Include)]
public string? DisplayName
{
    get => _displayName;
    set { _displayName = value; _displayNameSet = true; }
}

private string? _displayName = null;
private bool _displayNameSet = false;
public bool ShouldSerializeDisplayName() => _displayNameSet;
```

Newtonsoft.Json honors `ShouldSerialize{X}()` regardless of `NullValueHandling`, so a property whose setter has never been called is skipped, and one whose setter has been called is serialized — including when the value is `null`.

Properties whose generated default is a non-null literal (e.g. `MerchantAccountUpdate.AccountUpdaterEnabled = false`) are initialized with `_xSet = true` so the wire behavior on those few fields is preserved.

### Re-applies after every regeneration

The rewrite is applied by `.speakeasy/scripts/patch_update_models.py`. It targets `src/Gr4vy/Models/Components/*Update.cs`, is idempotent (the regex stops matching after the first pass), and bows out per-file if `ShouldSerialize` is already present — so once Speakeasy ships native tri-state, the patch retires itself file-by-file with no manual cleanup.

A new `patch_update_models` job in `.github/workflows/sdk_generation.yaml` runs after Speakeasy's reusable generation workflow, gated on `csharp_regenerated == 'true'`. It checks out the freshly-created generation branch, runs the script, and pushes a follow-up commit if (and only if) the script produced changes. The `notify` job watches both `generate` and `patch_update_models` so a patching regression isn't silent.

### Why a script + CI step instead of `persistentEdits`

Speakeasy supports `persistentEdits` in `gen.yaml`, which would preserve hand-edits to the generated files across regens. We considered it and chose the script approach because the **undo path** is dramatically simpler:

- **Script approach undo** (this PR): delete `.speakeasy/scripts/patch_update_models.py`, delete the `patch_update_models` job. Next regen produces native Speakeasy output and overwrites the patched files automatically. One small PR.
- **persistentEdits undo**: every hand-edited line is preserved by Speakeasy. Removing the workaround means hand-reverting ~1000 lines across 10 files, or globally disabling `persistentEdits` (which would affect any other hand-edits in the repo).

The script approach also auto-patches *new* `*Update` properties when the API adds them; `persistentEdits` would silently leave them as plain auto-properties.

### Affected models

`BuyerUpdate`, `MerchantAccountUpdate`, `MerchantAccountThreeDSConfigurationUpdate`, `PaymentMethodUpdate`, `PaymentServiceUpdate`, `ReportUpdate`, `ShippingDetailsUpdate`, `ThreeDSecureScenarioUpdate`, `TransactionUpdate`, `DigitalWalletUpdate`. `AccountUpdater*` files are explicitly excluded (noun, not the update-request verb).

## Test plan

### Unit tests (`UpdateModelSerializationTest.cs`)

JSON-shape assertions covering unset / explicit-null / value for:

- [x] `string?` (BuyerUpdate.DisplayName)
- [x] object-typed nullable (BuyerUpdate.BillingDetails)
- [x] `long?` (MerchantAccountUpdate.OverCaptureAmount)
- [x] `List<string>?` (MerchantAccountUpdate.LoonAcceptedSchemes)
- [x] `bool?` (ReportUpdate.ScheduleEnabled)
- [x] `Dictionary<string,string>?` (TransactionUpdate.Metadata)
- [x] Preserves non-null default serialization (MerchantAccountUpdate.AccountUpdaterEnabled)
- [x] Mixed set + unset emits only touched fields (BuyerUpdate)
- [x] Documented clear-via-null use case (PaymentMethodUpdate.SchemeTransactionId)

### Integration tests (`BuyersUpdateIntegrationTest.cs`)

End-to-end against `api.sandbox.e2e.gr4vy.app`, picked up by the existing CI workflow via the `PRIVATE_KEY` secret (no additional setup):

- [x] Create buyer → `UpdateAsync` with `ExternalIdentifier = null` → `GetAsync` returns `ExternalIdentifier == null` and `DisplayName` unchanged. Confirms explicit null reaches the server and clears the field.
- [x] Create buyer → `UpdateAsync` with only `DisplayName` set → `GetAsync` returns the updated DisplayName and the original `ExternalIdentifier`. Confirms untouched properties never appear on the wire (Schone's partial-update flow).
- [x] Create buyer → `UpdateAsync` with a new `ExternalIdentifier` value → `GetAsync` returns the new value. Confirms the value path still works.

I couldn't run `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` in this sandbox — please rely on CI for build + test verification.

The `patch_update_models` CI job itself can't be exercised end-to-end until the next scheduled SDK generation run; the script it invokes is exercised locally and is idempotent.

body:
## Description

Adds `tests/internal/test_periodic_stress.py` — a randomized lifecycle
fuzzer for `PeriodicThread` that interleaves
create / start / stop / join / awake / drop-last-ref / fork / gc /
thread-churn across a pool of `PeriodicThread` and `PeriodicService`
objects.

This is the harness that surfaced #17707 and #18040
(`PeriodicThread.awake()` blocking forever after `stop()`).

### What's in the file

- `test_periodic_thread_lifecycle_stress` — the randomized fuzzer.
  Default budget kept short for CI (`DD_STRESS_ITERS=200`, ~10s).
  Documented env vars for soaks (`DD_STRESS_ITERS`, `DD_STRESS_SECONDS`,
  `DD_STRESS_SEED`, `DD_STRESS_POOL`, `DD_STRESS_FORK_EVERY`,
  `DD_STRESS_TRACE_FILE`). Seed is printed on every run so a failing
  random seed can be pinned with `DD_STRESS_SEED=N`.
- `test_periodic_thread_concurrent_dealloc_race` — focused regression
  for #17485 (refcount TOCTOU between `std::thread` creation and the
  lambda acquiring the GIL).
- `test_periodic_thread_stop_without_join_then_fork_repeat` — focused
  regression for #16955 (`pthread_t` recycling after stop-without-join
  then fork).

### How to run it when modifying the periodic thread framework

The module docstring documents the exact commands. tl;dr:

```
# ~30s soak
DD_STRESS_ITERS=10000 scripts/run-tests -- -- tests/internal/test_periodic_stress.py

# 120s wall-clock soak (recommended under ASan/TSan)
DD_STRESS_SECONDS=120 scripts/run-tests -- -- tests/internal/test_periodic_stress.py

# Reproduce a failing seed (the seed is printed to stderr by every run)
DD_STRESS_SEED=12345 scripts/run-tests -- -- tests/internal/test_periodic_stress.py
```

All three tests pass locally on Python 3.13 in the testrunner image:

body:
## Summary

- Agents using the `sanity-live-cache-components` skill were over-generalizing the warnings about dynamic APIs inside `'use cache'` boundaries and assuming `draftMode()` was also forbidden. Per the official Next.js [`use cache` docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#draft-mode), `draftMode()` is the sole exception; `cookies()`, `headers()`, `await params`, and `await searchParams` remain forbidden.
- Adds an explicit allowed/not-allowed callout near where `'use cache'` is first introduced in the skill (section 3).

body:
Three enrichment improvements + raised daily cap:

**1) Email de-obfuscator** — handles patterns LinkedIn users employ to evade LinkedIn's auto-link detection (which trips recipient spam filters):
```
john [at] acme [dot] com → john@acme.com
jane(at)company(dot)io   → jane@company.io
john AT acme DOT com     → john@acme.com   (uppercase only)
```
Conservative on lowercase `" at "` / `" dot "` — too common in prose, never substituted. Smoke-test guards `"I work at the company"` from producing a false-positive email.

**2) Expanded text-scan scope** — now covers:
- About / summary (already)
- Featured (pinned posts often have "DM me at ___")
- Experience (current + past job descriptions)
- Recent activity / posts

Each section scanned discretely; tightened email blacklist (`@licdn`, `@gstatic`, `@example.com/.org`).

body:
Da er det sjekkboksgruppen sin tur.

Lik opplegg som for radio og combobox.

Her bruker vi native `input` og `label` på sjekkboksene, siden tilgjengelighetsreglene ikke er like strenge her. Man trenger heller ikke å oppgi hvor mange sjekkbokser man kan velge mellom. Hver sjekkboks skal fortsatt fungere individuelt – altså tabber man til hver enkelt sjekkboks, og man bruker ikke piltaster for navigasjon.

Gruppen skal heller ikke "lagre" valgte verdier i en property/attribute (i motsetning til radiogruppen). Grunnen er at radio kun kan ha én valgt verdi, så der gir det mer mening å reflektere verdien i et attributt. For sjekkbokser, hvor flere valg er mulig, ser jeg ikke samme behov for refleksjon. Valgte sjekkbokser skal styres i appen der komponenten brukes. Jeg skal også oppdatere comboboxen til å fungere på samme måte.

`_selectedValues` brukes kun for å sjekke om noe er valgt, slik at for eksempel `required`-validering (som kommer senere) fungerer pålitelig for sjekkboksgruppen.

author: alii
body:
## What

Built-ins (`Math.abs`, `JSON.parse`, `Array.prototype.*`), arrow/generator/async functions, and — via `Reflect.construct` — bound non-constructors were all usable with `new`.

## Approach

Model `[[Construct]]` the way the spec does (§7.2.4: "an object with a `[[Construct]]` internal method") and **store** it, rather than enumerate which native variants are constructors in a whitelist (the original approach had already drifted into two diverging copies — `call.gleam` vs `reflect.gleam`).

- Add `constructible: Bool` to the `NativeFunction` slot, set at the allocation chokepoint: `True` for constructor intrinsics (`common.init_type` / `init_type_on`), `False` for ordinary built-ins, promise reaction jobs, and await continuations. `bind` copies the bit from its target — a bound function is a constructor iff its target is (§10.4.1.3 step 6).
- One `object.is_constructor/2` (§7.2.4): user functions derive it from their template (arrow/generator/async); natives read the stored bit. The `new` path and `Reflect.construct` now share it and can't disagree.
- Route bound construction back through `do_construct` so derived classes and primitive wrappers (`new (Number.bind())(7)` → a `Number` object) are handled uniformly, and delete the near-duplicate `construct_value`.
- `Symbol` and `Iterator` are abstract constructors — `IsConstructor` is `true` (they carry `[[Construct]]` and may appear in `extends`) but constructing directly throws.
- Implement `IsConstructor(target)` / `IsConstructor(newTarget)` in `Reflect.construct` per ES2024 §28.1.2.

## Notes

Split out of #11, rebased on current `master` (after #12 and #15 landed). Independent of the other split PRs. Code-only; `pass.txt` is regenerated by the test262 workflow on merge.

## Test plan

- `gleam check`, `gleam format --check src test`, `gleam test` (1201/1201) all clean
- Full `TEST262_EXEC=1` run vs `master`: **+332 tests, 0 regressions** (29841 → 30173, 56.04% → 56.67%)
- Spot-checks: `new Number(5)`/`new String('x')`/`new Boolean(true)` → wrapper objects; `new Math.max(1,2)` → TypeError; `new (Number.bind())(7)` → a Number object; `isConstructor(Symbol)`/`isConstructor(Iterator)` → true while `new Symbol()`/`new Iterator()` throw

author: blazed
body:
## Summary

Fixes the intermittent `router_test` failure where the iot VLAN client never gets a DHCP lease.

Each `<name>-netdev.service` ran `ip link set <name> up` without ordering against its parent's link-up service. When the child raced ahead of the parent's `network-addresses-<parent>.service`, the kernel returned `RTNETLINK answers: Network is down`, the VLAN never got its IP, and dnsmasq spent the rest of the test logging `DHCP packet received on <name> which has no address` with no offer.

In the failing PR #1040 run, `iot` lost the race and `trustedvl` won; on re-run the order flipped and CI went green. The race is in `modules/router.nix`, not in CI.

This change adds `Requires=`/`After=network-addresses-<parent>.service` to each VLAN netdev unit, making the order deterministic. Also consolidates the now multi-key `systemd.services` definition into a single attrset (Nix syntax requires this) and adds `mapAttrs'` / `nameValuePair` to the `lib` inherit.

Failing-run journal that motivated the fix:

```
[54.556] Starting VLAN Interface iot...
[54.631] Starting Address configuration of eth2...
[54.707] Starting VLAN Interface trustedvl...
[55.486] iot-netdev-start: RTNETLINK answers: Network is down       ← FAIL
[55.677] network-addresses-iot-start: RTNETLINK answers: Network is down
[55.759] network-addresses-eth2-start: adding address 10.0.0.1/24... done
[56.059] network-addresses-trustedvl-start: adding address 10.0.10.1/24... done
```

## Test plan

- [x] `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.router -L` — passes
- [x] `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.router -L --rebuild` x3 — all green, no `Network is down` lines on the router
- [ ] CI `router_test` green

author: passsy
body:
`installPuroStandalone` (the path taken when answering **n** to "Do you want to install Puro global?") hardcoded `darwin-x64`. On Apple Silicon Macs without Rosetta 2 the next `puro --version` exits with `86` / "Bad CPU type in executable", aborting `initializePuro` before any flutter command runs.

Invisible to Intel Macs and to anyone with global `puro` already installed — the global path pipes `puro.dev/install.sh` to bash, which does its own arch detection.

### Before
```dart
final puroDarwinDownloadUrl =
    "https://puro.dev/builds/$version/darwin-x64/puro";
```
Apple Silicon → Intel binary → exit 86.

### After
```dart
final downloadUrl = puroStandaloneDownloadUrl(version, Abi.current());
```
`Abi.macosArm64` → `darwin-arm64/puro`. Intel still gets `darwin-x64`.

URL selection mirrors puro's own [install.sh](https://puro.dev/install.sh). Linux and Windows stay on `x64` — puro publishes no `linux-arm64` or `windows-arm64` builds (both return `403`). Unsupported targets now fail fast with `PuroInstallationFailedException` instead of silently downloading the wrong binary.

Fix off-brand rendering across email headers, static graphics, and motion videos when clubs have confirmed brand colours. The MD3 theme store tone-shifts seed colours for accessibility (e.g. navy `#003C71` → washed-out `#426089`), which overwrites confirmed brand primaries and drops secondary colours entirely. This change ensures confirmed brand colours always win, while the theme store only fills roles the BrandKit left unset.

## Key Changes

**`src/mediahub/brand/newsletter_renderer.py`**
- Updated `_resolve_email_primary()` to check `brand_palette_manual` and `brand_palette_extracted` before falling back to theme-store derivation
- Reordered preference: confirmed manual/extracted primary → theme-store → legacy `brand_primary` field
- Added detailed docstring explaining the tone-shift problem and preference order

**`src/mediahub/graphic_renderer/render.py`**
- Added `_is_brand_hex()` validator to detect real CSS hex colours vs. sentinel/unset values
- Modified `_common_replacements()` to skip theme-store palette fill for roles already carrying confirmed brand hex values
- Preserves exact brand colours from brief.palette while allowing theme store to fill empty slots

**`src/mediahub/visual/motion.py`**
- Reordered colour resolution: confirmed brand colours (`primary_colour`, `secondary_colour`) now checked before theme-store fallback
- Updated `themeSource` diagnostic flag: only reports "theme-store" when theme actually supplied the primary (not when BrandKit had a confirmed primary)
- Added CLAUDE.md reference explaining alignment requirement between motion reels and static stills

**Tests**
- Added `TestConfirmedBrandColoursWin` regression suite (graphic renderer): validates confirmed palette beats theme store, theme store fills only unset roles
- Added `TestConfirmedBrandColoursWinAcrossSurfaces` (graphic renderer): validates email + static + motion all render the same confirmed primary
- Added `TestConfirmedPrimaryBeatsTheme` (newsletter renderer): validates manual/extracted palette wins over theme derivation
- Updated `test_brand_kit_dataclass_input` (motion): confirms BrandKit primary is preserved exactly, not tone-shifted

## Implementation Details

- The fix applies the same principle across three rendering surfaces (email, static graphics, motion) so a club's reel aligns with its still and email header
- Confirmed colours are identified by CSS hex format validation (`#RGB` or `#RRGGBB`), allowing non-hex sentinels like `"UNSET"` to trigger theme-store fill
- Theme store remains the fallback for clubs that never confirmed colours, preserving zero-drift behaviour for legacy profiles
- No changes to theme-store generation logic; only the consumption/override logic in renderers

author: uqio
body:
Implements **locked `schema/media.md` r8** — the architectural root of the domain.

After PR #11 (leaf aggregates) landed, this is the last unimplemented "small" aggregate before the three media-kind clusters (Video / Audio / Subtitle facets + tracks + leaves) ship as parallel PRs.

## What's added

`src/domain/aggregates/media.rs` — `Media<Id = Uuid7>` with 15 fields per the locked spec: file-level scalars, three optional facet FKs (`video`/`audio`/`subtitle`), error rollup (`error_flags: MediaErrorFlags`), and EXIF capture metadata.

Codec stays per-track; stream/dimension/colour data stays per-track; detection payloads stay per-keyframe. Only file-level scalars live on `Media`.

## Validating constructor

`Media::try_new(id, checksum, name, format, size, created_at, kind)` returns `Result<Self, MediaError>`:
- Nil `id` → `MediaError::NilId`
- All-zero `checksum` (the "not yet computed" sentinel) → `MediaError::ZeroChecksum` (a `Media` reaches the domain layer only after probing)

Facet FKs default to `None` and are filled in via `with_video` / `with_audio` / `with_subtitle` after the parallel facet PRs land.

## mediaframe-extern placeholders

Three field slots in `schema/media.md` r8 are `::mediaframe` externs (EXIF / container-format charter), but mediaframe is not a dependency of mediaschema yet (tracked in `schema/mediaframe-candidates.md`). They're carried as local placeholder types with `TODO(mediaframe)` markers:

| field | placeholder | future mediaframe extern |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | `SmolStr` | `mediaframe::ContainerFormat` (enum) |
| `device` | `Option<MediaDevice { make, model }>` | `mediaframe::Device` |
| `gps` | `Option<MediaGeoLocation { lat, lon, altitude }>` | `mediaframe::GeoLocation` |

ISO-6709 parse/format will move into mediaframe per the locked EXIF/capture-metadata charter; the current `MediaGeoLocation` holds just the decimal-degree scalars.

## Conventions

- **Private fields.** Access via `const fn` getters; mutation via `with_*` builders + `set_*` setters returning `()`.
- **`MediaError`** derives `IsVariant`, `impl core::error::Error`.
- **`MediaDevice`** has a meaningful all-empty default (`new()` + `Default` delegation); **`MediaGeoLocation`** has no `Default` (no meaningful "default GPS reading").
- Module gated on `cfg(any(feature = "std", feature = "alloc"))` (uses `SmolStr` + `jiff::Timestamp` + `mediatime::Timestamp`).
- Tests gated on `cfg(all(test, feature = "std"))`.

## Verification

`cargo hack test --each-feature -Dwarnings` 9/9 green: `--all-features`, `--no-default-features`, `--features alloc | arbitrary | buffa | default | json | quickcheck | std`.

6 new tests cover happy-path, both validation errors, builder chain, in-place setters, MediaDevice empty/builder, MediaGeoLocation builder.

author: guzzzzzzzz
body:
## Fix: backslash in f-string crashes on Python 3.12+

**Fixes:** #2865
**Wallet:** `RTC241359b3438d1222fdc1c3e22fe980657a4bc54e`

### Problem

`miners/linux/rustchain_living_museum.py` uses backslash Unicode escape sequences (`\U0001F980`, `\U0001F3DB`, etc.) directly inside f-string literals. While Python 3.12+ (PEP 701) relaxed f-string restrictions, Python 3.11 and below raise `SyntaxError` for backslash sequences inside f-string expressions, and Python 3.12 emits `DeprecationWarning`.

### Fix

Extract Unicode emoji codepoints into local variables before the f-string, then reference them via `{variable}` inside the expression. This is compatible with all Python versions (3.6+).

**Example:**
```python
# Before (breaks on Python < 3.12)
tweet = f"\U0001F980 HALL OF RUST"

# After (works on all Python versions)
crab = "\U0001F980"
tweet = f"{crab} HALL OF RUST"
```

### Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile miners/linux/rustchain_living_museum.py` → passed
- No behavioral changes — only emoji rendering refactored

body:
## 🖇️ Related Issues * Closes #55 --- ## ✏️ Summary * `ActivitySummary` 공통 컴포넌트 구현 (`shared/ui/activity-summary/`) * `shared/ui/index.ts` barrel export 추가 * HomePage.tsx에 개발용 preview 추가 (머지 전 제거 예정) --- ## 📑 Details ### 왜 공통 컴포넌트로 분리했는가? 현재 서비스에는 아래 화면들에서 동일한 “나의 활동” UI가 반복되고 있었습니다. * 홈 화면 * 재학생 마이페이지 * 졸업생 마이페이지 각 화면은: * title * 카드 레이아웃 * 원형 아이콘 배경 * count * label 구조가 거의 동일했고, 실제 차이는: * 활동 item 개수 * tone 색상 정도만 존재했습니다. 처음에는 단순히: * 아이콘 + 숫자 + label 하나만 공통화할지 고민했지만, 그렇게 되면: * 카드 spacing * border * radius * title layout * item 정렬 을 사용하는 곳마다 다시 조립해야 했습니다. 그래서 이번에는 primitive 수준이 아니라: ```txt “나의 활동 section 전체” ``` 를 reusable presentational component로 분리하는 방향으로 구현했습니다. 즉: ```tsx ``` 하나로 홈 / 마이페이지 케이스를 모두 커버하도록 구조를 정리했습니다. --- ### 1. 컴포넌트 구조 분리 — ActivitySummary / ActivitySummaryItem 카드 전체를 담당하는 `ActivitySummary`와 개별 항목을 담당하는 `ActivitySummaryItem`을 분리했습니다. * `ActivitySummary` * 카드 레이아웃 * title * item 배치 * `ActivitySummaryItem` * icon * count * label * tone 를 담당합니다. 이렇게 분리한 이유는 item 개수가 화면마다 다르기 때문입니다. * 재학생: 커피챗 / 로드맵 / QnA → 3개 * 졸업생: 커피챗 / QnA → 2개 즉 item 배열만 외부에서 주입하면 동일 컴포넌트 구조를 그대로 재사용할 수 있도록 설계했습니다. ```tsx ``` --- ### 2. 아이콘 타입 — ComponentType> 아이콘은 URL 기반 ``가 아니라 React SVG Component를 직접 받도록 설계했습니다. ```ts export type SvgIcon = ComponentType>; ``` ```ts export type ActivitySummaryItemData = { icon: SvgIcon; count: number; label: string; tone: ActivitySummaryTone; }; ``` 선택 이유: * `vite-plugin-svgr`의 `?react` import와 자연스럽게 연결 가능 * Tailwind size utility 직접 적용 가능 * `currentColor` 기반 스타일 상속 가능 * 아이콘 색상을 tone variant와 함께 제어 가능 URL 이미지 방식은: * 색상 변경 * size 통일 * currentColor 상속 이 어렵기 때문에 현재 프로젝트 구조와 맞지 않았습니다. --- ### 3. tone variant — CVA 기반 색상 시스템 아이콘 배경색과 count 색상이 도메인에 따라 달라지므로 CVA variant로 관리했습니다. ```ts export const activitySummaryIconVariants = cva( 'flex items-center justify-center rounded-full w-11 h-11 shrink-0', { variants: { tone: { blue: 'bg-coffee-chat text-white', purple: 'bg-roadmap text-white', pink: 'bg-qna-soft text-qna', }, }, defaultVariants: { tone: 'blue', }, }, ); ``` tone을: * `'blue' | 'purple' | 'pink'` 유니온 타입으로 제한해 잘못된 값 전달을 컴파일 타임에서 방지할 수 있도록 했습니다. 또한 새 도메인 추가 시: * variant 한 줄 추가 만으로 확장이 가능합니다. --- ### 4. 스타일 분리 — activity-summary.styles.ts 프로젝트 기존 컨벤션: * chip.styles.ts * bottom-navigation.styles.ts * modal.styles.ts 과 동일하게 스타일 상수와 variants를 별도 파일로 분리했습니다. 컴포넌트 파일에서는: * JSX 구조 * props 흐름 만 읽히도록 역할을 분리했습니다. --- ### 5. Figma 스펙 기반 고정 사이즈 적용 ```ts export const activitySummaryContainer = 'w-[302px] h-[135px] bg-surface border border-border-light rounded-card shadow-card flex flex-col items-center pt-4'; ``` Figma 디자인 기준: * width: 302px * height: 135px 를 그대로 반영했습니다. 현재 프로젝트는: * 모바일 고정 레이아웃 * max-w-[430px] * Figma 1:1 구현 지향 구조이기 때문에 임의의 responsive width보다 고정값이 실제 디자인 일치 측면에서 더 적절하다고 판단했습니다. --- ### 6. Typography hierarchy 정리 Figma 기준 typography hierarchy를 그대로 반영했습니다. * title (`나의 활동`) * 10px * label (`커피챗`, `로드맵`, `QnA`) * 10px * count (`12`, `5`) * 15px * font-weight 강화 count가 시각적으로 가장 먼저 들어오도록 hierarchy를 조정했습니다. --- ### 7. 접근성 처리 시각적으로는: * icon * count * label 이 분리되어 있지만, 스크린리더에서는 하나의 정보로 읽히는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그래서 item 단위에: ```tsx role="img" aria-label={`${label} ${count}개`} ``` 를 부여하고 내부 요소는: ```tsx aria-hidden="true" ``` 처리했습니다. ```tsx

{count}

{label}
``` 이렇게 하면: ```txt "커피챗 12개" ``` 처럼 자연스럽게 읽힙니다. --- ### 8. Barrel export 정리 ```ts export { ActivitySummary } from './activity-summary'; export type { ActivitySummaryProps, ActivitySummaryItemData, ActivitySummaryTone, SvgIcon, } from './activity-summary'; ``` 컴포넌트뿐 아니라 타입도 함께 export하도록 정리했습니다. 특히 `SvgIcon` 타입은: * item 배열을 외부에서 미리 선언할 때 타입 안정성 확보에 필요하다고 판단해 함께 export했습니다. --- ### 9. HomePage preview 추가 실제 서비스 적용 전: * 3개 item 케이스 * 2개 item 케이스 를 빠르게 검증할 수 있도록 preview를 추가했습니다. 포함 케이스: * 홈 화면 스타일 * 졸업생 마이페이지 스타일 ※ preview 코드는 머지 전 제거 예정입니다. --- ## 📸 Screenshots 스크린샷 첨부 예정 --- ## 🔖 Etc * tone 색상은 theme.css 기반 semantic color 사용 * 현재 ActivitySummary는 purely presentational component * API / routing / role 분기 로직은 포함하지 않음 * item 개수 차이는 props 기반으로 처리 * ActivitySummaryItem은 우선 내부 컴포넌트로 유지 * 단독 재사용 필요 시 export 여부를 추후 검토 예정 ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **새로운 기능** * 활동 요약 컴포넌트 추가 * 활동을 그리드로 시각화하여 각 항목에 아이콘, 수치, 레이블을 표시 * 파란색·보라색·분홍색 색상 변형 제공 * 기본 제목은 '나의 활동'이며 제목·스타일 커스터마이즈 가능 * 화면읽기 지원을 위한 접근성 레이블 포함 [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/MJU-Capstone-4/ddingconnect-frontend/pull/56?utm_source=github_walkthrough&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=change_stack)

author: humurabbi
body:
## Summary

- **Site Map visibility for sent requests**: `send_http1_request` and `send_http2_request` route through `api.http().sendRequest()`, which bypasses Burp's proxy. Without intervention, MCP-issued requests are invisible to the user — Proxy History is read-only to extensions, and the existing `logToOutput` line only records `host:port`. Each tool now calls `api.siteMap().add(response)` after a successful send so the request/response pair shows up under Target > Site map.
- **Newline normalization in `create_repeater_tab`**: callers (LLMs in particular) often pass content with bare LF line terminators. The existing code forwarded that straight to `HttpRequest.httpRequest`, producing a garbled request in the Repeater tab that had to be hand-corrected. `create_repeater_tab` now applies the same `\n` → `\r\n` normalization that `send_http1_request` already uses (`Tools.kt:58`).
- No new tools, no API surface changes, no removed parameters.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew test` passes (16 tests in `ToolsKtTest`)
- [x] `verify { api.siteMap().add(httpResponse) }` on the success path of both `send_http1_request` and `send_http2_request`
- [x] `verify(exactly = 0) { api.siteMap().add(any()) }` when `sendRequest` returns null (no spurious site-map entries on connection failure)
- [x] New `create repeater tab should normalize line endings` test asserts LF-only input is rewritten to CRLF before reaching Repeater

## Manual verification

- Issued an HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 request via the MCP against an in-scope host; both appeared under Target > Site map with full request/response, where previously nothing was visible.
- Created a Repeater tab with content containing only `\n` line breaks; the resulting tab renders cleanly without manually re-entering carriage returns.

author: jianmosier
