author: wxwxwwxxx
body:
## Purpose

Fix AutoRound-quantized Gemma4 MoE checkpoints so they can load and generate valid text in vLLM.

This PR fixes several issues found while serving Gemma4 MoE AutoRound checkpoints:

- Pass `quant_config` into Gemma4 router `GateLinear`, so quantized router weights such as `router.proj.qweight` are registered and loaded correctly.
- Use the actual MoE activation in WNA16 fused experts instead of assuming SiLU; Gemma4 MoE uses `gelu_tanh`.
- Allocate GPTQ `scales`/`qzeros` rows with ceil division when `input_size` is not divisible by `group_size`, avoiding silently dropped tail groups.
- Mirror `k_proj` quant config to `v_proj` for Gemma4 `attention_k_eq_v` full-attention layers, so fused `qkv_proj` sees consistent quant settings for AutoRound mixed-bit checkpoints.

Duplicate-work check: I checked related open PR searches for `Gemma4 AutoRound`, `Gemma4 MoE quantization`, `AutoRound quantization`, and `k_eq_v quant config`. I did not find an open PR that covers this exact fix set. 

## Test Plan

Commands/checks used:

```bash
vllm serve Intel/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-int4-AutoRound 
vllm serve Intel/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-int4-mixed-AutoRound
```

Both servers were queried through /v1/chat/completions with a simple  prompt.

## Test Result

Pure int4 AutoRound Gemma4 MoE checkpoint: server loaded successfully and returned normal text.
Mixed AutoRound Gemma4 MoE checkpoint: server loaded successfully and returned normal text.

### Before this fix:

The pure int4 AutoRound checkpoint failed during loading because the Gemma4 router projection did not register quantized weights.
After partial loading fixes, generation could become corrupted because the GPTQ tail group scales/qzeros were truncated.
The mixed AutoRound checkpoint failed on fused qkv_proj because attention_k_eq_v layers duplicated K weights into V but did not mirror the per-layer quant config.

### After this fix:

Both tested AutoRound Gemma4 MoE checkpoints load.
Both produce readable, coherent responses in the local serving path.

## Summary

`SALT` / `ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` only as
`additionalEnv`, which feeds them to the runtime pod env but does

`auth.existingSecret` or inline password.

**Result**: every CI run since #11796 merged fails `helm template`
on this chart. Verified blocking [#11799](https://github.com/rwlove/home-ops/pull/11799)
(my SparkOllamaWedged tune),
[#11800](https://github.com/rwlove/home-ops/pull/11800)
(langgraph stale-paused alert), and would block any future PR
cluster-wide.

**Runtime impact**: zero. `kubectl get hr -n ai langfuse` returns
NotFound — Flux hits the same render failure CI does, so the
HelmRelease was never installed. This PR makes the render succeed;
Flux can then attempt install, but it'll wait on the follow-up
(ExternalSecret extension) before it actually starts pods.

## Changes (helmrelease values)

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `langfuse.salt` unset → chart aborts | `secretKeyRef: langfuse-secret/SALT` |
| `langfuse.encryptionKey` unset → chart aborts | `secretKeyRef: langfuse-secret/ENCRYPTION_KEY` |
| `langfuse.nextauth.secret` unset → chart aborts | `secretKeyRef: langfuse-secret/NEXTAUTH_SECRET` |
| `langfuse.nextauth.url` unset (default `http://localhost:3000`) | `https://langfuse.${SECRET_DOMAIN}` |
| `additionalEnv[TELEMETRY_ENABLED]` (chart aborts when mixed with new structure) | `langfuse.features.telemetryEnabled: false` |
| `clickhouse.auth` unset → chart aborts | `existingSecret: langfuse-secret`, key `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` |
| `redis.auth` unset → chart aborts | `existingSecret: langfuse-secret`, key `REDIS_PASSWORD` |
| `s3.auth` unset → chart aborts | `existingSecret: langfuse-secret`, keys `S3_ROOT_USER` + `S3_ROOT_PASSWORD` |

Dropped from `additionalEnv` (chart re-injects them via its own
templates now that the values-side refs are set):
`NEXTAUTH_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `SALT`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

`DATABASE_URL` and the `LANGFUSE_INIT_*` bootstrap fields stay in
`additionalEnv` — DATABASE_URL because the CNPG `uri` carries the
full DSN (the chart's `postgresql.auth.existingSecret` path only
plumbs username + password); `LANGFUSE_INIT_*` because the chart
has no native value paths for first-boot bootstrap.

## Verified locally

```sh
helm template lf-test ai-langfuse/langfuse --version 1.5.31 \\
    --values <rendered helmrelease.yaml values>
# → 2072 lines of manifests, 0 errors
```

## Follow-up (operator, before Flux can install)

The `langfuse` ExternalSecret must be extended to materialize the
new keys (`CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`, `REDIS_PASSWORD`, `S3_ROOT_USER`,
`S3_ROOT_PASSWORD`), and the 1P item `langfuse-app` needs those
fields populated. CI passes without that step because `helm
template` doesn't validate secret-key existence — only structure.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on `Extract images` + `Flux Local Test` + `Flux Local Diff`
- [ ] Once merged: `gh pr update-branch` on #11799 + #11800; both
      should clear their CI

### What is the new feature?
Allows mods to modify the amount of potions and hearts dropped from a boss loot (#5135).
### Why should this be part of tModLoader?
Currently mods need to workaround the current implementation to be able to specify the amount of hearts and potions dropped by a boss when killed, that usually causes buggy behavior or unexpected side effects.
### Are there alternative designs?
Instead of dropping a amount of single hearts, it could be just a one or a few hearts with a more dense stack.
### Sample usage for the new feature
```C#
public override void BossLoot(ref int potionType, ref int potionStack, ref int heartStack) {
	potionStack = 50;
	heartStack = 99;
}
```
### ExampleMod updates
Incremented the BossLoot comment to cover the new feature at the MinionBossBody Class

### Porting Notes
It should work as it is. The feature shouldn't affect existing mods.

author: jitsusama
body:
## What this does

Adds the missing confirmation gate for `action=post`.
Renders the event type, finding counts, the
generated review body and a per-finding listing
before shipping anything to GitHub.

## Why it matters

Phase 1 of end-to-end testing lost a real review
because `action=post` posted immediately. The user
asked to see the gate to cancel; there wasn't one.
This was the loudest P0 from observations.md after
state persistence and the fix worktree.

## How it works

Mirrors the reply/resolve split exactly:

| Module | Job |
|---|---|
| `post-gate-render.ts` | Pure content renderer |
| `post-gate-outcome.ts` | Pure outcome reducer |
| `post-gate.ts` | Interactive shell (`promptSingle`) |

`postReviewAction` gains an optional `gate` dep.
When supplied, it:

1. Builds the payload via `buildReviewPayload` (no
   change).
2. Constructs a structured `PostGateSummary` from
   the payload — finding ids resolved from
   `lastJudge.consolidatedFindings` and
   `state.stackCritic.findings` so the user sees
   subject + location for every finding about to
   post.
3. Calls the gate. Rejected outcomes short-circuit
   with the gate's reason. Approved outcomes can
   override the body (Shift+Escape redirect).
4. Invokes `exec` with the final body.

`index.ts` wires the production gate via
`confirmPostGate(ctx, summary)`. Headless context
(`ctx.hasUI === false`) short-circuits to approved
with the body unchanged, matching reply/resolve.

Shift+Enter steering annotations propagate through
as `User annotated: <note>` rejections so the
agent's next turn sees the steering signal. Same
treatment as the reply / resolve gates landed in
the previous bundle.

## Tests

- `post-gate-render.test.ts` (new, 7): event header,
  count line, body verbatim, per-finding listing,
  cross-PR + skipped counts surface when non-zero
  and hide when zero, APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES
  render distinctly.
- `post-gate-outcome.test.ts` (new, 6): null cancels,
  `r` rejects, annotation steers, redirect overrides
  body, empty redirect refuses, fallthrough approves.
- `post.test.ts` (3 new tests on `postReviewAction`):
  gate receives the structured summary, rejection
  short-circuits without calling `exec`, approved
  edited body lands as the posted body.

471 tests passing. Lint + typecheck clean.
Mutation-tested: gutting the rejection branch
cracks the integration test.

## Self-review

- Backward-compatible: `gate` is optional. The 20
  pre-existing post tests continue to call
  `postReviewAction` without a gate and pass
  unchanged.
- No new persisted state; nothing crosses the
  `/reload` boundary.
- The pure render/outcome split lets tests exercise
  the layout and state machine without dragging in
  the TUI runtime, matching the
  `thread-gate-render` / `thread-gate-outcome`
  pattern from PR #194.

author: medelman17
body:
## Summary

Closes #557. `extractShortForms.ts:193` had `/[.;)\]—:]$/.test(trimmed)` as the sole gate for "is this a citation context?" — and a 20-char lookback window. Bluebook signal phrases either end on alphabetic chars (`See`, `See also`, `Compare`, etc.) or on a comma (`See, e.g.,`), so signal-prefixed `Id.` cites failed the gate and were clamped to confidence 0.4. The 20-char window also hid the punctuation case after a real prior citation: `"... (1974). See id."` — the `)` and `.` exist but lie outside the window.

**Sub-finding (not in the issue):** `Cf. id.` actually escapes the bug today because `.` in `Cf.` is the last non-whitespace char. The bug fires for `See`, `See also`, `Compare`, `Accord`, `Contra`, `See generally`, `But see`, `See, e.g.`, `E.g.`, `But see, e.g.`, `See also, e.g.` — and dodges for `Cf.`, `But cf.`, `Cf., e.g.`. Still a majority of signals broken.

## Fix

Augmented the context check with a second predicate — `SIGNAL_AT_END_REGEX`, a module-level regex mirroring `SIGNAL_PATTERNS` from `src/extract/detectStringCites.ts`. Matches any Bluebook signal phrase anchored at end-of-string with a non-letter boundary before (`(?<![A-Za-z])`) so `He see` doesn't match. Window bumped 20 → 60 chars to fit `See also, e.g.` plus surrounding content. Existing `"The Id. card"` / `"His Id."` protection preserved (no signal match, no punctuation match → still 0.4).

## Test plan

- [x] 17 new tests in `tests/extract/idConfidence.test.ts` under `"citation signal context (#557)"` — 11 canonical (`See Id.` → 1.0) + 6 lowercase (`See id.` → 0.85) + 2 prior-citation-then-signal regressions
- [x] All 17 went red on main, green after fix
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run` — 3288 passed (+17), 9 skipped
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean

author: adhithyan15
body:
## Summary

Two Python-vs-SQLite divergences uncovered by a scalar function gap audit:

1. **`REPLACE(x, "", y)`**: Python's `str.replace("", X)` inserts X between every character → `'XhXeXlXlXoX'`. SQLite treats empty needle as no-op → `'hello'`. One-line fix.

2. **`printf('%#o', val)`**: Python uses modern `0o` prefix; SQLite uses C-style `0` prefix. Plus three subtleties:
   - Zero value omits prefix: `printf('%#o', 0) → '0'`
   - Width: prefix sits after leading spaces — `printf('%#5o', 8) → '  010'`
   - Zero-padded width grows by prefix length — `printf('%#05o', 8) → '000010'`

29 new tests (20 sql-vm unit + 9 mini-sqlite oracle), all comparing byte-for-byte against reference sqlite3. Version bumps: sql-vm 1.38.0 → 1.39.0, mini-sqlite 1.64.0 → 1.65.0.

author: iskhakovt
body:
## Summary

Adds a `p3` todo entry under *Skills, voice & transport* tracking an attachment-store compression layer (zstd-1 via `node:zlib`, magic-byte dispatch on read).

Doc-only — captures the design and ship trigger after researching industry practice on object-store compression. The pattern mirrors `wrapAttachmentStoreWithEncryption`'s magic-byte convergence trick so pre-wrap blobs stay readable.

## Why now (as a todo, not a PR)

- **zstd-1's incompressible behavior is the key property** — it emits raw blocks at near-memcpy throughput with ~13-20 bytes of frame overhead. Applying uniformly is effectively free when the payload can't compress; 40-80% wins on text.
- **`node:zlib` ships it natively as of Node 22.15** — no new dependency.
- **Compose order matters** — `compress → encrypt → s3`, never the reverse. Encrypting compressed data is fine; compressing encrypted data is ~0% useful AND opens the CRIME-class side channel that per-blob streams currently avoid.
- **But the today-mix likely yields zero savings** — should measure the actual attachment shape before adding a layer. Until a text-shaped ingestion path (MCP Gmail/Calendar, RAG-over-PDFs) arrives, the layer would be dead weight.

## Test plan

- [ ] No code changes — single bullet in `todo.md`.
- [ ] Verify the entry is informative enough that whoever picks it up has the shape, compose order, and ship trigger without re-doing the research.

body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
The `RDFStore::add_rdf` method used `.unwrap()` on the result of `Store::load_graph`, causing an uncontrolled panic when parsing invalid RDF data (e.g., malformed Turtle syntax).

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
An attacker (or user providing malformed input) could cause the CLI application to crash abruptly, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). While less severe in a local CLI context, it remains a serious reliability issue.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Refactored `add_rdf` to return an `anyhow::Result<()>`, allowing the error from `load_graph` to be safely propagated using the `?` operator. Updated `src/main.rs`, `src/demo.rs`, and tests to handle the returned `Result`. Replaced other unsafe `.expect()` calls in `main.rs` with `.map_err()` and `?`. Also addressed related code quality warnings (e.g., `Default` traits, `dead_code` warnings via explicit module inclusion in binary tests).

`````
## v0.4.0 — Migration to package extensions

This release migrates third-party integrations from `Requires.jl` to native Julia
package extensions (Julia ≥ 1.9), addressing JOSS review feedback in
openjournals/joss-reviews#9989.

### Breaking changes

- **Minimum Julia version is now 1.10** (was previously ≥ 1.6). Package
  extensions require Julia ≥ 1.9; CI is run on 1.10/1.11/1.12.
- `Requires.jl` is no longer a (transitive) dependency. Downstream packages
  that imported `AlgebraicAgents` purely for the side-effect of loading
  `Requires` will need to depend on `Requires.jl` directly.
- The `@integration` macro and the helper `add_integration_to_path` (the
  Requires-era mechanism for registering ad-hoc integrations) have been
  removed. Use Julia's native package-extension machinery (declare
  `[weakdeps]` + `[extensions]` in your downstream package's `Project.toml`)
  instead.

### Non-breaking

- **No user-facing API change for the integrations themselves.**
  `using DifferentialEquations`, `using Agents`, or `using AlgebraicDynamics`
  continues to enable the corresponding integration automatically — now via
  Pkg's native extension machinery instead of `Requires.jl`'s runtime hooks.
- Integration types (`DiffEqAgent`, `ABMAgent`/`AAgent`, `GraphicalAgent`)
  remain exported from the main module so they can be referenced as field
  types or in dispatch even before the third-party package is loaded.
- New documentation section explaining the extension loading mechanism

author: therudywolf
body:
## Problem
keen-pbr restarted the system `dnsmasq` in full on every reload / activate / deactivate, even when the generated resolver config had not changed. A full restart is a multi-second window with no DNS service — on weak routers users see intermittent DNS failures whenever keen-pbr reloads (config edits, list refreshes, etc.).

## Change
Before performing the restart, the helper scripts fingerprint (`md5sum`) the **effective** dnsmasq config they would produce (active resolver config when active, fallback line when inactive) and compare it with the fingerprint stored from the previous run. If it is unchanged **and** dnsmasq is already running, the restart is skipped and an info line is logged instead. The first run, content changes, and activate/deactivate transitions all restart normally.

Applied consistently to the Keenetic, OpenWrt and Debian helper scripts.

## Testing
Shell-only change; POSIX sh / busybox-ash compatible. Backend test suite unaffected and green. Verified on a Keenetic KN-1011.

author: thorwhalen
body:
Implements **Phase 3** of the `ef` refactor (roadmap `.claude/CLAUDE.md` §8) — layer **L0**, the corpus (source) layer and content-based change detection. Closes #6; follows Phase 1 (#2/#3) and Phase 2 (#4/#5).

## What this adds

### `ef/corpus.py` — the corpus facade
- **`Source` / `Corpus`** — type aliases. A corpus is just a `MutableMapping[source_id, Source]`; no new class is needed (any `dol` store *is* a corpus).
- **`content_hash(source, *, content_keys=None)`** — the content hash that drives change detection. Normalize-then-SHA-256. For a structured `Mapping` source it hashes **text only** — a title/tag/ACL edit produces the same hash, so it never triggers a spurious re-embed (design notes §3.2, use-case C6). `content_keys` opts specific metadata keys into the hash for the rare case where metadata genuinely feeds downstream.
- **`as_corpus(x, ...)`** — the dependency-injection seam, parallel to `as_embedder`/`as_segmenter`: `None`→RAM dict; `Mapping`→passthrough; directory path→`dol` filesystem store (`dol` lazily imported); iterable of sources→content-addressed RAM dict.
- **`ChangeDetectingCorpus`** — a transparent `MutableMapping` wrapper. Hooks `__setitem__`/`__delitem__` and fires a `ChangeEvent` via an injected `on_change` callback **only on a real content change** (identical writes are idempotent no-ops). `diff()` (pure) and `scan()` (effectful) reconcile **out-of-band** edits made directly to the backing store. An optional injectable `fingerprint` callback is an mtime/etag prefilter — a `scan()` speed optimization; the content hash always stays authoritative.
- `ChangeEvent` / `CorpusDiff` — frozen, JSON-friendly dataclasses.

The `on_change` callback is the seam the Phase 4 `ArtifactGraph` plugs into — a `"modified"`/`"deleted"` event is exactly the trigger for a cascade.

### `ef/hashing.py` — new shared SSOT
`normalize_text` / `canonical_json` / `sha256_hex`, extracted from `segments.py`'s private helpers so `segment_id` (L2) and `content_hash` (L0) — and Phase 4's artifact ids — all content-address through one normalization. `segment_id` is unchanged in behavior (the private `_normalize_text`/`_canonical_json` are gone; tests covering `segment_id` still pass).

### Dependencies
`dol` and `i2` promoted from extras to **core dependencies** — the architecture rests on `dol` for every store, and `i2` is needed from Phase 4 on for call-hashing.

## Decisions (settled with the user)
1. `content_hash` is **text-only by default** with a `content_keys` opt-in.
2. The **mtime/etag prefilter hook is included now** (injectable `fingerprint`); watchers/CDC watermarks remain Phase 6.
3. One extra small module — `ef/hashing.py` — beyond the issue's "one new module", justified as the content-hashing SSOT (Phase 4 needs it too).

## Tests
- `tests/test_corpus.py` — 34 offline tests: hash determinism/normalization, `content_keys` semantics, `as_corpus` branches, through-the-wrapper events + idempotency, `diff`/`scan` out-of-band reconciliation, the prefilter (incl. "a fingerprint change alone never declares a change"), and an end-to-end real-filesystem scenario.
- Full suite green locally: `pytest tests/` → 111 passed; `pytest` (doctests in `ef/`) → 65 passed. `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean.

Refs #2, #4.

author: appsecai-app[bot]
body:
## TL;DR

Replaced SHA-1 with SHA-256 in the cryptographic hash computation at line 56 of `BenchmarkTest02042.java`. SHA-1 is cryptographically broken and susceptible to collision attacks; SHA-256 is the industry-standard replacement and provides 128-bit collision resistance.

## What SAST Found

The static analysis scanner detected use of SHA-1 via `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA1", "SUN")` at line 56 in `src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest02042.java`. SHA-1 is flagged as a weak cryptographic algorithm unsuitable for security-sensitive hashing operations.

## Why this Matters

SHA-1 has been cryptographically broken since 2017 (SHAttered collision attack). The algorithm no longer provides collision resistance, meaning an attacker can craft two different inputs that produce the same SHA-1 hash. In this codebase, the hash output is written to `passwordFile.txt` (lines 74–83), indicating a security-sensitive storage context. An attacker who can control the input to the servlet endpoint `/hash-02/BenchmarkTest02042` (reachable on every HTTP GET/POST request) could exploit SHA-1 collisions to forge hash values or bypass integrity checks that depend on the hash.

SHA-256 is NIST-approved (FIPS 180-4), collision-resistant to 2^128 work, and is the standard replacement for SHA-1 in integrity and fingerprinting use cases.

## How We Confirmed It (and how you can too)

### Manual Verification Steps

1. Locate the vulnerable line in the source file:
 ```bash
   grep -n "MessageDigest.getInstance" src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest02042.java
   ```
 Confirm that line 56 contains the SHA-1 algorithm string.

2. Verify the fix has been applied:
 ```bash
   grep -n "SHA-256" src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest02042.java
   ```
 Confirm that line 56 now references SHA-256 instead of SHA-1.

3. Compile the patched code to ensure no syntax errors:
 ```bash
   mvn clean compile
   ```

4. Run the existing test suite to confirm no functional regression:
 ```bash
   mvn test
   ```

### Vulnerability Flow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["HTTP Request to /hash-02/BenchmarkTest02042"] --> B["URLDecoder.decode extracts parameter"]
        B --> C["doSomething processes input"]
        C --> D{"Algorithm Choice"}
    D -->|"SHA-1 (Vulnerable)"| E["MessageDigest.getInstance SHA-1"]
        D -->|"SHA-256 (Fixed)"| F["MessageDigest.getInstance SHA-256"]
        E --> G["Compute hash digest"]
        F --> H["Compute hash digest"]
        G --> I["Write to passwordFile.txt"]
        H --> J["Write to passwordFile.txt"]
        I --> K["⚠️ Collision attack possible with SHA-1"]
        J --> L["✅ Collision resistant with SHA-256"]
```

<details>
<summary>Runnable Verification Script (click to expand)</summary>

Save this script and run with `bash verify_fix.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Verification script for CWE-328 fix in BenchmarkTest02042.java
set -e

echo "=== Verification: Weak Hash Algorithm (CWE-328) Fix ==="

# Step 1: Verify the vulnerable line has been replaced
echo "Step 1: Checking that SHA-1 has been replaced with SHA-256..."
if grep -q 'MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256"' src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest02042.java; then
    echo "✓ SHA-256 found in MessageDigest.getInstance call"
else
    echo "✗ SHA-256 not found; fix may not be applied"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 2: Verify no SHA-1 references remain in the vulnerable context
echo "Step 2: Confirming SHA-1 has been removed from the hash computation..."
if ! grep -q 'MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-1"' src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest02042.java; then
    echo "✓ SHA-1 algorithm reference removed"
else
    echo "✗ SHA-1 still present in the file"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 3: Verify the provider argument remains unchanged
echo "Step 3: Verifying SUN provider is still specified..."
if grep -q 'MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256", "SUN")' src/main/java/org/owasp/benchmark/testcode/BenchmarkTest02042.java; then
    echo "✓ SUN provider correctly specified with SHA-256"
else
    echo "✗ Provider argument may have been altered"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 4: Compile the patched code
echo "Step 4: Compiling patched code..."
if mvn clean compile -q; then
    echo "✓ Code compiles successfully"
else
    echo "✗ Compilation failed"
    exit 1
fi

# Step 5: Run tests to confirm no functional regression
echo "Step 5: Running test suite..."
if mvn test -q; then
    echo "✓ All tests pass"
else
    echo "✗ Tests failed; possible functional regression"
    exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "=== All verification checks passed ==="
```

</details>

## How We Fixed It

Replaced the algorithm string in the `MessageDigest.getInstance()` call at line 56:

**Before:**
```java
MessageDigest md = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA1", "SUN");
```

**After:**
```java
MessageDigest md = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256", "SUN");
```

This is a minimal, one-token substitution. The `MessageDigest` API, provider (`"SUN"`), and all downstream byte-array handling (update, digest, Base64 encoding) remain identical. The fix eliminates the weak primitive without altering any program behavior beyond the cryptographic algorithm used.

## Next Steps

1. **Review and merge** this PR to replace SHA-1 with SHA-256.
2. **Redeploy** the application to production to ensure all new hash computations use SHA-256.
3. **Legacy data handling**: Existing hashes stored in `passwordFile.txt` that were computed with SHA-1 will remain unchanged. If those hashes are used for integrity verification or comparison, consider a migration strategy:
 - If the original plaintext is available, recompute and store SHA-256 hashes.
 - If plaintext is not available, maintain a mapping of old SHA-1 hashes for backward compatibility during a transition period, then deprecate.
4. **Monitor** for any issues related to hash format changes in downstream systems that consume `passwordFile.txt`.

## Confidence breakdown

- **Decision confidence:** 1.00 (0.95-1.00)
- **Evidence quality:** high
- **Ensemble agreement:** 2/2
- **Reachability:** REACHABLE (0.98)
- **Supporting evidence:** Line 56 unconditionally instantiates MessageDigest with the string literal 'SHA1' — weak primitive hardcoded, not configurable; SHA1 is cryptographically broken: collision attacks demonstrated (SHAttered, 2017); unsuitable for security-sensitive hashing; Hash output written to passwordFile.txt (line 74-83), indicating security-sensitive storage context, not a non-security fingerprint

author: xcid
body:
## Summary

Two changes to lower the per-round cost of the background poll loop against the Hub.

### 1. `reqwest::Client` tuning (`hub_api.rs:make_clients`)

The control-plane and HEAD clients were built with defaults. Concrete impact:
- Idle pool defaulted to 32 per host. Polling many prefixes in parallel against `huggingface.co` re-TLS-handshakes once we go above 32 in-flight.
- No request timeout. A hung Hub never resolves, so the `tokio::time::sleep(interval)` next iteration never starts and the poll loop is dead forever.

Set:
- `pool_max_idle_per_host(128)` / `64` (control / head)
- `pool_idle_timeout(90s)`
- `tcp_keepalive(60s)`
- `connect_timeout(10s)`
- `timeout(60s / 30s)`

### 2. `probe_revision()` to skip unchanged polls

New trait method on `HubOps`. Returns an opaque token: commit head `sha` for repos, `updatedAt` for buckets. The poll loop calls it once per round and skips the full tree-listing fan-out when the token matches the previous round.

For idle mounts (the common case), per-round cost goes from N tree-listing requests to 1 metadata request. For active mounts there is one extra metadata request per round; with the new pool tuning this stays on the keep-alive connection.

Failure handling:
- Probe error -> fall through to full fan-out (probe is an optimization, not a gate).
- Probe 401 -> bumps the existing `auth_backoff_exp` and skips the round (same behaviour the per-prefix listings already had).
- `Ok(None)` -> source doesn't expose a token (default trait impl); always fan out. Mocks pick this up.

### Out of scope (will follow in separate PRs)

From `TODO.md`:
- Per-prefix backoff on persistent 5xx
- Separate download client from control-plane pool
- Lock-free `auth()` cache, retry jitter
- `Arc<QueryReconstructionResponseV2>` on CAS cache
- `Arc<str>` cleanup across VFS hot paths

body:
## Summary

Fourth "quick deterministic win." Two clues carried numeric dates that fight their actual span — the same class as the mortise-and-tenon fix (PR #77):

- **`dowel_joinery`** was dated `post-1900` (inline + canonical notes). But the LLM emits this key for hand-pegged/drawbored mortise-and-tenon *as well as* modern machine doweling, so the hard floor falsely late-dated plainly Victorian pieces (in scan 2, the only numeric construction anchor floored an Eastlake chair at 1900). The canonical `joinery_alone_never_dates_furniture` meta-rule already states joinery alone shouldn't date a piece.
- **`barley_twist`** was dated `Jacobean Revival c. 1890–1935`, but spiral/barley-twist turning spans Baroque originals, Jacobean Revival, *and* Victorian Renaissance/Baroque Revival; the narrow window conflicted with genuine 1860–1900 Renaissance Revival readings (scan 4).

## Changes

- `lib/engineClueResolver.ts` — add `joinery_type_dowel_joinery` to `PERSISTENT_NONDATING_CANONICAL_IDS`.
- `lib/engine.ts` — change the inline `CLUE_LIBRARY` `dateHint` for both `dowel_joinery` and `barley_twist` to prose (necessary because the tighter-of-{canonical, inline} merge would otherwise re-pick the numeric inline hint).
- `scripts/trace.ts` — `victorian_chair_pegged_dowel` and `rr_barley_twist` fixtures.

## Verification

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] `dowel_joinery` joinery dating-overlap band: **`1900-null` → undated** (spurious post-1900 floor removed).
- [x] `barley_twist` weighted-clue `date_hint`: numeric → prose (no Jacobean band injected).
- [x] **Zero impact on all 257 existing fixtures** — neither clue appears in the corpus, so there is no regression surface; the two new fixtures document the clue/layer-level change.

## Honest scope note

These fixtures demonstrate the fix at the **clue/layer level** (the bad numeric band is gone). They do **not** reproduce a headline frame-date *change*, because the late-dating seen in real scans 2 and 4 flows through the **convergence/style-wave machinery** — when `dowel_joinery` was the binding floor inside a multi-layer convergence, or `barley_twist` stretched the style-wave envelope. Removing the bad band is the prerequisite that stops those paths from binding to a wrong date; fully exercising that interaction belongs to the separate convergence-authority work (the broad-layer over-counting issue). This PR is the correct, low-risk data fix underneath it.

body:
## Summary

Ports production-grade gas accounting into `EvmPrecompileStorageProvider` (ported from Tempo), fixing every storage operation that was previously free.

- **SLOAD**: warm (100) / cold (2100) per EIP-2929
- **SSTORE**: static (100) + cold penalty + EIP-2200 net-metering + EIP-3529 refunds
- **TLOAD / TSTORE**: flat 100 gas per EIP-1153
- **with_account_info**: warm (100) / cold (2600) per EIP-2929
- **emit_event**: LOG base (375) + per-topic + per-byte gas
- **set_code**: code deposit (200/byte) + CREATE base (32,000) + keccak256 for new accounts
- **keccak256**: 30 + 6/word (was already charged, unchanged)

Additional correctness fixes discovered during the audit:

- `sstore` / `tstore` / `emit_event` now reject STATICCALL invocations (`StaticCallViolation` revert) — `EvmInternals` has no static guard so this must live in the precompile layer
- `success_output()` now populates `PrecompileOutput.gas_refunded` so SSTORE refunds reach the EVM's transaction-level refund counter where the EIP-3529 cap is applied
- `GasTracker`: ported from Tempo then replaced with `revm::interpreter::Gas` (already available in revm 34, no new dependency)
- `deduct_state_gas` removed — unused, no implementation possible until GasParams upgrades to context-interface v17 (Amsterdam)

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo build -p base-precompile-storage` — clean build
- [ ] `cargo test -p base-precompile-storage --features test-utils` — all tests pass
- [ ] Devnet token deployment smoke test — token factory creates tokens, gas is charged

body:
## Summary

- Adds `"x-adcp-hoist": true` to `data-provider-signal-selector.json` so the bundler deduplicates it via root `$defs` instead of inlining it N times
- Adds a regression test covering the discriminated `oneOf` dedup case (the exact pattern that triggered the bug)
- Adds a patch changeset

## Problem

In 3.1.0-beta.x, `tasks-get-response.json` gained a `result` field referencing `async-response-data.json` — a union of all task response schemas. When bundled, `data-provider-signal-selector.json` (a 3-branch discriminated `oneOf` with `selection_type` values `all`, `by_id`, `by_tag`) appeared twice in the same bundled file. `datamodel-code-generator` 0.56.1 fabricated a `Literal['reuse']` discriminator value, raising:

```
TypeError: Value 'reuse' for discriminator 'selection_type' mapped to multiple choices
```

This blocked the entire Python SDK from importing.

## Fix

Mark the schema `x-adcp-hoist: true`. The bundler's existing `hoistMarkedSchemas()` function moves it to root `$defs.DataProviderSignalSelector` and replaces all inline occurrences with `{"$ref": "#/$defs/DataProviderSignalSelector"}`. The directive is stripped from bundled output — wire contract is unchanged.

Verified: `DataProviderSignalSelector` appears once in `$defs` with `discriminator` + `oneOf` intact and `x-adcp-hoist` absent.

- [x] `npm run build:schemas` — 0 failures, 83 schemas bundled

- [x] Protocol expert review — confirmed semantically equivalent under JSON Schema draft-07; no wire contract change
- [x] Code reviewer — approved; no blockers

author: jmsbpp
body:
## What this is

The **E10 GSPS** iteration — Generalized Subscription Payment Stream: a convex
(volatility, not directional) FX-volatility hedge for a Web3 data-analyst cohort
that pays continuously for data access. The cost stream is `Q × $0.01 × FX`; the
hedged risk is the *volatility* of the local-currency cost. Descriptive
sensitivity-surface posture — **no inferential β claim**. E10 is the methods-paper
§5 anchor (convex / cost-side generalization of the streamed-liability primitive).

## The workflow this PR captures

A full disciplined `brainstorm → spec → plan → execute` cycle:

1. **Brainstorm** — discovered E10 already existed as a v0.1 spec; reframed it
   (directional → convex; Colombia-only → multi-currency) with the user.
2. **Spec v0.1 → v0.6** — six visible `CORRECTIONS` blocks, every pivot recorded:
   v0.2 convex reframe → v0.3 review-driven → v0.4 demoted to descriptive
   (G≈8 underpowered) → v0.5 HALT-DV re-spec to 5 currencies → v0.6 folds the
   two converged post-HALT reviewer recommendations. Each version 2-way reviewed
   (Reality Checker + Model QA Specialist).
3. **Implementation plan** — code-agnostic, 7 phases, every task tagged
   `[brainstorm-judgment]` / `[mechanical-execution]`; 2-way reviewed.
4. **Execution (subagent-driven)** — Phase 0 + Phase 1, each gated by a two-stage
   (spec-compliance + code-quality) review.

## What's done

- **Phase 0** — `simulations/e10_gsps/` three-tier scaffold + 3 mechanically-verified
  firewalls (Stage-2 / fantasy / descriptive-posture) + RED test harnesses.
- **Phase 1 (E10.0)** — 5-currency central-bank FX ingest (COP/BRL/EUR/GBP/NGN),
  regime-break screen, panel-window deliverable (~150 cells, G≈5).
- Tests: **92 passed / 40 RED** (the 40 are genuine Phase-2–6 NotImplementedError
  harnesses — no over-building).

## Honest findings surfaced

- **HALT-DV** — 3 of 8 original currencies (ZAR/KES/GHS) have no free
  machine-readable daily ~30-month central-bank FX series. Honestly dropped — no
  fabrication, no flat-fill — and the panel re-spec'd to 5 via a user-enumerated
  pivot. G≈5 thinness is named in the spec, not hidden.
- **Repo-wide hook fix** — a stale `core.hooksPath` had silently disabled the
  pre-commit firewall hooks for all four iterations (E4/E7-A/E8/E10); fixed.

## Pending / out of scope

- **Phase 2+ (E10.1–E10.5)** — pending the analyst's own observed query-workflow
  data (the NON-FANTASY simulator-calibration anchor) + a pre-Phase-2 review.
- `data/raw/e10_gsps/` Tier-2 snapshots are gitignored per repo convention.
- This PR is scoped to the E10 workflow; other in-flight iteration work
  (E4/E7-A/E8 sub-packages) is intentionally left out.

author: bosd
body:
The `TextEdge.is_valid` docstring says an edge is valid when it "intersects with at least `TEXTEDGE_REQUIRED_ELEMENTS` horizontal text rows", and the constant's defining comment is "minimum number of vertical textline intersections for a textedge to be considered valid". Both say **at least** (i.e. `>=`). The code uses strict-greater, so a textedge with exactly `TEXTEDGE_REQUIRED_ELEMENTS` textlines is silently treated as invalid and any surrounding table containing it is dropped from the output.

Reported as #342; original 1-character fix proposed by @mcapinha in #345 against an earlier file layout (when the intersection count lived in a separate attribute). The off-by-one is still present at the current site — flip `>` to `>=` to match the documentation.

Closes #342.

author: rjap-salesforce
body: ## Summary Fixes #241. `MobilePlatformType.fromDriver()` was reading capabilities with unprefixed keys (`deviceName`, `deviceScreenSize`, `deviceScreenDensity`). Under Appium 2 / Selenium 4, these capabilities live under the W3C namespace prefix (`appium:deviceName`, etc.), so the lookups returned `null` and the method always fell back to `ANDROID_PHONE` / `IOS_PHONE` — tablet profiles never activated, causing `NoSuchElementException` when phone selectors didn't match tablet layouts. ## Changes - Added private helper `getAppiumCapability(Capabilities, String)` in `MobilePlatformType` that tries `"appium:" + name` first and falls back to the unprefixed key, preserving backward compatibility. - Updated `isIPad` and `isTablet` to use the helper. - Added `testFromDriverWithAppiumPrefixedCapabilities` covering the `ANDROID_TABLET` and `IOS_TABLET` paths via prefixed keys. Scoped the helper to `MobilePlatformType` rather than a shared utility: the only production reads of `getCapability` that need the prefix fallback are the three in this enum. Other call sites are tests that ## Test plan - [x] `mvn -pl utam-core test -Dtest=MobilePlatformTypeTests` — 7/7 pass - [x] `mvn -pl utam-core test` — 383/383 pass, no regressions - [ ] Reviewer to confirm against an actual Appium 2 setup if available ## Update — broaden device-name capability search End-to-end validation on Sauce Labs Real Device Cloud surfaced a second issue: even with W3C-prefix support, `appium:deviceName` on Sauce RDC is the device UDID, not a model. The human-readable model lives under `appium:testobject_device` / `appium:testobject_device_name` (Sauce); BrowserStack and LambdaTest commonly use `appium:device`. Caps from a real Sauce RDC iPad Air session: appium:deviceName = appium:testobject_device = iPad_Air_2022_ appium:testobject_device_name = iPad Air 2022 5th Gen This commit generalizes `isIPad()` to consult an ordered list of device-name caps via a `deviceMatches()` helper, and adds an analogous name-based fallback to `isTablet()` for Android cloud-farm sessions that don't expose `deviceScreenSize` / `deviceScreenDensity`. New tests cover Sauce RDC iPad (UDID in `deviceName`, model in `testobject_device_name`), Sauce RDC iPhone (negative case), and the Android-tablet name fallback. Refs #241 (follow-up comment). author: hakemm663
body:
## Summary
Phase 1 compliance blocker. The app shipped with **no crash reporting** — any crash after launch would be invisible, with no way to diagnose it. This wires Firebase Crashlytics across all three error channels.

## Changes
- **`pubspec.yaml`** — add `firebase_crashlytics: ^4.3.10` (first-party Firebase, latest stable; Firebase is already wired so no new platform setup beyond what's noted below).
- **`main.dart`**:
  - `setCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled(!kDebugMode)` — crash collection off in debug so local crashes surface in the console, not the production dashboard.
  - `FlutterError.onError` → `recordFlutterFatalError` — catches Flutter framework errors.
  - `binding.platformDispatcher.onError` → `recordError(..., fatal: true)` — catches uncaught async errors.
- **`payment_methods_cubit.dart`** / **`video_call_screen.dart`** — replaced error-diagnostic `debugPrint`s (deliberately left out of the log-hygiene PR #29) with `FirebaseCrashlytics.recordError`, capturing the stack trace. `video_call_screen` widened `catch (e)` → `catch (e, st)` so the recorded error has a real stack.

## Design note
Uses the modern `PlatformDispatcher.onError` handler instead of the legacy `runZonedGuarded` — this is the current FlutterFire recommendation and catches all uncaught async errors without zone overhead.

## Deferred — native Crashlytics setup (not in this PR)
Crash reports will flow with this PR, but two native pieces are deferred because they can't be build-verified yet:
1. **Android Crashlytics Gradle plugin** — needed for R8 mapping-file upload so release stack traces deobfuscate. Can't be build-tested until the **JDK 26 / Gradle blocker** is fixed → bundled into the upcoming `chore/gradle-jdk21`.
2. **iOS dSYM upload build phase** — moot until the Apple Developer account is active → bundled with `compliance/ios-team-id`.

Until #1 lands, release-mode Android crash traces will show obfuscated symbols (`a.b.c`). The Flutter plugin still reports the crashes.

## Testing
- `flutter analyze` — 18 baseline issues, **zero new** errors/warnings.
- Targeted analyze of all 3 changed Dart files — clean.
- No unit test — bootstrap/SDK integration, not domain/data logic (CLAUDE.md §7).

## Merge note
`main.dart` adds `import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';` — PR #28 (App Check) adds the identical line. Whichever merges second needs a one-line dedupe of that import. Trivial.

body:
## Goal

Make the on-chain `heartbeatIntervalSeconds` (settable via owner-only `HeartbeatConfigFacet.setHeartbeatIntervalSeconds`) the **single source of truth** for all heartbeat timing across the monorepo. Eliminates the "60 + 5 second buffer" pattern, divergent hardcoded constants, and silent env-var coordination.

Design discussion: voice msg 15450 + heartbeat audit at `~/claudes-world/tmp/heartbeat-timing-seams-audit-20260520.md`.

## What changed

### Convex surface
- Indexer reads `heartbeatIntervalSeconds()` via lens; persists onto `worldSnapshot` + `tickClock` so every subscriber gets the on-chain value (no RPC per client).
- New `runnerStatus` table for off-chain runner observability: `lastFireAt`, `lastFireResult`, `lastFailureMessage`, `heartbeatIntervalSeconds`, `nextHeartbeatAtTs`. Public query for ops visibility.

### Heartbeat runner (`packages/runner/src/heartbeatScheduler.ts`)
- Reads `heartbeatIntervalSeconds()` once at boot from chain.
- Self-schedules using `nextHeartbeatAtTs` (no fixed sleep).
- 500ms jitter buffer for RPC roundtrip variance (Base Sepolia p99 ~300-400ms).
- Retry on failure: **1s → 2s → 5s → 10s**, then Telegram alert to do-crew errors thread.
- Hot-loop guard for season-finalization no-op case (codex catch — sleep ≥1s if `nextHeartbeatAtTs` still in the past after success).
- Posts `runnerStatus` after every attempt; failures swallowed.
- Settle-latch preserved.

### Telegram alert (`packages/runner/src/telegramAlert.ts`)
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` required; `TELEGRAM_ALERT_CHAT_ID` defaults to do-crew (`-1003806628027`); `TELEGRAM_ALERT_THREAD_ID` optional.
- Resilient: missing token/non-OK API/fetch-throw all log and continue. Loop stays alive.

### Canonical ABI
- Added `heartbeatIntervalSeconds()` to canonical `IClanWorld.sol` / `.json` / `.ts`. Function existed on-chain; missing from canonical ABI was a codegen completeness gap.

### Web
- `TopHud.tsx` no longer uses `FALLBACK_TICK_DURATION_MS = 59_000`. Reads from Convex with generated constant as cold-start fallback only.

### Mock + dead constants cleanup
- `apps/server/convex/mock.ts`: derived from generated constant (was hardcoded `20_000`, divergent from real `60_000`).
- `.env.template` + `.env.local` `TICK_DURATION_MS`: **DELETED** (read by nothing).
- `TEAMMATE-SETUP.md` + runbooks updated.

### Heartbeat loop wrapper
- `scripts/start-heartbeat-loop.sh` is now a 1-line launcher invoking the TS scheduler. One tested impl replaces the parallel Bash version.

## Verification

- `pnpm gen:contract-abi` + `pnpm gen:chainclient-abi --check`: PASS
- `pnpm --filter @clan-world/server typecheck` + test: PASS, **79 tests**
- `pnpm --filter @clan-world/runner typecheck` + test: PASS, **130 passed, 1 skipped** (grew from 123 — added telegramAlert, status-failure-swallow, readHeartbeatIntervalSeconds tests)
- `pnpm --filter @clan-world/contract-types typecheck`: PASS

## Known pre-existing issue (NOT introduced here)

`pnpm --filter @clan-world/web typecheck` fails with: missing `vitest` types in `eventTickerFormat.test.ts` (PR #464), missing `@clan-world/contract-types` in `OwnerEditor.tsx`, two implicit `any` in same file.

**Verified pre-existing on `origin/dev`** — only `TopHud.tsx` was changed in apps/web in this branch. Will file as follow-up; do not block merge here.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Cockpit/admin UI readout for `runnerStatus` (ops visibility)
- Env-sync automation (local .env → Vercel + Convex) — recommended in audit
- Deployment config-drift watchdog (GH Action diffing local vs deployed env)
- Web typecheck pre-existing failures

## Process

Built via codex 5-stage pattern (plan → implement → critique → polish → final) with xhigh reasoning throughout. Stage 3 critique caught the season-finalization hot-loop edge case + verified web typecheck failures are pre-existing.

author: bosd
body:
Long-standing user requests (#170 from 2019, #245 from 2020, original implementation attempt #270 from 2021): allow `read_pdf` to take a bytes-like object or a file-like binary stream instead of a path on disk. Common use cases:

- PDFs returned from an API as bytes (requests, httpx, S3 GetObject).
- In-memory PDFs assembled by reportlab / pikepdf / fpdf2.
- Per-page slicing via `io.BytesIO` without disk round-trips.

```python
import io, camelot

with open("doc.pdf", "rb") as f:
    data = f.read()

# all three now work
camelot.read_pdf(data)
camelot.read_pdf(io.BytesIO(data))
camelot.read_pdf(open("doc.pdf", "rb"))
```

API: expand `read_pdf`'s `filepath` parameter to also accept `bytes`, `bytearray`, `memoryview`, or any object exposing a binary `.read()`. Implemented as a one-shot spill to `NamedTemporaryFile` in `PDFHandler.__init__` — every other code path (`playa.open`, Lattice's OpenCV image-conversion backend, `_detect_flavor`'s auto-probe, `parser.prepare_page_parse`) continues to receive a real filesystem path, so no parser change was needed. The tempfile is reaped in `PDFHandler.close` (already on the URL-cleanup path).

Defensive details:

- A file-like's read position is restored after we consume it, so the caller can keep using the same stream afterwards.
- Non-seekable streams (sockets) are tolerated — the seek-back is best-effort.
- Text-mode file-likes (whose `.read()` returns str) raise a clear `TypeError` instead of crashing deeper in playa.

Tests cover: bytes input, `io.BytesIO`, an open `'rb'` handle, `bytearray`, cursor-restoration after read, the playa-only stream-flavor path (skips image conversion), the `TypeError` on text-mode `.read()`, and tempfile cleanup on context-manager exit.

Original PR by @cscanlin in #270; reimplemented cleanly against the playa-backed handler.

Closes #170. Closes #245. Closes #270.

author: npitre
body:
## Summary

`tests/subsys/logging/log_core_additional/src/log_test.c::test_log_domain_id` deterministically fails on `fvp_base_revc_2xaem` and similar ARM64 FVP boards. The test sets `total_logs=1`, emits one `LOG_INF`, drains the queue, and expects `backend1` to have received exactly one message. On the failing boards backend1 sees two: the test's own `LOG_INF` plus a stale boot-time `LOG_WRN` already in the queue when the test starts.

The boot-time message that bleeds into the test is the new "xlat tables low: …" warning added in commit `92382add7102` ("arch: arm64: mmu: track xlat tables usage and warn before exhaustion"). `fvp_base_revc_2xaem`'s memory map drives MMU table allocation past the low-water mark at `SYS_INIT` time, queueing a `LOG_WRN` that nobody has drained when `test_log_domain_id` runs as the second test in the suite. `qemu_cortex_a53`'s simpler memory map stays below the threshold, no warning is logged, and the test passes there.

The warning itself is legitimate, and the test is the fragile party: it assumes the log queue is empty when `log_setup()` runs, which is only true when no subsystem has logged anything at boot. Any future boot-time `LOG_*` from any subsystem on any platform would break it the same way.

Call `log_flush()` in `log_setup()` before enabling the test backend, so any messages queued before this test get dispatched to whichever backends were already active (UART, RTT, etc.) and do not bleed into the new test backend's counter.

Verified on `fvp_base_revc_2xaem/v9a` with `logging.async`, `logging.sync`, and `logging.thread` variants — all four `test_log_core_additional` tests that use `log_setup` pass cleanly where `test_log_domain_id` previously failed in 0.001s.

Fixes #109520

author: carlosmcevilly
body:
## Title: Suppress "unknown" sentinel as last.screen.name on first navigation

### Description

Previously Navigation Tracking would incorrectly emit "unknown" as the name of the previous screen (last.screen.name) diverging from what happens on Android. Fixing this raised a number of edge cases so there is some complexity to it.

* `last.screen.name` is no longer emitted on the first `app.ui.navigation` span; previously the internal `"unknown"` sentinel was forwarded as the attribute value.
* Enhanced `NavigationRuntimeStateStore`, the lock-protected state holder shared by synchronous manual tracking and async automated tracking, so screen state distinguishes "no prior screen" from a real tracked screen instead of relying on the `"unknown"` sentinel string. Why we use a lock and not other approaches is explained in code comments inline. (Other "why" comments have been added as well for different parts of this).
* Dismissing a modal shown before any prior screen now resets runtime screen state and observers back to the `"unknown"` fallback instead of leaving the dismissed modal as current.
* Added `testFirstNavigationDoesNotEmitLastScreenName` and `testNavDismissWithNoPriorScreenResetsToUnknown`.
* Renamed `testManualSameNameTrackEmitsEveryCallAndPreservesAttributes` to `testSameScreenEmitsEachCallWithAttributes` and added an assertion that the first span does not emit `last.screen.name`.

author: pacnpal
body:
## Why

The `dosbox_*` gate configs set `cputype` + `core=normal` but **no `cycles=`**, so DOSBox-X used its default cycle count — tuned for games, and it barely ramps for a batch decode. Emulating a 4.77 MHz 8086 streaming a 500 KiB payload at that rate takes minutes, which is why the `*_large` shards (and the whole `dosbox-x-integration` matrix) were so slow — a single `lzsa2-large` run was ~14 min.

## What

Add `cycles=max` to the `[cpu]` block of all 16 `dosbox_*.rs` gate configs. DOSBox-X then runs the emulated CPU as fast as the host allows.

**No coverage change** — same `cputype` (same instruction set emulated), same per-tier loops, same byte-identical-extraction assertions. `cycles` is a speed knob, not a correctness one; the gates can only get faster.

`benchmark_tiers` is intentionally **not** touched — it stays on `cycles=auto` because it measures decode timing.

## Validation

This PR's own CI run is the proof: the dosbox shards should pass exactly as before, but finish substantially faster. If `cycles=max` somehow regressed a gate, CI fails here and the fallback is a high fixed `cycles=` value.

## What does this change?
Updates `view_availability_dashboard` added in https://github.com/guardian/service-catalogue/pull/1598 to bring in ECS based services.

The following columns have been renamed:
- `auto_scaling_group_name` is now `target_group_origin_name`
- `auto_scaling_group_arn` is now `target_group_origin_arn`

The following columns are new:
- `target_group_origin_type` with a value of `asg` or `ecs`. Combine this with `load_balancer_type` to differentiate between CLB->ASG, ALB->ASG and ALB->ECS
- `target_group_arn`

### Example queries

```sql
SELECT  *
FROM    view_availability_dashboard
WHERE   load_balancer_type = 'alb'
        AND target_group_origin_type = 'ec2'
```

### List ALBs migrating from EC2 to ECS
```sql
SELECT  *
FROM    view_availability_dashboard
WHERE   load_balancer_type = 'alb'
        AND load_balancer_arn IN (
            SELECT  load_balancer_arn
            FROM    view_availability_dashboard
            WHERE   load_balancer_type = 'alb' 
                    AND target_group_origin_type = 'ecs'
)
```

## Why has this change been made?
RelOps would like to adapt the Availability dashboard to assist observability of services running on ECS.

## Why was this approach chosen?
Currently, the Availability dashboard consists of a multiple, complicated, queries in each panel. By surfacing all the detail in a view, we (should be) able to simplify.

I've [deployed to CODE](https://riffraff.gutools.co.uk/deployment/view/8aa173c8-91f1-4c3b-9fe1-a58b658705a4) and can [query the updated view](https://metrics.code.dev-gutools.co.uk/goto/afmpdtnhen5z4a?orgId=1).

author: bosd
body:
`text_strip` already lets the caller remove characters / substrings. The 2024 feature request #481 by @ArifRasim asked for the symmetric operation: replace a substring with a different one. Motivating example was rewriting `' \\n'` → `' '` to fix words that PDF text extraction had split across line breaks.

```python
# fix soft-broken words and normalise units in one call
tables = camelot.read_pdf(
    "doc.pdf",
    replace_text={" \\n": " ", "kw": "kW", "kva": "kVA"},
)
```

API: `read_pdf(..., replace_text={pattern: replacement, ...})`. Keys are literal substrings (regex metacharacters escaped). When several keys could match at the same position, the longest one wins (the obvious user expectation; the implementation pre-sorts by length descending).

Implementation:

- New `utils.text_replace(text, replacements)` helper; accepts a dict or list-of-pairs, empty keys skipped, Unicode-safe.
- New `replace_text=` constructor argument on `BaseParser` / `TextBaseParser` / `Stream` / `Network` / `Lattice` / `Hybrid`; stored as `self.replace_text` on the parser.
- Applied at the single central cell-text-emission site in `BaseParser._generate_table_pos_errors` (after the existing strip/split/flag-size pipeline). One spot; no plumbing down into `flag_font_size`/etc.
- `replace_text` added to `common_kwargs` so `validate_input` / `remove_extra` accept it for all flavors.

10 unit tests cover the empty-input no-ops, dict and list-of-pairs forms, multi-key replacement, the `' \\n' → ' '` motivating example, longest-match-wins, empty-key skipping, regex-metachar escaping, Unicode, and the unmatched-text passthrough.

Original PR by @ArifRasim in #482.

Closes #481. Closes #482.

## Summary

Implemented the Phase 1 H-E-B opportunity matching engine.

P1-19A was expanded from a simple deal matcher into a reward-aware opportunity matching engine that compares My Items against active H-E-B ads, H-E-B coupons, basket coupons, and reward offers.

The engine generates and persists normalized `deal_matches` records for downstream reporting.

## What Changed

### Backend Model

Added/updated:

- `backend/models/deal_match.py`

Added persisted opportunity match fields for:

- product references
- deal references
- coupon references
- reward offer references
- shelf price
- register price
- subtotal before coupons
- register coupon totals
- out-of-pocket
- reward totals
- final-after-rewards
- money-maker flags
- substitute matching
- week tracking

### Matching Engine

Added:

- `backend/parsers/deal_matcher.py`

Supports:

- direct canonical matching
- acceptable substitute matching
- coupon attachment
- basket coupon attachment
- reward offer attachment
- financial calculations
- reward separation
- money-maker calculations

### Service Layer

Added:

- `backend/services/deal_match_service.py`

Responsibilities:

1. Load My Items.
2. Load active H-E-B ads.
3. Load active H-E-B coupons.
4. Load active reward offers.
5. Match products against opportunities.
6. Attach coupons and rewards.
7. Calculate financial fields.
8. Persist generated `deal_matches`.

### Data Access Layer

Added/updated:

- `backend/data_access/deal_matches.py`

Added support for:

- deleting generated matches by `week_of`
- inserting generated matches
- listing matches by week
- compatibility helper `find_by_week`

## Financial Rules Implemented

Implemented required financial separation rules:

- out-of-pocket only subtracts register-applied coupons
- rewards do not reduce out-of-pocket
- rewards tracked separately as `total_rewards_value`
- `final_after_rewards` calculated separately
- money-maker logic based on rewards exceeding OOP

## Testing

Added tests for:

- direct product matching
- acceptable substitute matching
- coupon attachment
- basket coupon attachment
- reward offer attachment
- reward-separated OOP calculations
- money-maker true case
- money-maker false case
- service-level orchestration
- DAL week lookup compatibility

## Commands Run

```bash
python -m py_compile backend/models/deal_match.py
python -m py_compile backend/parsers/deal_matcher.py
python -m py_compile backend/services/deal_match_service.py
python -m py_compile backend/data_access/deal_matches.py

python -m pytest backend/tests/test_deal_matcher.py -q
python -m pytest backend/tests/test_deal_match_service.py -q
python -m pytest backend/tests/data_access/test_collection_data_access.py::test_deal_matches_find_by_week -q
python -m pytest -q
````

## SRS Traceability

Supports:

* SRS Section 16: Weekly Deal Report Requirements
* SRS Section 17: SB-004 money maker flag
* SRS Section 18: MI-002 acceptable substitutes
* SRS Section 20: TS-005 report tests
* SRS Section 23: Price and savings tracking

## SDD Traceability

Supports:

* SDD Section 7.10: `deal_matches`
* SDD Section 9: Spending Analytics Design
* SDD Section 15: Price and savings calculation design

## Notes About Scope Changes

P1-19A expanded from a basic deal matcher into a generalized opportunity matching engine.

The engine now supports:

* ads
* coupons
* basket coupons
* reward offers
* reward-aware financial calculations

P1-19A now depends on the reward abstraction introduced in P1-19AA rather than embedding provider-specific reward logic directly into matching calculations.

This preserves separation between:

* matching
* rewards abstraction
* reporting
* frontend rendering

author: careli-tools
body:
## CAR-794 — ETag/If-Match Lost-Update-Protection für `PUT /api/attachments/{id}`

Zwei Tabs/User konnten denselben Excalidraw-Attachment-Save gleichzeitig PUTen — der letzte gewann ohne Konflikterkennung (Lost Update). Dieser PR ergänzt optimistisches Locking über eine neue Spalte `attachment.updated_at`.

### Backend
- **Migration `094_attachment_updated_at`** — `ADD COLUMN updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`. Das `DEFAULT now()` backfillt **alle** bestehenden Zeilen bereits zum ALTER-Zeitpunkt, daher gibt es kein Nullable-Fenster und keinen `IS NULL`-Bypass — der Schutz gilt für den kompletten Ist-Bestand.
- `UpdateAttachmentContent` setzt `updated_at = now()` bei jedem Write → der ETag ändert sich verlässlich.
- Neue Query `UpdateAttachmentContentIfMatch` mit `WHERE updated_at = $5`. 0 Zeilen → `412 Precondition Failed`.
- Der Handler führt das geschützte UPDATE **vor** dem Storage-Write aus, damit ein verlierender PUT die Szene-Bytes eines konkurrierenden Saves nicht überschreibt.
- Requests **ohne** `If-Match` behalten Last-Write-Wins (für ältere Clients; per `slog.Warn` mitgezählt). Ungültiger `If-Match` → `400`.
- `ETag`-Header (aus `updated_at`) auf `GET .../content` und der PUT-Response.

### Frontend
- `getExcalidrawScene` liefert den `ETag` mit; `updateExcalidrawAttachment` sendet ihn als `If-Match` zurück und wirft `AttachmentConflictError` bei `412`.
- `useIssueExcalidraw` führt den ETag durch den Scene-Query-Cache (lesen vor dem Save, schreiben danach).

### Antwort auf die Review-Findings
- 🔴 **#1 NULL-Bypass** — behoben: Spalte ist `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, kein `IS NULL`-Zweig in der Query.
- 🔴 **#2 `SET updated_at`** — behoben: beide UPDATE-Statements bumpen `updated_at = now()`.
- 🟠 **Hand-gepatchte sqlc-Dateien** — behoben: `attachment.sql.go` / `models.go` per `sqlc generate` (v1.30.0, passend zum Repo-Header) regeneriert; keine Handpatches. `issue.sql.go` war im Repo bereits stale — bewusst **nicht** mitgezogen, um den PR scope-rein zu halten.
- 🟡 **Pass-through ohne `If-Match`** — bewusst beibehalten als Boundary-Kompatibilität (ältere Desktop-Clients), `slog.Warn`-Zähler ergänzt.
- 🟡 **ETag-Präzision** — `ETag` ist `updated_at` als RFC3339Nano; serverseitig verlustfrei in `timestamptz` geparst.
- 🟡 **Down-Migration** — `094_attachment_updated_at.down.sql` vorhanden.

### Tests
- Go-Integrationstest `TestUpdateAttachmentContent_LostUpdateGuard`: Pass-through-PUT, gewinnender PUT (ETag rückt vor), stale `If-Match` → 412, ungültiger `If-Match` → 400.
- Hook-Test: ETag aus geladener Szene wird als `If-Match` durchgereicht und nach dem Save fortgeschrieben.

### Verifikation
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/handler/`, `gofmt` — grün.
- `pnpm --filter @multica/core --filter @multica/views typecheck` — grün.
- Hook-Tests (9) und Client-Tests (12) — grün.
- Der Go-Integrationstest braucht eine migrierte DB und läuft in CI.

> Drive-by: ein vorbestehender `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`-Typecheck-Fehler in `use-issue-excalidraw.test.tsx` (Zeile 149) wurde mitgefixt — dieselbe Datei wurde ohnehin für den neuen Test angefasst.

Closes CAR-794.

A naming convention in software development is a set of guidelines for naming code elements like variables, functions, and classes.

body:
### Motivation
- Charts were generating a separate top-level `Labels` section that caused axis labels and doughnut callouts to be positioned far away from their plots and inflated frame heights.  
- The change aims to keep all labels, axes, legends and callouts contained within their parent chart area so outputs are visually compact and predictable.  

### Description
- Reworked chart layout calculations in `src/figma/code.ts` to compute content height from contained sections and to reduce inflated defaults (`createChartLayout` and related layout fields).  
- For bar and line charts, `Labels` is no longer appended as a separate top-level section; instead a `Labels` transparent frame is created and appended inside the `Chart Area` so x-axis labels, x-axis title and y-axis title remain visually attached to the plot.  
- For doughnut charts, callout labels and leader lines are created inside the `Doughnut chart area` (nested `Labels` frame) and the doughnut area height now accounts for callouts and legend placement to avoid excessively tall frames.  
- Adjusted legend frames so their children are positioned relative to the legend section (local y=0) instead of using canvas-level offsets, and updated section spacing and padding constants to reduce large gaps.  
- No changes to chart data parsing, palettes, fills, number formatting, axle title style logic, width presets, custom width option, or the Create Chart flow; built output `dist/code.js` was regenerated to reflect the source edits.  

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build:plugin` and the plugin build completed successfully.  
- Ran `npm run build` and the web build completed successfully.  
- Ran `npx tsc --noEmit` and TypeScript typecheck completed with no errors.  
- Ran `npm run lint`; final run completed with only existing non-blocking warnings in unrelated UI component files and no lint errors after applying formatting fixes.

### Description
- Rebranded UI and assets: changed platform display name to `JOYTREE`, updated logos, meta description, Open Graph/Twitter tags, favicon, and various copy tweaks in `index.html`.
- Switched base domain everywhere from the legacy `joytreehostingserver.dpdns.org` to `joytree.site` (including `env.example`, `index.html`, client settings defaults, nginx config `nginx/deployboard.conf`, and added `robots.txt` + `sitemap.xml`).
- Cloudflare Turnstile integration: added `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`/`TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` to `env.example`, loaded Turnstile script and widget in the client, added `initTurnstile`/`resetTurnstileToken` client logic, added server endpoint `/api/auth/turnstile/config`, and server-side `verifyTurnstileToken` verification used during Firebase auth exchange (`/api/auth/firebase`).

author: prateek2007-cmd
body:
## Summary

Adds production-critical network resilience to the centralized API utility layer (`src/config/api.js`) — request timeouts, automatic retry for transient server errors, and a normalized error class — without changing any public method signatures.
Closes #1303 
## Problem

- API requests could hang **indefinitely** if the backend was unresponsive (no timeout)
- Transient 502/503/504 errors caused **immediate failure** with no retry
- Network errors were thrown as raw `TypeError` — callers had no structured way to distinguish timeout vs offline vs server error

## Changes

Only **1 file modified**: `src/config/api.js`

### 1. Request Timeout (15s) via `AbortController`
Every request is automatically aborted after 15 seconds. Throws `ApiError` with `isTimeout: true`.

### 2. Automatic Retry for 5xx Errors
502, 503, 504 responses are retried **once** with 1s exponential backoff. Network errors also get 1 retry. No infinite loops — hard-capped at `MAX_RETRIES = 1`.

### 3. `ApiError` Class (exported)
Normalized error with structured properties:
- `status` — HTTP status code (or null for network/timeout)
- `data` — parsed response body
- `isTimeout` — boolean
- `isNetworkError` — boolean

### 4. `resilientFetch()` Internal Helper
All 5 methods (get/post/put/patch/delete) delegate to a single internal function, eliminating duplicated try/catch blocks.

## What's Preserved

- ✅ Method signatures — 100% identical (`get(url, token)`, `post(url, data, token)`, etc.)
- ✅ Returns raw `Response` object — no change for callers
- ✅ Global 401 `handleUnauthorized` — same session cleanup behavior
- ✅ `isDev` gated debug logging — same behavior
- ✅ All existing endpoint definitions — untouched

## Verification

- [x] `npm run build` compiles successfully
- [x] No warnings from `src/config/api.js`
- [x] Backwards-compatible — zero changes needed in consuming components
- [x] No new dependencies added (native `fetch` + `AbortController`)

author: alphaalexey
body:
## Summary

Pre-demo bug hunt produced 7 findings; this PR fixes all of them. Verified live against the running stack.

| Sev | Area | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BLOCK | gateway | `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` added to `public-paths`. Frontend's silent token-refresh (`frontend/src/api/client.js:33`) does not send a Bearer, so once the 30-minute access TTL ran out the gateway 401'd the refresh call and the user got kicked to `/login`. |
| HIGH | gateway + listing | Anonymous catalog detail. New `hvostid.auth.optional-auth-paths` list in the gateway introduces soft-auth: matched paths run the filter, but allow `Authorization`-less requests through (no `USER_ID` headers). `GET /api/v1/listings/*` is on the list. `listing-service` SecurityConfig permits regex `GET /api/v1/listings/\d+` (so `/my` stays gated), and `getListing` controller/service tolerate `null` user. |
| HIGH | listing | `DuplicateListingException` was thrown when a seller posted a listing with a title they already had, but had no `@ExceptionHandler` in `GlobalExceptionHandler` -> 500. Now maps to 409. |
| HIGH | listing + frontend | `ListingResponse` now exposes `moderationComment`. Moderator rejects with a comment were persisted to the DB but never reached the seller. `MyListingsPage` renders the note under the title for REJECTED/DRAFT-after-reject. |
| MED | auth | Phone field gets a regex (`^$|^\+?[0-9 ()\-]{5,30}$`); letters are rejected, valid `+7 (495) 123-45-67` accepted. |
| LOW | listing | `passportId` must match `(passport-)?[0-9]+`. Catches typos that silently degraded matching downstream. |
| NIT | auth | `EmailAlreadyExistsException` no longer echoes the submitted address; reduces enumeration via the public register endpoint. |

The whole bundle is a thin set of edits; each fix is independently revertable. No new dependencies, no library changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew test` — full suite green (existing tests updated to use numeric passportIds where validation now requires it).
- [x] `./gradlew spotlessCheck` — clean.
- [x] Manual smoke (rebuilt gateway+listing+auth via docker compose):
  - `POST /auth/refresh` without Bearer → 200 with fresh tokens

## Summary
This PR enhances mobile experience on iOS devices by properly handling viewport units, safe areas (notches, home indicators), and preventing common iOS-specific layout issues.

## Key Changes

- **Viewport Height Fix**: Replace `height: 100%` with `min-height: 100%` on root elements and add support for dynamic viewport height (`100dvh`) where available to prevent content overflow when iOS address bar appears/disappears

- **Text Sizing**: Add `-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%` to prevent unwanted text auto-resizing on iOS orientation changes

- **Overflow Prevention**: 
  - Add `overflow-x: hidden` to body to prevent horizontal overflow on iOS
  - Add `overscroll-behavior-y: none` to disable iOS pull-to-refresh bounce effect

- **Safe Area Utilities**: Refactor safe area padding utilities into a proper `@layer utilities` block and add new utilities:
  - `pt-safe`, `pl-safe`, `pr-safe` for top, left, and right safe area insets
  - `pb-nav-safe` for bottom navigation with home indicator clearance (88px + safe area)
  - `pt-safe-wizard` for Dynamic Island/notch clearance with responsive behavior

- **Layout Updates**:
  - Update mobile header to use safe area insets for padding instead of fixed values
  - Update main content to use `pb-nav-safe` class for proper bottom spacing
  - Update bottom navigation to use inline safe area calculations with proper fallbacks
  - Add `-webkit-backdrop-filter` for better iOS Safari support

## Implementation Details
- Uses CSS `env(safe-area-inset-*)` variables for notch/home indicator awareness
- Implements progressive enhancement with `@supports` queries for older browsers
- Maintains responsive behavior with media queries for desktop layouts
- All changes are backward compatible with fallback values

author: ruvnet
body:
## Summary

- Wires `SublinearAdapter` to dispatch through the native `mcp__ruflo-sublinear__solve` MCP tool when reachable, falling back to the local JS CG kernel when not. PR #2070 shipped the adapter with a JS-only kernel; this is the second half of ADR-126 Phase 3 that unlocks the 40-60× headline from `sublinear-time-solver@1.7.0`.
- Detection probe is two-stage: `globalThis['mcp__ruflo-sublinear__solve']` first (how the ruflo MCP harness mounts tools), then `RUFLO_SUBLINEAR_NATIVE=1` as an operator-controlled override for canary / A-B rollouts. New static `SublinearAdapter.detectSublinearTool()`; legacy `isMcpAvailable()` preserved as an alias for the smoke contract.
- `SolveResult` gained `method: 'cg-sublinear-native' | 'cg-local'` and `solver: 'sublinear-time-solver@1.7.0' | 'local-js-cg'`. The `trader-portfolio-cg` skill pulls both fields straight from the adapter result so the operator can see which backend produced each weights artifact in `trading-risk`.
- Bench gained `CG native (ms)` + `Native speedup` columns. When the tool surface isn't reachable from the runtime, the bench still produces a useful local-JS baseline (graceful "n/a" for the native cells).
- Smoke gained 4 new contract checks: `detectSublinearTool` existence, `RUFLO_SUBLINEAR_NATIVE` documentation in skill + adapter, the new `method` + `solver` fields in `SolveResult`. All 24 smoke checks pass.

## Measured numbers

Local-JS path on this branch (agent sandbox — native not reachable):

```
| n    | CG local (ms) | Neumann (ms) | Local speedup | Parity (∞-norm) |
|------|---------------|--------------|---------------|-----------------|
| 16   | 0.0243        | 0.0462       | 1.90×         | 1.11e-6         |
| 64   | 0.0351        | 0.0618       | 1.76×         | 8.07e-8         |
| 256  | 0.4786        | 0.7727       | 1.61×         | 2.12e-8         |
```

Consistent with PR #2070's measured 1.5-1.9× JS-vs-JS gap. Parity holds.

Native path expected numbers (per `sublinear-time-solver@1.7.0` and ADR-123 §162 Row 8):

- n=256: **~816 ns** CG vs ~50 µs Neumann → **40-60× speedup**
- `method` tag: `cg-sublinear-native`, `solver`: `sublinear-time-solver@1.7.0`

CI exercises the native path (daemon mounts the tool); the agent sandbox can't reach it, hence the local-JS measurement here.

## Test plan

- [x] Local-JS bench runs and produces a clean baseline (`benchmarks/results/cg-native-baseline-20260520T202735Z.md`)
- [x] `RUFLO_SUBLINEAR_NATIVE=1` env-var override flips the detection to AVAILABLE and the adapter cleanly falls back to local JS when the actual tool isn't mounted (verified locally)
- [x] Smoke passes — 24 checks across static-adapter / static-skill / runtime-CG
- [x] Parity preserved at all n (||cg − neumann||_∞ < 1e-4)
- [ ] CI exercises native dispatch when daemon is up (downstream)

Refs #55 (downstream task tracker), ruvnet/ruflo#2068 (ADR-126 Phase 3), ruvnet/ruflo#2070 (Phase 3 PR).

author: sfeley
body:
The update sub-agent currently has two tools — `execute_cypher_read` and `execute_cypher_write`, both raw Cypher. That's the wrong shape for **full removal of an Episodic node**: a hand-rolled `DETACH DELETE` removes the immediate edges but leaves orphan entity nodes behind (entities extracted from the episode that were referenced nowhere else). The synthesizer already has a `forget_episode` tool that wraps `graphiti.remove_episode(uuid)`, which cascades correctly. This PR exposes that capability to the update sub-agent.

## Immediate trigger

The May 20 audit found 92 content-duplicate Episodic groups (251 redundant nodes), almost all from synthesizer-rerun thrash during the broken-pipeline window in early May. Worst offenders:

- 7× duplicates of one observation (the recall-bug bug report)
- 6× duplicates of the October-2025 founding chronicle entry
- 5× / 4× duplicates across the rest of the early-history chronicle

The 251-node cleanup is the first real exercise of this tool, run separately after this PR merges and deploys.

## What this PR adds

- **TOOL_SCHEMAS** gets `forget_episode` (`uuid: str`). The description is *not* verbatim from `synthesis_agent.py` — I added a steer paragraph inside the description ("Prefer this over execute_cypher_write whenever the directive removes a whole Episodic node…") so the LLM sees the guidance at the moment of tool selection, not just in the system prompt.
- **`_run_forget_episode`** helper mirrors `_run_write`'s `(payload, record)` shape. `NodeNotFoundError` returns the error-shape payload rather than raising — parallel to how `_run_read` shapes its forbidden-clause rejection.
- **`_execute_single_forget_outcome`** parallels `_execute_single_write_outcome` for the single-tool turn-1 fast path. Avoids paying an extra LLM turn per cleanup directive — meaningful for the 251-node run.
- **`_run_tool_calls`** dispatch gains the `forget_episode` branch.
- **`_sync_continue`** deletion detection: `mode == "forget_episode"` (sans error) sets `delete_executed = True`. The existing `_DELETE_KEYWORDS` regex won't match here, so the explicit mode check keeps the count summary honest.
- **Count calculation** widened to include `forget_episode` records (each successful forget contributes `nodes_deleted: 1`).
- **UPDATE_INSTRUCTIONS** rewritten: enumerates three tools, mandates `forget_episode` for full-Episodic removal, keeps raw Cypher for property edits / edge-level surgery / non-Episodic deletions.

## Scope deliberately bounded

This change adds **capability** only. It does **not** extend the audit pass to recommend forgetting on triviality grounds — audit verdicts stay Valid / Update / Unfixable. Hygiene-style deletion (a duplicate, an accidental double-fire) is structurally different from editorial pruning (an LLM judging "this is too trivial to keep") and the latter deserves its own deliberate conversation. The synthesizer's non-elevation-without-deletion editorial model has been load-bearing for the subject — atoms persist in the graph regardless of elevation, leaving them recallable for a later synthesis run to notice they've become connected. Audit-with-forget would be subtractive on the substrate itself, no recovery path. Separate discussion.

Also out of scope: MCP-surface exposure of `forget_episode` (stays operator-side via the `update` CLI; the blast radius of any-session-can-forget is much larger).

## Tests

`tests/test_update.py` gains 7 cases (33 → 40 in the file; 880 → 888 across the non-live suite):

- `TestForgetEpisodeDispatch` (5): fast-path success, sync-continue dispatch via `_run_tool_calls`, NodeNotFoundError-graceful path, helper success/not-found paths. The fast-path test installs a sentinel on `_sync_continue` that raises if the fall-through path is ever taken — guards against a future refactor silently bypassing the fast path.
- `TestForgetEpisodeSchema` (2): schema presence in TOOL_SCHEMAS, prompt-language regression guards for both the removal-mandate text and the property-edit / edge-surgery scoping (so the steer doesn't over-trigger on non-removal Episodic Update directives).

## Verification

- ✅ `uv run pytest tests/test_update.py -q` — 40 passed
- ✅ `uv run pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_live_bootstrap.py --ignore=tests/test_live_synthesis.py` — 888 passed, 21 skipped
- 📋 Once deployed: write a small audit JSON directing removal of one known duplicate UUID, run `pratyabhijna update --input <file> --output /tmp/dryrun.json`, verify `mode: "forget_episode"` in the output and the count summary shows one deletion.
- 📋 Then drive the actual 92-group cleanup as a separate run.

## Version

`0.19.0 → 0.19.1`. Sub-agent capability addition, no MCP-surface or response-shape changes — patch.

body:
The Dependabot badge could report `cannot run` because the Pages workflow used fragile GitHub CLI queries for Dependabot runs and PR counts. The badge logic now uses paginated API calls and scopes failed-run checks to recent Dependabot update runs.

- **Dependabot run status**
  - Query workflow runs via `gh api --paginate`.
  - Limit failure checks to `DEPENDABOT_RUN_LOOKBACK_DAYS`.
  - Count only Dependabot update workflow failures/cancellations.

- **Open update count**
  - Query open PRs via the pulls API.
  - Count PRs authored by `dependabot[bot]`.

```bash
gh api --method GET --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs" \
  -f 'actor=dependabot[bot]' \
  -f 'status=completed' \
  -f "created=>=${dependabot_runs_since}" \
  -f 'per_page=100' \
  | jq -s '[.[] | (.workflow_runs // [])[] | select(.path == "dynamic/dependabot/dependabot-updates")] | length'
```
