author: doeljavid
body:
## Summary

This change replaces `Transform3D` in the network transform sync with a new `TransformPayloadDto`, a class that contains only the necessary transform data that's needed to be applied between server and client. The data for each transform is compressed into four floats. This is achieved by unpacking the position, and by compressing the rotation in the form of a unit quaternion. The rotation is bit-copied into a float in order to send the data as a float array, but it may be nice to consider changing the array to a byte array to allow for further compression. In total, there are 8 less 32-bit values being sent between client and server. This, combined with the existing ZSTD compression, saves a significant amount of bandwidth from server to client.

So much bandwidth is saved from this change that the `SyncInterval` for all objects can be uncapped completely. Now that the send rate for transforms are completely uncapped, this should make all objects appear smoother due to the minimization of packet loss, allowing for a (slightly) better experience. While this isn't the complete solution to the stuttery lockstep replication algorithm, I believe this is a step in the right direction towards a smoother Polytoria experience.

author: seanoc5
body:
## Summary

When multiple repos share a workspace parent dir (e.g. `/opt/work/oconeco/` holding `wt-issue-*` worktrees for fand-guide, fand-etl, fand-app, fand-poc), the watcher's `WORKSPACE/wt-issue-*/.swarm/tasks/done/` scan fires for **any** worker completing under that parent — every coordinator wakes on every sibling repo's worker event.

Observed in practice today: **three consecutive misfires** on the fand-guide coordinator from fand-etl worker completions in a single session. Coordinator runs the full triage checklist each time, finds nothing of its own, and reports an empty wake. Noise scales linearly with sibling-repo activity.

## Fix

Add an `is_our_worktree` filter that checks the outcome's containing worktree against `git -C $PROJECT_DIR worktree list --porcelain`. Only fire `on_outcome` when the worktree is registered with this coordinator's repo. **Fail-open** if git fails (preserves pre-patch behavior for non-git setups).

Both backends (inotify, poll) now route through a shared `dispatch_outcome` wrapper so the scoping logic lives in exactly one place.

## New event type

`worker.finish.skip` — logged when a foreign-worktree outcome is filtered out. The cross-talk remains observable (you can grep `events.log` to see what's happening in sibling repos) without waking the coordinator. Help section documents it.

## Verification

Tested `is_our_worktree` directly against real paths in `/opt/work/oconeco/`:

```
--- known worktrees for fand-guide ---
/opt/work/oconeco/fand-guide

--- test: fand-etl wt-issue-173 outcome (foreign) ---
SKIP (foreign)

--- test: hypothetical fand-guide outcome ---
FIRE
```

`bash -n` clean on the updated script.

## Test plan

- [ ] Restart `coordinator-watch.sh` for fand-guide; trigger a known fand-etl worker completion; confirm fand-guide coordinator no longer wakes (verify via `tail -F .swarm/events.log` — should see `worker.finish.skip` lines, not `coord.wake`)
- [ ] Provision a fand-guide worker and confirm its completion still wakes the coordinator (regression check)
- [ ] Confirm `bash -n scripts/coordinator-watch.sh` stays clean
- [ ] For setups without git (if any exist), confirm fail-open still wakes correctly

## Blind-merge risk

<!-- BLIND_MERGE_RISK: low -->
**Blind-merge risk:** 🟢 low — single-file additive change, both backends use the same wrapper, fail-open policy preserves backward compat, syntax-checked, behavior verified against real paths.

## Summary

- adds a structured `canonical phase failed` log with scope, generation, repo, phase, mode, statement count, duration, and error

Live ops-qa webhook validation proved GitHub events are handed off and the ingester fetches `private org/iac-eks-eshu`, but freshness is blocked by a NornicDB canonical projection timeout in `phase-group write (retract)`. The failing statement was the stale File retract query: it started from `MATCH (f:File)` and filtered by repo/generation. On a populated graph that is a broad label-scan-shaped delete. The fix starts from the indexed repository identity and only considers files attached to that repository through `REPO_CONTAINS`.

- Adds an **Ask for Help on Discord** button to the Feedback & Support companion that creates a forum thread in the DXOS #help channel and opens it in a new tab
- Includes a direct PostHog event link in the Discord thread so the team can connect to the submitter's session
- Adds a live **team / community online** presence indicator below the Discord button, powered by the new `discord-service` Edge worker
- Moves the Download Logs button above the submit actions
- `CaptureUserFeedback` operation now returns the PostHog event UUID (threaded back through the observability extension → operation → handler)

## Architecture

All Discord interactions are routed through `https://discord-service.dxos.workers.dev` (see companion PR in `dxos/edge`):
- `POST /feedback` — creates the forum thread server-side so the webhook URL is never in the browser bundle
- `GET /presence` — returns cached team/community online counts from a Durable Object refreshed every 60 seconds

The `DISCORD_SERVICE_URL` is a hardcoded constant for now; the webhook URL and bot token live as Cloudflare Worker secrets.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open Feedback & Support companion in Composer
- [ ] Verify both buttons are disabled when the message field is empty
- [ ] Enter a message — both buttons should enable
- [ ] **Send Feedback** submits to PostHog and shows toast
- [ ] **Ask for Help on Discord** creates a thread, opens it in a new tab, and shows Discord toast
- [ ] Verify the Discord thread body contains the message and a PostHog event link
- [ ] Verify presence indicator shows non-zero counts (omits any zero values)
- [ ] Remove `DX_DISCORD_SERVICE_URL` is no longer needed as a secret (URL is now a constant)

author: prabhuk
body:
Ensure that `llvm-readobj` / `llvm-readelf` processes and dumps all 
SHT_LLVM_CALL_GRAPH sections present in an object file, rather
than just the first one.

**Motivation:**
Consider this `foo.s` file
```
.pushsection .text, "axG", %progbits, foo
  .globl foo
  foo:
  ret
  .pushsection .llvm.callgraph, "?", %llvm_call_graph
    .byte 0, 0
    .dc.a foo
    .quad 0
  .popsection
.popsection

.pushsection .text, "axG", %progbits, bar
  .globl foo
  bar:
  ret
  .pushsection .llvm.callgraph, "?", %llvm_call_graph
    .byte 0, 0
    .dc.a bar
    .quad 0
  .popsection
.popsection
```
`clang -c foo.s && llvm-readelf --elf-output-style=JSON --pretty-print --call-graph-info foo.o` on that shows that there is only one record reported because the current implementation just looked at the first SHT_LLVM_CALL_GRAPH section and then ignored all others. This patch will address this gap by iterating over all the SHT_LLVM_CALL_GRAPH sections.

author: raeedzz
body:
## Summary

- **Restore standard macOS clipboard shortcuts in bundled builds.** `tauri dev` injected a default app menu so ⌘C/⌘V/⌘X/⌘A/⌘Z worked locally, but the bundled `.app` shipped with no app menu — the OS stub's Edit items aren't wired to AppKit's responder chain, so the shortcuts silently no-op in WKWebView for non-terminal inputs. Registering `tauri::menu::Menu::default` installs `PredefinedMenuItem`s that dispatch the native `cut:` / `copy:` / `paste:` / `selectAll:` selectors WebKit honors out of the box. Terminal panes are unaffected — `PtyPassthrough`, `CanvasGrid`, and `PromptInput` each `preventDefault` on these chords first, so PTY-aware clipboard semantics still win.
- **Unstick the release pipeline.** PR #13 merged with `for (const project of projects)` over a `Record<string, Project>` in `AppShell.tsx`, which `tsc` rejects (TS2488). `release.yml`'s `bun run build` failed at the tsc step, so v0.0.15 never published. Switched to `Object.values(projects)`.
- **Add a PR-time CI gate so this can't recur.** `release.yml` only runs on push to `main`, with no typecheck before merge. New `ci.yml` runs `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, and `bun run test:rs` on every PR (and on pushes to main, so Branch Protection has something to pin). Pin "Typecheck + tests" as a required status check in repo settings to make this enforceable.
- **Re-bring forward the unmerged horizontal-scroll commit** that was on `restore-scroll-during-agent` past the PR #13 cut.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun run typecheck` — passes locally (✓ confirmed)
- [ ] `bun run test` — 103 pass (✓ confirmed)
- [ ] `bun run test:rs` — 228 pass (✓ confirmed)
- [ ] CI's "Typecheck + tests" job goes green on this PR
- [ ] After merge: the next release run on `main` actually publishes a new tag (will be v0.0.16)
- [ ] In the new DMG: focus the project's add-folder input (or any text field), type → ⌘A → ⌘C → click another field → ⌘V → text round-trips
- [ ] In a terminal pane: ⌘C with a selection still copies to clipboard, ⌘V still pastes into the PTY (regression check on the terminal's existing chord handlers)
- [ ] Right panel's secondary terminal still scrolls horizontally on long lines without showing a horizontal scrollbar track

author: dereuromark
body:
Third of four landing the high-impact findings from the cross-impl gap audit (carve vs djot vs djot-php). ## P1.2 — Adopt djot `
` wrapper around headings ### Today Carve emits bare headings: ```html

Welcome

Getting started

Setup

``` ### After this PR (spec) + impl follow-ups Carve will match djot's structural model: ```html

Welcome

Getting started

Setup

``` Verified against djot's official `headings.test` (vendored at `djot-php/tests/official/headings.test`). ## Why move The audit surfaced this as the biggest single carve-vs-djot divergence that the README didn't even document. Investigating the history: the bare-`` choice was set in early M1 and never revisited; recent PRs focused on features (translit, refs, smart typography) not output structure. It was almost certainly **Markdown muscle memory** rather than a deliberate divergence from djot. Reasons to move: 1. **Document structure as queryable data.** JS gets `document.querySelectorAll('section')`; CSS can style "current section"; TOC generation is trivial. 2. **Anchor stability.** `
` puts the anchor on the *container*. Renaming heading text doesn't break inbound deep-links if the section element survives. 3. **Implicit hierarchy → nested sections.** `# H1 / ## H2` becomes a DOM tree matching the outline. Print stylesheets, screen readers, OPDS generators, page-break controllers all benefit. 4. **Accessibility.** HTML5 spec recommends grouping under `
` for proper document outline. ARIA tooling understands sections as landmarks. Cost we accept: 1. **Output size roughly doubles** for heading-dense docs. 2. **Renderer becomes stateful** — tracking the open-section stack and closing all sections of equal-or-deeper level when a new heading arrives. 3. **CSS migration cost** for projects styling `.content > h1`, `h2 + p`, etc. ## What's in this PR (spec only) - `resources/grammar.ebnf` — new PART 9 §13 pinning the algorithm with full edge cases (adjacent same-level, skipped levels, explicit `{#id}` placement, empty docs). - `docs/case-study/syntax.md` §4.1 — section-wrapping rule documented with a worked example. - `README.md` comparison table — gains a "Heading structure" row. Fragment-URL behavior (`#slug`) is unchanged — browsers resolve to whichever element carries the id, `` or `
`. Existing `` cross-references and `[Heading][]` implicit references resolve via the same slug; only the *emission site* of the id moves. ## What lands separately This is **spec only**, same pattern as carve PRs #16 (ASCII slugs) and #17 (list/admonition rules): - **carve-js impl** — switch `render-html.ts` to the section-wrapping algorithm; update corpus fixtures (02-headings, 19-heading-ids, anywhere headings appear in expected output). - **carve-php impl** — same. Algorithm closely mirrors djot-php's `renderDocumentWithSections` (`/tmp/djot-php/src/Renderer/HtmlRenderer.php:343-425`). - **carve repo follow-up** — re-vendor carve-lib + update `tests/corpus/02-headings*.html` / `19-heading-ids.html` to the new shape. ## Audit reference Spec sequencing for the gap audit's four big findings: - ✅ **P1.4** list marker change (#17) - ✅ **P1.12** admonition rendering rule (#17) - 👉 **P1.2** `
` wrapper (this PR) - ⏳ **P1.5** inline span `[text]{.attr}` (next, largest)

The prior diagnostics commit improved crash visibility but did not fully implement the audited requirements, and critical FPK compliance gaps were still affecting generated Canvas pages. This PR completes the error-handling implementation and applies the remaining high-impact FPK correctness fixes.

- **Error boundary + app wiring**
  - Replaced `ErrorBoundary` with the audited class-based implementation (`getDerivedStateFromError`, `componentDidCatch`, reset flow, dev-only stack details).
  - Moved `ErrorBoundary` to wrap `AppContent` **inside** `ConfigContext.Provider` (not around the entire provider chain).

- **Diagnostics runtime checks**
  - Replaced `src/lib/diagnostics.ts` with the required exported contract:
    - `runDiagnostics()`
    - `overallStatus()`
    - `DiagnosticResult`
  - Added Supabase connectivity/system_config/table checks and status aggregation.
  - Integrated live diagnostics into `HealthMonitorPage` with auto-run + re-run + status badge.

- **FPK-critical generation/validation fixes**
  - Updated Canvas HTML generation so all required FPK blocks are emitted in the expected flat sibling structure, including Friday mapping to `kl_custom_block_1`.
  - Corrected Language Arts default title format to remove the redundant “Shurley” wording in non-CP titles.
  - Aligned FPK validator behavior and issue codes with required deploy gating semantics.
  - Kept pre-deploy validation enforced in `PageBuilderPage` before `canvas-deploy-page`.

- **Schema + compliance tests**
  - Ensured migration adds `newsletters.homeroom_notes_html`.
  - Reworked compliance coverage in `src/test/fpk-compliance.test.ts` to explicitly assert required block IDs, Friday block mapping, wrapper/sibling structure, cross-course leak detection, LA CP title format, and fallback prefix behavior.
  - Updated `ErrorBoundary` tests to validate real crash/fallback/reset behavior.


body:
## Summary

Anti-drift scaffolding for fresh-agent ergonomics, plus four new canonical
skills that make the scaffolding self-enforcing. No product source, no
`state/`, no `packages/policies/`, no `packages/schemas/`. Five linear
commits; ready to squash-merge or merge as-is.

## What landed

### Root orientation
- `REPO_MAP.md` — 60-second five-zone orientation for fresh agents
- `docs/preflight-for-agents.md` — read-first sequence + default-safe /
  explicit-approval / forbidden zones + product-app scope rule
- `CLAUDE.md` — added `todos/` row and "Read first" pointer block
- `apps/README.md` + `apps/worker-engineering/README.md` — per-worker
  README template populated for the engineering lane
- `HANDOFF.md` — banner only; preserved as historical, superseded by the
  new dated convention

### Indexes (plans / todos / handoffs)
- `docs/plans/INDEX.md` — all 38 plans classified (32 open, 6 done, 0
  abandoned), with a documented YAML frontmatter convention for new plans
- `docs/handoffs/INDEX.md` — dated `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` convention with
  the eight required sections
- `todos/README.md` — naming + lifecycle convention; 18 `*-complete-*`
  filenames renamed to `*-completed-*` via `git mv` (zero content
  changes) so the canonical `completed` token is uniform

### Doc-path drift checker (advisory)
- `scripts/ci/check_doc_paths.sh` — dependency-free bash; resolves
  repo-relative tokens in the five entry docs; supports a narrow
  `RUNTIME_ALLOWED` list for documented runtime-only paths
  (`state/checkpoints/platform/`)
- Advisory `doc-path-check` job added to `.github/workflows/tests.yml`
  with `continue-on-error: true`. Promote to required once policy is
  decided.
- `make audit` runs the checker locally; `make doctor` and `make handoff`
  are read-only operator helpers
- Three legacy `fishing-logbook-ios` references reconciled to
  `catchbook-ios` (`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/local-dev.md`,
  `docs/ios-conventions.md`); subsystem identifier in `ios-conventions.md`
  updated to `com.ai-company-os.catchbook`

### Anti-drift skills (canonical → adapter → project-skill pointer)
- **`agent-preflight`** — structured preflight report for a fresh agent
  session: git state, edit boundaries, read-first presence, product-app
  scope classification
- **`stale-doc-detector`** — wraps `scripts/ci/check_doc_paths.sh` and
  classifies each finding as `fix_now` / `allowlist` / `founder_decision` /
  `ignore`; adds a legacy-slug heuristic for product-rename rot; never
  edits docs
- **`handoff-write`** — writes exactly one dated handoff under
  `docs/handoffs/`; refuses to overwrite; never commits or pushes
- **`codex-cloud-dispatch`** — canonicalizes the workflow previously
  documented in `docs/codex-cloud-dispatch.md`; encodes 12 invariants
  (`staging` only, no `_PREEXISTING_FAILURES` edits, eight-section brief
  shape, no merge/push, etc.); the original doc is preserved as the
  detailed UI reference with a banner pointing back to the canonical

### Fixture coverage
- One structural fixture per new skill (codex-cloud-dispatch and
  stale-doc-detector add one adversarial each; handoff-write adds one
  overwrite-refusal case)
- Four new pytest files mirroring the `test_repo_onboarding_skill.py`
  pattern; data-driven from fixtures
- All four registry entries land at `fixture_status: passing`, backed by
  the new tests
- Skill reconciliation, skill-stocktake, and the wider 133-test
  skill/registry/loader keyword suite all pass

## Scope discipline

- No product app source touched (`products/catchbook-ios/`,
  `products/after-plans-ios/`, `products/life-clock-ios/`)
- No `state/` mutation
- No `packages/policies/` or `packages/schemas/` edits
- No generated files, no `.claude/settings*.json`, no `.claude/hooks/`,
  no `.claude/commands/`
- `.claude/skills/*` files are 12-line thin pointers per
  `skills/WIRING.md`

## Testing

This PR is documentation + skill scaffolding. Four new pytest files
were added for the new canonical skills, data-driven from each
skill's structural fixtures:

- `tests/python/unit/test_agent_preflight_skill.py`
- `tests/python/unit/test_stale_doc_detector_skill.py`
- `tests/python/unit/test_handoff_write_skill.py`
- `tests/python/unit/test_codex_cloud_dispatch_skill.py`

The two new files under `apps/` (`apps/README.md` and
